fix(doctor): bind session import receipts to inode and birthtime instead of the device id (#163904)

A completed, verified deferred session-SQLite import flipped back to retained_plugin_source_conflict after every macOS VM reboot because the receipt bound databaseIdentity to device-id:inode and the virtual filesystem device id changes per boot while the file, inode and contents stay the same, forcing repeated recovery and finalization work (#163870). The receipt owner now persists inode:<ino>:birthtime:<value> (existing birthtime policy, 0 where unavailable); retained-source SHA-256/size checks are unchanged, recovery operations keep strict device/inode checks, and Doctor upgrades legacy receipts once. A legacy receipt whose canonical history was deleted cannot distinguish reboot from replacement and keeps the previous behavior. Thanks @paulotvlincelia for the evidence.

Closes #163870

fix(agents): stale pause notice wakes the requester after a quick subagent follow-up (#163814)

* fix(agents): stale pause notice wakes the requester after a quick subagent follow-up

A follow-up admitted while a child is still yielding with waitFor "message"
registers as its own task at the next session generation, because adoption
only matches rows that are already paused. Since #163352 a newer task can no
longer revoke another task's requester custody, so the paused row's pause
notice stayed current and woke the requester with a "paused awaiting
continuation" turn after the follow-up had already continued the child.

A yield-paused row holds no result, only its continuation: treat any newer
execution of its session as superseding it. Completed rows keep the
same-task rule that preserves retained delivery from #163352.

Fixes the Gateway E2E shard 1/4 failure in
plugin-subagent-self-yield-followup.e2e.test.ts.

* fix(agents): keep requester-bound siblings from cancelling a paused child's notice

A plugin follow-up that names its own requester is an independent sibling
with its own completion delivery; by contract the original paused task stays
resumable and its pending pause notice is still owed. Supersede a
yield-paused row only by a newer execution of the same task or one without
its own completion audience (a default follow-up that continues the child).

## What Problem This Solves

Doctor stopped explaining how to recover retired Teams conversation, poll, SSO-token, and feedback-learning JSON after #163850 removed its warning-only detectors.

## Why This Change Was Made

The July-plus migration floor retires import algorithms, while the documented retirement contract still requires bridge-release guidance. The earlier interpretation of that floor was too broad. This focused correction restores the existing detectors, matching manifest declarations, and behavior/cold-import coverage.

refactor(commands): deslop commands, CLI, and infrastructure (#163840)

## What Problem This Solves

Commands, Doctor, and infrastructure repeat option forwarding, migration traversal, result projection, and error handling that already have canonical owners.

## User Impact

No intended user-visible change. CLI flags, messages, exit codes, JSON output, migration precedence, persisted data, and authorization checks stay unchanged. Supported July 2026-and-later migrations and the older-Gateway node-list fallback remain supported.

## Why This Change Was Made

This combines the subsystem cleanup into one batch, removing 1,459 net production lines instead of paying for separate CI runs for each small simplification.

- Consolidate onboarding installation, auth selection, migration item selection, and cleanup reporting; retain branch-specific consent and error behavior.
- Reuse Doctor's model-slot traversal, parsing, package identification, report projection, and session-key collection instead of parallel implementations and forwarding helpers.
- Let status reports consume their existing overview facts directly, and share archive/storage command registration.
- Map device-pairing authority refusals at the mutation owner after admission and publication settle; preserve locks, revalidation, cleanup, and each caller's return shape.
- Consolidate receipt-authoritative APNs/MCP source cleanup at the source-claim owner, keeping each migration's safe reader and receipt commit.
- Remove redundant outbound target forwarding and reuse existing filesystem, normalization, and text helpers.

Updater lifecycle, dependencies, schemas, and plugin SDK contracts are unchanged. The native assertion-baseline tool records five removed assertions; no allowance grows. No newly discovered product bugs or flaky-test fixes are included.

## Evidence

- Both import-cycle checks passed again on the final rebased head: 0 Madge cycles and 0 runtime-value cycles.
- AWS focused run: 3,324 passed, 2 skipped, and one inherited Doctor fixture failure across 174 files. The same failure reproduced on the clean base. The branch now includes the upstream repair from #163777; no duplicate fix is included.
- The complete changed-file gate passed, including production/test types, lint, dead exports, boundaries, and ratchets. The final Gateway send rerun passed all 83 tests. Git range-diff confirms the rebase preserved the cleanup patch.
- After the final Testbox exceeded the ten-minute queue limit, the local `nice -n 15` confirmation completed with 82 Gateway tests passing and one 120-second timeout in the Telegram live-owner test; Doctor did not run because the first group failed. Native worker compilation took 566 seconds under severe host load. The failure is recorded, not counted as passing proof.
- Exact-head CI [37074925001](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/37074925001) passed types, lint, architecture, builds, Windows, and most test shards. Five test jobs failed; every failure has matching pre-existing evidence below. The tests and the relevant refusal, worker-admission, session mutation, and cache-validity owners are unchanged by this cleanup. Landing uses the maintainer-authorized inherited-failure exception, pinned to `714c365b1775c10760276a4dbc8bbf05141d4e5d`; no green-CI claim is made.
- Independent autoreview is scoped-clean at P0/P1 after supplying unchanged owner context: the early ref-mode branch still enforces env-reference precedence; all migration command entrypoints retain the Codex-only flag guard; the cleanup serializer already normalizes local paths while delegated paths bypass it. improve(update): skip re-reading unchanged package files during publication checks (#163432)

After #163370, npm package publication still fully re-hashes package
generations four times while the Gateway is stopped, and retirement hashes the
live package once more. Each walk re-reads ~44k files (~700 MiB).

The integrity reader can now reuse a content digest from an earlier in-process
observation of the same generation. A file's bytes are skipped only when the
earlier read was settled (its ctime predated the read by at least five seconds,
the racy-timestamp guard) and the fresh lstat matches device, inode, mode,
owner, link count, size, mtime and ctime exactly. Every walk still lists every
directory, lstats every entry, re-checks links, entry and byte limits, the
manifest version and the final metadata sweep; digests, order and refusal
precedence are unchanged. Publication passes the expected fingerprint, which
preparation already carries with its in-process observation; recovery processes
parse the descriptor from the journal and re-read all contents.

This deliberately relaxes the fresh-hash rule from #163370: a same-user writer
storing to an already-dirty writable shared mapping can change bytes without
updating timestamps. The reader only observes and never excluded such writers;
the owner accepted this tradeoff for the downtime it saves.

feat(memory): resolve the memory audience in the host (#162176)

* feat(memory): resolve the memory audience in the host

Memory providers had to re-derive whether a caller acts for the agent
owner privately or for one conversation, walking spawn lineage through
session lookups.

When the memory slot owner registers providerRuntime, the host mints a
MemoryAudience (owner-private, or one exact conversation) from the
admitted turn entry and, for spawned children, the exact parent key,
session ID, lifecycle revision (or its recorded absence), and captured
owner bit of every hop. Memory Core and other legacy owners resolve no
audience: their turns take no session leases, read no lineage, and log
nothing new. Native, ACP, and realtime voice consult children record the trusted
spawning sender's owner status and parent incarnation so that lineage
survives session creation, reset, and rollover. The receipt stores the
parent session id as spawnedBySessionId, so navigation's parentSessionId
and sessions.list stay unchanged; a child of a parent without a lifecycle revision,
such as a channel-created group row, records that absence. Incomplete or
stale lineage yields no audience; only a spawned row without the owner
receipt predates the lineage receipts, and it logs a respawn
instruction. A parent without a stored row spawns as before. Spawn rechecks
a stored parent on the session read worker immediately before the child
commits. Parent rows are read on the session read worker, and every captured hop holds
a session generation lease, so currency checks stay synchronous and
read-free. Audiences are bound to their session, released when the
owning attempt or run ends, and delegated to same-agent children bound
to the child's current incarnation. The host checks currency before and
after opening a provider and around every provider call, and the guard
it passes to a provider includes audience currency. The memory slot
owner's own tools, Active Memory, and project recall also recheck it
before their effects; other plugin tools reach memory only through the
provider guard and do not fail on a stale audience.

Session authority, plugin tool contexts, hook contexts, and Codex
dynamic tools carry the audience. Native consumers cut over to it:
Active Memory trigger, deep, and summary recall (caches keyed by
audience; default deep-recall tools from the slot owner's
recallToolNames; trigger recall runs only while tool policy allows every
recall tool the provider declares), project recall, Memory Wiki,
post-compaction provider refresh, doctor memory status and recall/search
checks, and the status scan, which report provider health instead of
legacy index counters. Legacy owners keep their trigger-recall gate,
doctor and status ordering, and post-compaction sync without loading or
calling the slot plugin to decide.

* test(memory): consolidate memory audience tests

Fold the real session-owner audience test into the shared real-lineage
fixture, drop the spawn lineage unit test that the real-SQLite spawn tests
already cover, share spawn parameters, and remove cases that only mirrored
implementation (log text, mock passthrough, per-kind passthrough).

native hook relay, macOS node worker) now turns off Maglev and concurrent
Sparkplug at startup when it runs as main, matching Node 22's tiering and
the existing Vitest policy. Library imports keep stock V8; explicit
--maglev or --concurrent-sparkplug flags still win.

hung with defaults, 0/1019 with the policy; re-enabling only Maglev hung

feat(memory): add a provider-neutral memory provider runtime (#162175)

Memory consumers were bound to the file-backed search manager, so a
memory plugin whose records are not workspace files could not serve
recall.

Add a caller-bound MemoryProviderRuntime (search, get, health, optional
candidates and refresh) registered as MemoryPluginCapability
.providerRuntime. Providers declare their capabilities (sources,
pagination, candidate kinds, project filtering); the host validates them
at open and the bound handle rejects undeclared requests before calling
the provider.

Project recall, realtime voice context, Active Memory trigger recall,
and Memory Wiki use the neutral runtime when the selected slot owner
registers providerRuntime. With a legacy runtime they keep their
manager calls, purposes, authorization, results, and citation labels
unchanged. Deciding which path to take reads only owners this process
already loaded (the current registry, the process registry, or a
standalone owner), never loading the slot plugin to decide.

Add the Gateway memory.search v2 / memory.get / memory.status RPCs. A
legacy adapter serves them over existing file-backed managers,
preserving session-hit authorization: session callers keep requester
visibility plus any host-granted conversation recall pass carried on
their session authority, and sessionless host or operator callers keep
the opened agent's own session hits through Memory Core's trusted agent
scope. Its health omits host paths. Any authenticated operator
connection with operator.read can call them, as with unversioned
memory.search; in-process agent callers keep their run's operator
authority. memory.search v2 rejects missing, unknown, or empty source
restrictions before provider admission. Unversioned or version 1
memory.search directs a provider-runtime owner's clients to retry with
version 2.

Realtime voice fast context binds its provider reads to the live call and
consult abort signal. Plugins released before that liveness argument keep
their call shape: without it, legacy owners answer as before and a native
provider is never read. When another plugin owns the memory slot, Memory
Core's CLI reports that provider's health from memory status, refuses
memory search, and labels index commands as acting on its sidecar index.
The memory-host-search SDK subpath stays private-local, so the public SDK
surface does not grow. Memory Wiki's package boundary maps memory-core's
session visibility leaf to its declaration producer.

fix(talk): retire a replaced legacy realtime reply before it can start (#163732)

With an actor-bound legacy PCM player, RealtimeTalkOutput started each
reply's playback as a MainActor task guarded only by Task.isCancelled,
and cancelled it solely from the detached owner task's cancellation
handler. When a newer turn replaced the reply before the detached owner
had a cooperative-pool thread, the handler was not yet registered, so the
retired reply's playback ran after its replacement and played its
buffered audio (RealtimeTalkRelaySessionPlaybackTests flake in
macos-swift (packages)).

The legacy task now checks the same generation fence the owner's
completion path uses (outputSessionId and isClosed, under the output
lock), so a stop retires a not-yet-started reply synchronously. The
realtime backend path already fenced by generation and is unchanged.

fix: show embedding vectors and dimensions in infer text output (#163722)

Closes #163696

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes missing embedding vectors and dimensions when `openclaw infer embedding create` succeeds without `--json`. Thanks to @LinzeShi for the report and fixture-backed diagnosis.

## User Impact

Each input now shows its dimension count and a bounded vector preview, under the existing provider/model header. Full vectors remain available with `--json`; no configuration changes are required.

## Why This Change Was Made

The shared text formatter treated embedding input text as the entire result. Handle embedding results there, showing at most eight values with an ellipsis for longer vectors. This retains the same header and labeled-line convention used by `infer audio transcribe`, `infer image describe`, and `infer video describe` through `formatEnvelopeForText` (`audio.ts:67`, `image.ts:322`, `video.ts:276`). JSON serialization and error handling are untouched.

No overlap with Pash/Sarah changes.

## Evidence

- Regression fails on main `a458fa7ee4dd7306acc14b6f445c133c9791b142` because dimensions and vectors are absent; passes after the repair. Covers ordered batched inputs, a short vector, a 1,536-dimensional vector, and empty input/vector values.
- `pnpm test src/cli/capability-cli.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: 98 passed; 23.66 seconds wall time in isolated Linux/Node 24.21.0. Baseline: 97 passed, the new regression failed. Hosted CI timing will be reported by the checks.
- Real `pnpm openclaw --profile <isolated-profile> infer embedding create --text hello --text world`, backed by OpenAI `text-embedding-3-small`: base printed only `hello` and `world`; rebuilt candidate printed each input with `dimensions: 1536` and an eight-value preview under the provider/model header.
- JSON controls replayed each captured live response through the CLI: stdout was byte-identical between base and candidate after replacing only vector values, with complete 1,536-value arrays and identical structure. A local HTTP 400 control kept exit 1, empty stdout, and identical stderr after profile-name normalization.
- Candidate built output was inspected before the successful live check and its formatter source SHA-256 matched the committed source. An initial candidate attempt reused stale output; it was rebuilt before the final successful check.

chore(release): fail package acceptance before the installed tree outgrows shipped updaters (#163612)

* ci(release): guard installed package tree against shipped updater caps

Published updaters (2026.9.7 and current main) fingerprint the whole
npm-installed package tree with createPackageIntegrityReader().tree(),
capped at 50,000 entries (root included) and 1 GiB. The staged-candidate
walk in preparePackageActivation does not tolerate the limit error, and
installed updaters cannot be patched, so a candidate whose installed tree
crosses the cap cannot be installed by those drivers. The tarball check
only sees the ~13.9k tarball entries, not the installed dependency tree.

Package Acceptance's npm_12_install_sh job already installs the exact
candidate globally; a new step measures that install with the reader's
counting rules (root plus every dirent, no symlink following, regular-file
bytes excluding npm's hidden lockfile) and fails above 47,500 entries or
900 MiB, while every shipped updater can still install the candidate.
It runs wherever Package Acceptance runs (release checks, the 3-hourly
main Full Release Validation, weekly Update Migration) at the cost of one
directory walk; no new job or install.

Measured: main candidate 44,074 entries / 562.0 MiB; published 2026.9.7
44,098 / 630.3 MiB, both matching an independent find oracle. The real
reader accepts a 50,000-entry tree the guard counts as 50,000 and refuses
the 50,001-entry tree.

* fix(release): charge hidden lockfile bytes like published updaters

Published updaters 2026.9.3 through 2026.9.7 add every regular file's
bytes to the 1 GiB rollback-verification cap, including npm's hidden
node_modules/.package-lock.json. Only main (#162365, unreleased) skips
those bytes, and the guard had copied main's more lenient rule, so it
could pass a tree that every shipped updater refuses. Count every
regular file so the guard never undercounts relative to any shipped
driver. Entry counting is identical across all shipped tags.

Real global installs write no hidden lockfiles: published 2026.9.7
still measures 44,098 entries / 630.3 MiB, matching an all-files find.

fix(test): Telegram runtime test leaks temp roots when a case times out on a loaded host (#163624)

Telegram skill runtime test (`telegram-runtime.test.mjs`) removed its temp root before stopping the uv/Python children of a timed-out case, so on loaded hosts those children kept writing under the removed tree and the directory leaked.

Each case registered `fs.rmSync(root)` as its first after hook and every `run()` registered its own kill-and-join hook later. node:test runs after hooks in registration order and stops at the first one that throws (verified on Node 24.21.0), so the root was removed while stalled children were live, and a throwing removal skipped every kill hook.

fix(i18n): stop parallel native PRs from conflicting in the string inventory (#163330)

The generated native inventory stored one line per string with every
extraction site inline, sorted alphabetically. Two PRs reusing a string
("Retry") both rewrote its line, and a feature's new strings ("Group by",
"Group chat") landed in the same insertion gap, so parallel native PRs
conflicted in apps/.i18n/native-source.json and needed a rebase plus a
full CI rerun.

Inventory v3 writes one line per extraction site, clustered by source
file, with clusters ordered by a hash of the path so new sibling files do
not share a gap. Each row's position depends only on its own content, so
independent edits merge cleanly (including GitHub's server-side merge)
and the merged text equals a fresh baseline. The new
scripts/native-i18n-inventory.ts owns serialization and parsing; the
generator, Android/Gradle and Apple readers migrate to it together and
receive the same entries in the same order as before.

perf(gateway): attribute git subprocesses and bound the startup git burst (#163445)

* perf(gateway): attribute git subprocesses and bound the startup git burst

Two minutes after a Team Gateway start the worker-placement recovery
sweep launched ~800 git subprocesses in one minute (one `for-each-ref`
inventory per historical local checkout, even when no cleanup refs
exist), stalling the event loop for 4 s per minute, and the spawn
counter could only say `family="git"`.

Git executions now carry a bounded operation label (fixed allowlist,
`unknown` for unattributed git, `none` for other families) that the
shared spawn owner records and the Prometheus plugin exports; worker
launches keep the parent-admitted operation across batching and
retries. Startup orphan-ref cleanup runs only while the Gateway is idle,
inventories at most eight roots per full sweep, and remembers completed
roots for the startup pass, so cold-start work no longer scales with
history size while every root is still eventually cleaned.

* fix(gateway): resolve orphan-cleanup workspace roots once per startup pass

Bounded orphan-ref sweeps re-resolved every placement's workspace to
rebuild the root map before cleaning their eight roots, so a Gateway
with 50 historical placements paid the resolution twice. The startup
pass now remembers each placement's resolved root (or that it has none)
while every sweep still admits the current placements, so a sharing
session that was busy is retried against fresh session facts. Failed
resolutions stay uncached and retry on the next sweep.

Also map the optional spawn operation before sorting in the git-worker
lifecycle test.

refactor(channels): drop pre-July-2026 Matrix state migrations (#163292)

## What Problem This Solves

Retires Matrix state imports whose last shipped JSON writers predate the July 2026 migration support window.

## User Impact

Upgrades from pre-July-2026 versions are no longer migrated: Matrix `thread-bindings.json` and `startup-verification.json`. Doctor and the affected runtime preserve those files and explain how to upgrade through OpenClaw 2026.9.5: run Doctor, start Matrix once to import them, then install the latest release.

July and newer SQLite bindings, verification cooldowns, device metadata, token-root selection, and schema upgrades remain supported. Public plugin SDK compatibility and other Matrix migrations are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

Both file writers ended in `84a965a1a27` on May 30. The last confirmed stable JSON writer, `v2026.5.28`, was published May 30; `v2026.5.30-beta.1` first shipped SQLite on May 31, followed by stable `v2026.6.1` on June 3. Inspection of `v2026.7.1` confirms the same SQLite namespaces and keys, with no JSON rewrite or restoration path. The 2026.9.5 bridge retains both runtime imports.

Deletes JSON decoding, merging, import-marker stores, cleanup writes, and the obsolete thread-binding JSON root score. The plugin owns the source-preserving refusal; existing Doctor ordering and schema migration ownership stay intact. Net production reduction: 140 lines.

Other channel config aliases remain: supported July config rewrites can still preserve them. Separate owner follow-ups will cover independently proven formats.

## Evidence

- Independent isolated review: no actionable findings through P2.
- Matrix runtime/storage/Doctor boundary tests passed, including July-shaped binding keys and verification cooldowns, unchanged retired-file bytes, and archive exclusion.
- The intact shipped `v2026.7.1` account SQLite fixture upgraded through the actual Doctor CLI; canonical rows and archived database bytes remained intact.
- Doctor state/config migration suites passed. Plugin contracts: **1,132 tests / 48 files passed**.
- `node scripts/check-changed.mjs` passed; both `check-madge-import-cycles.ts` and `check-import-cycles.ts` report **0**.
- Linux single-worker wall measurements (`pnpm test <file> --maxWorkers=1`): Doctor import contract **2.89s**, storage **29.49s**, bindings **15.10s**, startup verification **13.73s**. No new process boot, timer, retry, or weakened assertion was added.

Proof used an isolated AWS checkout pinned to the base and byte-verified candidate patch. Hosted CI will validate the pushed head. Release history and retention decisions were checked separately from test execution.

fix(test): Gateway e2e connect fails with 1006 when another fixture takes the instance port (#163003)

gateway-cold-agent-abort intermittently failed with `gateway closed during connect (1006)` about 260 ms into the test, too early for its own cold Gateway child to have answered readiness.

OpenClawTestInstance claims its port block and releases its reservation listener right before spawning the child. In-process Gateway fixtures picked ports with getGatewayE2ePortBlock(), a probe that released its claim before returning, and then started a Gateway whose listener retries EADDRINUSE every 500 ms. A fixture that probed the same candidate just before the instance claimed it won the port at the handoff, and the instance's /readyz was answered by that foreign Gateway (1006 while it closed, token mismatch while alive).

getGatewayE2ePortBlock is removed. acquireGatewayE2ePortBlock (beside startClaimedGateway) returns a held claim, and every caller keeps it until the Gateway or server bound to that port has closed, including same-port restarts, unstarted-claim guards, and listener-specific release in the MCP App conformance fixture. Kernel-assigned port-0 binders stay out of scope (the Linux pool excludes the ephemeral range). The test instance gains bounded post-start diagnostics (diagnose(), responder uptime vs child age, Linux listener owners, handshake stage in the close error).

Regression: an instance whose first candidate is an in-process Gateway E2E port must allocate a different port (fails on the probe-only helper).

fix(agents): fall back to the primary's CLI runtime when the derived utility model has no credential (#157867)

* fix(agents): keep auto-derived utility models on the primary's runtime

Automatic utility routing derives a provider-declared small model from the
primary's provider, so the derived ref matches no configured model entry of its
own. A runtime pinned on the primary model entry
(agents.defaults.models["<provider>/<model>"].agentRuntime) therefore did not
carry, and the derived ref fell back to the default runtime and its HTTP auth
path.

For a CLI-backed primary such as claude-cli the provider holds no API key on
purpose, so the session observer's isolated completion failed with "No API key
found for provider anthropic" and disabled itself after two attempts. The
surfaced remedy pointed at "models auth paste-api-key" for a provider that is
deliberately subscription-authenticated.

docs/gateway/cli-backends.md already documented that utility completions use the
selected model's runtime, including canonical anthropic/* refs configured with
agentRuntime.id "claude-cli". PR #135711 delivered that for an explicit
utilityModel; the auto-derived ref kept no runtime owner. This restores the
documented contract for the automatic path.

Inheritance applies only when the utility setting is auto, the provider matches,
the derived model resolves to the default runtime, and the primary resolves to a
non-default one. The last two conditions make a provider-level agentRuntime and
OpenAI's implicit Codex harness self-exclude, since both already resolve a
non-default runtime for the derived ref.

One seam covers all three consumers: session observer digests, progress
narration, and tool-call titles all spread the prepared object into
runIsolatedCompletion, which already accepts agentHarnessRuntimeOverride.

Fixes #138789.

* fix(agents): route auto-derived utility models through the primary's CLI runtime

- Key the utility runtime override on the resolved selection, not on an absent modelRef; the session observer passes the derived ref back in as modelRef
- Inherit only a runtime pinned on the primary's model entry (runtimeSource model); provider-level and implicit runtimes are not copied
- Add an end-to-end test: the prepared utility completion for a claude-cli primary resolves the CLI owner instead of host credential preparation
- Keep isolated-completion fixture selection real; only prepareSimpleCompletionModel stays mocked

Closes #138789

* fix(agents): inherit the CLI runtime only for the derived utility model

Selection prefers a caller-supplied modelRef over automatic derivation, so
useUtilityModel alone did not prove the selected ref was the provider-declared
automatic utility model. Provider equality alone let an explicitly selected
same-provider model inherit the primary's pinned CLI runtime and consume its
subscription quota instead of staying on its own HTTP route.

Confirm the selection is the manifest-declared automatic utility model before
inheriting, and plumb the caller's manifest snapshot so the check resolves the
same catalog the derivation used. The session observer's pre-resolved derived
ref still inherits, since that ref matches the declared default.

Also give the provider-level fixture the baseUrl and models fields that
ModelProviderConfig requires, which fixes the TS2352 cast that failed
check-test-types-core-1.

* test(agents): pin the dual-credential opt-outs for utility runtime inheritance

The HTTP opt-out this change relies on was documented but never tested,
and the wording did not hold: an entry for the derived model only opts
out when it names a non-default runtime, so a bare entry or
`agentRuntime.id: "default"` still inherits the primary's CLI runtime.

Cover both supported opt-outs and that boundary, and write the config
into docs/gateway/cli-backends.md alongside the subscription-quota note
so the behavior change is reversible from the docs alone.

* fix(agents): inherit the primary's CLI runtime only when the derived model cannot authenticate

The auto-derived utility model has no entry of its own, so a runtime
pinned on the primary never carried and the derived ref fell back to the
HTTP route. On a CLI-backed primary that provider holds no API key, so
digests, progress narration and tool-call titles failed with "No API key
found for provider".

Inheriting unconditionally would have fixed that by moving every
dual-credential installation's utility traffic from API billing onto CLI
subscription quota on upgrade. Gate the inheritance on the derived
model's own credential instead: it borrows the primary's runtime only
when the provider has no usable auth, which is exactly the failing case.
Installations holding both a credential and a CLI-backed primary keep
their existing HTTP route, and configuring a key later moves the traffic
back onto it.

The probe runs only when a runtime would otherwise be inherited, so the
ordinary path adds no credential lookup. An explicit runtime on the
derived model's own entry still wins over both.

* docs(agents): state that the utility route is decided per preparation

The guide promised that configuring an API key later moves these
completions back to HTTP. The session observer reuses one prepared
completion for the life of an observer run and re-prepares only when its
utility model reference changes, so a credential added mid-run does not
move that run back; it applies at the next preparation.

Fix the claim rather than the caching. Re-evaluating provider auth inside
the observer would put a credential lookup on its hot path to chase a
transient, self-correcting state, and the caching predates this change.

* fix(gateway): re-decide the utility route when the observer borrowed a runtime

A prepared utility completion carries an inherited runtime only because the
derived model had no usable provider credential. The session observer memoized
that preparation for the life of an observer run, so a credential added mid-run
could not move that run back to its own HTTP route.

Serve the digest from the borrowed preparation, then drop it, so the next digest
re-decides. A preparation that borrowed nothing stays memoized, so an install
already on its own credential keeps a single preparation and adds no auth lookup
to the observer's hot path.

* refactor(agents): simplify automatic utility runtime preparation

* fix(agents): refresh borrowed narration routes across queued turns

* fix(agents): keep utility runtime projection on prepared auth

refactor(doctor): retire pre-July Telegram config inputs

## What Problem This Solves

Doctor still carries Telegram transforms for configuration formats last written before the supported July 1, 2026 cutoff.

## User Impact

Pre-July Telegram DM/thread, native-draft, and scalar/flat streaming settings now stop at the existing shared retired-format check before backup recovery or unknown-key cleanup can discard them. The message directs operators through OpenClaw 2026.9.5 and its Doctor first. Current nested streaming and supported July-and-later settings remain eligible for Doctor.

**Update behavior:** supported 2026.9.7 writers use the canonical shapes. Their updater and normalization paths are unchanged. Unsupported older inputs receive actionable intermediate-upgrade guidance with the root config, includes, and backup bytes preserved. Nextcloud's state-importer retirement and the update-sensitive listener migration remain in #162759 with its published-driver proof.

## Why This Change Was Made

Retirement follows actual shipped-writer dates, including extended-stable releases. Git history and release tags on both sides establish these cutovers:

- Native drafts: `e8b142feb117` on June 13, following the June 12/13 releases.
- DM/thread settings: `aa117ec4dece` on May 27, after `v2026.5.25-beta.1`.
- Flat streaming: `0fdf9e874b7` on April 6, after `v2026.4.5`.

September's extended-stable `v2026.6.35` still writes some older Telegram tuning and group-history settings, so those transforms remain. Explicit listener migrations and recorded SDK compatibility removal dates remain supported.

This deletes obsolete transforms, plugin-local checks, and their tests, extending the existing shared refusal owner. Concurrent additions to that owner and the shared docs are preserved. Production (`src/**` and `extensions/**`, excluding tests/support/helpers/utils/e2e/fixtures): **+32/-158/net -126**. Tests are +80/-212/net -132. No changelog edit; this body carries release-note context.

## Evidence

Fresh Codex autoreview is scoped-clean with no actionable P0/P1 findings. Formatting and `git diff --check` pass. Final head `c83516c95a6e9f6db54b8911d7a183ac76fcabcc` passed [CI 36960472012](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/36960472012), including `openclaw/ci-gate`, applicable test suites, types, lint, and guards. The coordinator-authorized hosted-CI fallback is used for this unsupported-config retirement. A second native Testbox request, `tbx_01m3xamsy7z50drnw0be5wq1ax`, remained queued for 35m23s without a runner or executed payload after native readiness timed out. It was stopped and verified completed; that attempt is not a test result. The final-head CI above is the final gate. No retries, longer test timeouts, weakened assertions, or skipped tests were added.

The fully paginated GitHub files API confirms five changed files, including two production files: +32/-158/net -126.

Prior-scope evidence is retained separately: Blacksmith Testbox `tbx_01m3x7r56cy31kgravnhf6sny7`, [run 36956718354](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/36956718354), tested head `558b70db76b8b9f4c83ccbc0694793635d5f8c30`, tree `6509eca5e6a8f4b10dcaa92a48c90d1edd7f2209`. Frozen install, all 62 tests across five files, and canonical changed checks passed. The changed-check took 1630.48s. That lease is completed.

Telegram production is byte-identical to that tested revision. Relevant `pnpm test <file> --maxWorkers=1` costs were Telegram Doctor 36 tests/19.24s, history limits 2/1.62s, and the shared retired-input entrypoint 12/40.88s. refactor(ui): drop pre-July-2026 storage migrations (#163083)

## What Problem This Solves

The Control UI still reads top-level session selections and rewrites durable shared-token settings produced before the supported July 2026 upgrade window.

## User Impact

Upgrades from pre-July-2026 versions are no longer migrated: top-level remembered session selections and durable-token settings cleanup. Users with those unsupported selections can select their session again; conversations remain on the Gateway. Current shared credentials stay in session storage and are never restored from durable settings.

## Why This Change Was Made

This implements the maintainer's July-and-later migration policy at the settings owner. The scalar session writer was replaced by `sessionsByGateway` in d37e3d582fd, first shipped in v2026.3.22 (March 23); v2026.3.13-1 was the last prior tagged writer. Durable token writes were removed by 10d0e3f3ca9, first shipped in v2026.3.7 (March 8); v2026.3.2 still wrote them.

Actual v2026.7.1-beta.1, v2026.7.1, and v2026.7.35 source writes `sessionsByGateway` and omits durable tokens. The July sidebar-pins upgrader, device-token import, and chat-outbox/group migrations remain: supported releases still produced those shapes. The September-published v2026.7.35 still writes outbox v1 and browser-local groups, so main's earlier cutovers are insufficient evidence for deleting them.

Net production reduction: 9 lines. The obsolete migration test is removed, and the existing settings-upgrade test now exercises representative July beta/stable persisted shapes. No protocol, schema, SDK, or rendered appearance changes.

## Evidence

- Isolated Codex AutoReview: no actionable P0–P2 findings.
- Blacksmith Testbox, pinned source and edited-file hashes: settings and preference suites passed, 33 tests, 1.60 s total Vitest duration; July beta/stable fixtures load, migrate pinned routes where present, and round-trip.
- Both import-cycle checks: 0 cycles.
- `check-changed` against pinned base 04fbf17d6c2: passed, including UI types, eight affected test-type graphs, lint, i18n, and dead-export checks.
- Doctor legacy-config and migration suites: both passed (32.03 s across the two Vitest shards, including cold worker preparation).
- `git diff --check`: clean.

The repository wrapper's source staging hit local ENOSPC before upload. Native Blacksmith sync on the same owned lease verified the exact base and file hashes and ran the proof remotely. An initial changed-check invocation used the remote's newer `origin/main` and included inverse sibling changes; the corrected invocation pins this branch's actual base.

Hosted CI on head `7366eaed49bcc5f3e9750418180795bdc7355179`: [checks-ui (1/3)](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/36940168750/job/110629901361) passed 8,023 tests but failed `UsagePage detail requests > releases a loaded overview when its Gateway identity is replaced`: `expected OverviewPayload to be undefined`. Fail-fast cancelled the remaining run. The same failure is independently verified on unrelated PR #162874's still-current head `dda3f8258915c215083578eb6a46dc4b95c6d9ae`, [run 36898732505](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/36898732505/job/110492893649); its Usage test and page blobs match this head. feat(tools): run non-live generator FunctionTools via FunctionNode

Generator FunctionTools now run with the same semantics as a workflow
FunctionNode, so a plain generator passed in `tools=[...]` can:

- stream intermediate `Event`s (messages and `state` deltas) to the caller
  while it runs, without those events entering the calling agent's LLM context;
- pause for human input by yielding `RequestInput`, and resume on the next turn
  with `tool_context.resume_inputs` (requires a resumable App);
- return its final result as the single non-`Event` value it yields.

Node-level `retry_config` and `timeout` are not exposed on FunctionTool; wrap the
function with `@node(...)` and pass it as a NodeTool for those. Live
(bidirectional streaming) generator tools keep their existing behavior.

Implementation:

- Route non-live sync and async generator `FunctionTool` callables through `FunctionNode` execution via `tool_context.run_node(...)` so generator tools can emit intermediate `Event`s (persisted on the tool sub-branch with `state_delta`), yield `RequestInput` for HITL pause/resume, and produce at most one final output as the tool `FunctionResponse`. Those sub-branch events stay out of the calling agent's LLM context.
- Node-backed generator `FunctionTool`s run on the caller event loop, including when `RunConfig.tool_thread_pool_config` is enabled, so their events are enqueued on the caller's loop. Offloading synchronous generator steps to the tool thread pool is handled separately.
- Leave `Event` and `RequestInput` out of a generator tool's declared response schema, so the yield type can be annotated with everything the generator yields (e.g. `AsyncGenerator[Event | dict[str, Any], None]`) and still describe only the final output. Previously such an annotation put the full `Event` JSON schema (about 72 KB) into the Vertex AI function declaration. This applies to the default JSON-schema declaration builder, which also builds the output schema of `@node` tools.

Resolves https://github.com/google/adk-python/issues/2014

fix: stop dropping temperature and top_p on the interactions API

`build_generation_config` dropped temperature, top_p and top_k with a warning that the installed google-genai has no field for them. google-genai 2.26.0 declares temperature and top_p on `interactions.GenerationConfigParam`, so on that release the warning is wrong and the caller's values are thrown away for nothing. ADK supports google-genai `>=2.19,<3`, which spans releases on both sides of the change, so the split is now read from the installed `GenerationConfigParam`: a declared knob is sent, an undeclared one is still dropped with the same warning. top_k is undeclared even in 2.26.0.

fix(flows): keep tool sub-branch events out of the calling agent's LLM context

- They hijacked the turn anchor of `single_turn` agents, so the tool's FunctionResponse was dropped from the follow-up request.

`_contents.py` now filters these events with `_BranchPath.is_tool_branch`. Every path segment below the agent's branch is checked, not only the leaf, so nested sub-branches (e.g. fan-out nodes of a NodeTool-wrapped Workflow on `<tool>@<id>.<node>@<run_id>`) are filtered too. Behavior change: a root agent no longer sees a `_SingleTurnAgentTool` sub-agent's intermediate transcript; it still receives the FunctionResponse. Agents with a non-empty branch were already excluding these events, so this unifies the two cases.

fix(proxy): stop queued registry read-throughs spending the resync budget (#44277)

* fix(proxy): stop queued registry read-throughs spending the resync budget

RegistryReadThrough.attempt serializes misses behind one lock, but every
request that was queued behind the first one still spent a unit of the
20-per-5s resync budget and re-ran the DB resync, even though the first
request had already loaded the object. A burst of more than 20 requests
for a model created on another worker therefore exhausted the budget and
the rest got 400 "Invalid model name".

attempt now checks whether the key is already loaded once it holds the
lock and returns early without touching the budget. Models check the
router's model names and deployment ids, guardrails and agents reuse
their existing registry lookups.

* test(proxy): gate the queued read-through test on events and cover each registry's loaded check

The queued-requests test now holds the first resync on an asyncio.Event instead of
a timed sleep and records calls in a recorder with tuple and frozenset state. New
tests show the model, guardrail and agent read-throughs each answer an object that
is already loaded without reading the database, so rewiring any registry's loaded
check now fails a test

* test(proxy): keep the queued read-through recorder inside its test and type the agent registry fixture

chore(helm): drop migrationJob values the chart never reads (#42141)

`migrationJob.retries` and `migrationJob.disableSchemaUpdate` are declared
in values.yaml but referenced by no template, no test and no README row.
Setting either changes nothing about the rendered Job.

`disableSchemaUpdate` is the misleading one: its comment promises "the job
will exit with code 0", but the Job hardcodes DISABLE_SCHEMA_UPDATE=false
and renders it after envVars/extraEnvVars precisely so nothing can turn the
migration off — that ordering is what #12809 fixed. An operator who reads
values.yaml, sets the flag and watches migrations run anyway has no way to
tell the knob is inert. `migrationJob.enabled: false` is the supported way
to skip the Job, and the componentized chart in helm/litellm already ships
a migrationJob block with neither key.

`retries` is simply dead: Jobs retry through `backoffLimit`, which the
chart does render.

Removing values keys is backward compatible — Helm ignores user values that
no template consumes, so existing releases setting either key keep working.

Adds a test pinning the override: with envVars.DISABLE_SCHEMA_UPDATE="true"
the Job's last env entry is still DISABLE_SCHEMA_UPDATE=false, so the
last-wins ordering cannot regress and the key cannot quietly come back as a
chart value. Verified by mutation: flipping the hardcoded value and moving
the entry above the envVars loop each fail the suite.

api_version 'v1' by the old shared default: the v1 webhook rejects that key with 401.

instead of allowing the request. A detect-mode action is still not a block.

question again is scored instead of refused from memory. The replay memory is scoped
by principal and session together, so two principals on one session id never share a
block. A text-only /guardrails/apply_guardrail call relays the text as a user turn.

* fix(guardrails): straiker v3 relays text beside an empty messages list and keys the memory on the key

/guardrails/apply_guardrail sends `messages: []` beside `text`; an empty list is no
conversation, so the text is relayed as the user turn. A verdict whose blocked_by is not
a list states no decision and takes the failure policy, the same way a missing decision
does. A key that names no user is still the caller, so the replay memory is keyed on the
key when no user is known.

test(pm): pin held-tree cleanup with two invariants and a live Windows hold

Folds the four salvaged regression tests into two invariants (publish arm,
restore arm with gc selectivity) and adds a windows-only test that maps a
real DLL from inside the live entry and reinstalls over it.

fix(pm): set a held replaced tree aside instead of failing the install

Every cleanup that runs after a publish or restore has finished deletes
garbage: the displaced .previous-* entry, a restored .displaced-* tree,
the fetch-* archives. A running Hermes process keeps the replaced
interpreter's DLLs mapped, so on Windows that delete can fail far past
the retry window and turned a completed update into "install failed:
[WinError 5]" (#124807).

One helper now owns that cleanup for all four sites. When the delete
fails it renames the tree to .reclaim-<uuid> (Windows permits renaming a
tree with mapped images): the old slot is free for the next publish of
the same entry, no restore can ever pick the half-deleted tree up, and
the next install or `hermes pm gc` deletes it once the hold is gone.
This replaces the sidecar marker for restored displacements (#128955)
and the warn-and-keep for previous entries from the salvaged commit:
a kept .previous-<entry> blocked the next publish of that entry, could
be restored half-deleted, and was unreachable by gc after a version bump.

test(fallback): trim llama.cpp alias tests to two invariants on a real endpoint

Replaces the five resolver-stub tests (one of which asserted the cloud
fall-through) with two invariants driven by a real server.json naming a live
child process, read through the ownership-checked resolver:

- fallback resolution reaches the live managed server, and with the server
  stopped returns (None, None) even with a cloud key present;
- the cached auxiliary client follows a restart onto a new port/key and
  resolves to nothing once the server stops.

Both fail on origin/main (Gemini client returned) and on the original rung
(stopped server -> Gemini; cached path -> Gemini).

fix(fallback): a bare llama.cpp alias resolves only to the live managed server

Completes the managed-endpoint rung for every caller that resolves a bare
llamacpp / llama.cpp / llama-cpp alias outside the main ladder:

- The rung moves from _resolve_custom_branch to the resolve_provider_client
  entry and to _get_cached_client, via agent/auxiliary_local_runtime.py.
  The `main_runtime is None` gate is gone: the cached auxiliary path always
  passes a normalized dict, so the rung never ran there, and a task pinned to
  llamacpp inherited a foreign main runtime's URL instead.
- No running server now means (None, None) — the same answer the main ladder's
  _resolve_llamacpp_runtime gives — instead of continuing into
  _try_custom_endpoint / _resolve_api_key_provider, which posted the local GGUF
  slug (and, for compression, the conversation) to whichever cloud provider held
  a key (#119227) or to the primary's own endpoint. OPENAI_BASE_URL is not
  consulted either: the alias table entry (b7e0d715be0) exists for explicit
  base_url lanes, and the main ladder never reads it for a bare alias.
- The cached client keys on the live endpoint (base_url + key), read at call
  time, so a server restarted on a new port/key gets a fresh client and a
  stopped one resolves to nothing instead of a stale client.
- The endpoint is resolved with the calling profile's config (load_config() at
  call time), matching the main ladder; a configured provider entry named like
  the alias still wins.
- Vision keeps the raw provider name for its final resolve so the alias is not
  flattened to bare `custom` first.
- The aux "unavailable" message names the stopped local server instead of an
  invented LLAMACPP_API_KEY.

Co-authored-by: Gille <4317663+helix4u@users.noreply.github.com>

fix(fallback): resolve llama.cpp aliases to the managed local endpoint

try_activate_fallback resolves through auxiliary_client.resolve_provider_client,
which does not use the main ladder's managed-local rung. A llamacpp alias with no
explicit base_url therefore fell through _resolve_custom_branch to
_try_custom_endpoint/_resolve_api_key_provider and got back whichever cloud
provider held credentials: the fallback posted a local GGUF slug to
generativelanguage.googleapis.com, which answered 400 "unexpected model name
format", and Hermes surfaced that as a bogus context-size rejection.

Resolve the alias to the live managed endpoint and re-enter the branch with it,
so the alias /v1 tail and alias key-scoping rules stay in force.

(vswhere -requires Microsoft.VisualStudio.Component.VC.Tools.ARM64) and
initializes VsDevCmd against it, then builds OpenSSL through vcpkg. But
vcpkg resolves Visual Studio on its own and takes the newest instance. On a
host with a second BuildTools install that lacks the native arm64 toolset,

  The selected Visual Studio instance is at: ...\Microsoft Visual Studio\18\BuildTools
  The available toolchain combinations are: x86, amd64, x86_amd64,
  amd64_x86, arm64_x86, arm64_amd64

...in the same run that logs "-> ARM64 C++ build tools found: ...\2022\BuildTools".

the desktop relaunches on the previous build ("running with the previous
dependencies — run `hermes update` to finish it"), so it never updates.

lever vcpkg's own error points at, without clobbering a caller's explicit pin
(same respect-if-set shape as CARGO_HOME/RUSTUP_HOME above).

setup (e.g. 80 for a quiet mic that peaks at RMS ~160) the VAD correctly

except silently disabled streaming TTS for every macOS voice user.

fix(desktop): drop a settled live reply the page still carries as its streaming copy

The switch-back hydrate can be composed from the baseline that still held the
reply's streaming row, under the same id the store later settled. The overlay
replaced that row in place and never checked whether the page already had the
reply committed, so the answer painted twice until the next refresh (about one
run in three of the tool-turn race). The represented-on-page check now runs
before the in-place replace and drops the stale copy; a folded tool bubble is
also matched by its answer text when the completion carried no row receipt.

fix(desktop): a finished tool turn stays one bubble when the switch-back hydrate races it

The tool-turn switch-back race still painted the answer twice, frozen on its
first chunk, in two places:

- appendLiveSessionProjection only stood the stale activate snapshot down for
  a tool-free committed reply. A tool turn's snapshot carries the turn's whole
  text and history folds narration, tools and answer into one bubble, so it
  never matched. It now stands down when the committed bubble ends in a reply
  that covers the snapshot; a mid-turn commit ends on a tool and still projects.
- overlayConcurrentMessageChanges only adds and replaces. A page composed from
  the older baseline could carry a live row the store had already retired into
  the committed reply. A baseline live row missing from the current store now
  stays retired.

The steer matrix also covers the steered tool finishing in the background:
the oracle skips backend notice rows (process_complete and friends) the way
hydration draws them.

fix(desktop): a tool turn completing during the switch-back hydrate renders once

The new switch-back-race tool-turn case caught it: when message.complete
settles the live reply while the switch-back REST page is in flight, the
overlay kept the settled stream row unless the page carried an assistant
message with the same words. History folds a tool turn's narration, tool and
reply into one bubble, so its text never equals the reply and the answer
painted twice. The completion already binds the reply to its stored row;
match that row first and keep the text rule as the fallback.

The oracle now compares a steer stored at a tool boundary by the user's
words, not the out-of-band wrapper the model sees. The review-row scenario
does not reproduce #131626's duplicate on main, so it is a plain guard
instead of a KNOWN entry.

fix(desktop): activate a tray-hidden window when anything but the tray restores it

On Windows, restore() or showInactive() on a window that the tray hid
paints the window, but it does not become the foreground window. The
window then drops all mouse and key input until the app restarts. A
relaunch from the taskbar or Start menu, a deep link, and a notification
click all restore the window this way. Only the tray menu and tray click
ran show() and focus().

that the tray hid: show(), then focus(). The call is deferred past the
native restore. Windows that the tray did not hide are not changed.

fix(relay): hand each streamed chunk over before the provider sends the next

With shared metrics on, every provider stream runs through Relay's managed
pipeline. Relay pulls the next provider chunk before it delivers the current
one, and the provider read blocked the stream's private loop, so each chunk
was withheld until the next arrived. On Desktop the reply looked stopped while
the timer kept going and queued follow-ups waited on a turn that was still
running; a steer aborted text the user never saw, stacking user bubbles with
no output between them.

The off-loop read from the previous commit fixes it. Correct its comment to
the real cause, replace the two-loop starvation test (production gives every
stream its own loop, and it bounded wall-clock at 150ms) with a single-stream
contract that deadlocks on the old code, and add a core e2e spec that steers
and queues against a paused provider with Relay managed execution on.

73c17151f61 (Sep 29) persisted maintenance.auto=false, gc.auto=0 and
fetch.writeCommitGraph=false in treeless install checkouts. 6880ffc1afa
stopped writing gc.auto=0 but never removed it, and `gc --auto` with
gc.auto=0 is a no-op (git skips every heuristic, gc.autoPackLimit included),
so the update's pack fold never ran on those checkouts: 203 -> 203 packs.

The previous commit's fingerprint required gc.writeCommitGraph=false, which
only the Oct 2 cut wrote, so the Sep 29 cohort also kept maintenance.auto=false.
Both cuts wrote maintenance.auto=false together with
fetch.writeCommitGraph=false and neither wrote
maintenance.commit-graph.enabled; that pair is now the fingerprint, and
gc.auto=0 is removed under it as well. An operator's own lone
maintenance.auto=false still never matches.

Real clear_git_debris() on a treeless clone with 203 lazy-fetch packs, git
2.53.0 and 2.55.0 alike:
  Sep 29 keys:   main 203 -> 203, #131741 203 -> 203, this 203 -> 1 (both keys gone)
  Oct 2 keys:    203 -> 1, maintenance.auto gone
  operator's own maintenance.auto=false: 203 -> 1, setting kept

fix(update): only migrate the maintenance.auto=false Hermes itself wrote

_restore_auto_maintenance unset any local maintenance.auto=false, so an
operator's own setting on a partial-clone checkout was erased on every
update (nothing records who wrote it). Remove it only with the first cut's
fingerprint: maintenance.auto, gc.writeCommitGraph and fetch.writeCommitGraph
all false and maintenance.commit-graph.enabled not yet set. The first pass
of disable_tree0_auto_maintenance writes that key, so the migration runs once
and an operator's setting is left alone before and after.

Review point from @Godhet on #131718.

fix(update): keep git's own lazy-fetch pack fold on in a partial clone

#131679 set maintenance.auto=false in the treeless install checkout to stop the
commit-graph lazy-fetch loop (#127711). That also switched off the post-fetch
`gc --auto` that git <= 2.53 runs after every lazy fetch, so packs piled up
between updates and only folded on a manual `hermes update` / `--check`
(nothing runs `--check` automatically).

The loop needs a commit-graph write, and gc.writeCommitGraph=false +
fetch.writeCommitGraph=false already stop gc and fetch from writing one.
maintenance.commit-graph.enabled=false closes the last writer (a commit-graph
maintenance task, e.g. from a user's global maintenance.strategy) while
leaving automatic maintenance, and its gc fold, on.

Checkouts that already got maintenance.auto=false from the first cut are
converged: the next update/--check unsets exactly that value.

after one updater run:
  git 2.53.0: main 101 packs, this change 1 pack, 0 commit-graph writes
  git 2.55.0: 101 / 101 (stock 2.55 maintenance does not fold), 0 writes

reported that no GUI was installed and returned without deleting it, and
the next update put the app back.

and removes it. No new removal targets: uninstall_gui() already deletes
the record. The retention tests now also run with the record as the only

fix(update): make the partial-clone pack fold and maintenance keys work together (#129712, #127711)

The two salvaged commits above disagree: #127721 persists gc.auto=0, which
turns the fold's `gc --auto` into a no-op (106 packs stay 106 on git 2.50.1,
2.53.0 and 2.55.0), and the fold itself is exposed to the loop #127721
guards against. Probed on all three gits against a blobless clone whose
commit-graph carries changed-path (Bloom) data:

- gc, `gc --auto`, `maintenance run --task=commit-graph` and
  fetch.writeCommitGraph each lazy-fetch the trees of every commit the graph
  has not seen (30 unseen commits: 30 fetches, 30 packs), and every lazy
  fetch spawns `git maintenance` again. gc.writeCommitGraph=false stops it
  (gc: 31 packs -> 1).
- Without a Bloom graph none of that happens, so the keys are a guard, not a
  fix for every partial clone.

Changes:
- keys: maintenance.auto, gc.writeCommitGraph, fetch.writeCommitGraph; gc.auto
  stays default. Idempotent (no rewrite when already set), `--local`, hidden
  console on Windows. install.sh and install.ps1 set the same three keys.
- consolidate_lazy_fetch_packs applies the keys before the fold, so installs
  that predate the installer change converge on their next update check.
- the fold runs under bounded_probe_run: subprocess.run(timeout=) kills only
  `git gc` and leaves `pack-objects` running (reproduced), and with
  GIT_NO_LAZY_FETCH.
- dropped the post-gc mark_unmarked_packs_promisor: gc keeps the .promisor
  marker on 2.50.1, 2.53.0 and 2.55.0.
- docs: updating.md troubleshooting entry.
fix(install): disable auto maintenance in tree:0 clones (#127711)

fix(update): fold lazy-fetch packfiles so a partial clone's .git stops growing

Every on-demand fetch on the promisor remote of a tree:0 installer
checkout writes its own small packfile, and no update-path step ever
consolidates them, so .git grows without bound (2,475 packs / 39 GiB
observed for a ~1 GiB repo, #129712).

Ride git's own threshold: run `git gc --auto` from the debris-cleanup
step both `hermes update --check` and `hermes update` already run.
Below gc.autoPackLimit (default 50) small packs it exits in
milliseconds; past it, the lazy-fetch packs fold into one. The folded
pack is re-marked .promisor so git 2.53+ fetches keep working (#124272),
and the gc does not write a commit-graph, which git <=2.50 misreads on
the next lazy fetch.

fix(tests): failure-writer ownership probe no longer races a real tirith download

The probe scrubs the environment down to PATH/LANG/LC_ALL/TZ, which also
dropped the harness's HERMES_DISABLE_LAZY_INSTALLS. In a fresh home with no
tirith on PATH (CI), GatewayRunner() then starts tirith's startup install on a
background thread: the PM runtime downloads and unpacks Python and uv from
GitHub while the cases run. When that unpacking overlaps the archive case, its
buffers land in the process-wide tracemalloc window and push the peak past the
8 MiB bound, so the probe reports 19/20.

The loopback fence also missed it: hermes_bootstrap's happy-eyeballs
create_connection dials with connect_ex, so the downloads reached GitHub with
blocked_external_attempts empty.

- set HERMES_DISABLE_LAZY_INSTALLS=1 in the probe environment
- fence socket.connect_ex as well as connect
- assert the receipt records no external network attempts

test(memory): migration fixture provider stands in for a formerly bundled one

Unattended consent is limited to providers that left core (#131266), so the
multi-profile fixture's fake provider has to be on that list to exercise it.

fix(memory): warn every profile whose memory provider is unavailable; say "Install declined" for a first install

The unavailable-provider warning was deduped by provider name process-wide,
so a multiplexed gateway or Desktop backend told only the first profile.
It is now keyed by (home, provider).

A first-time install refused at the consent gate said "Reinstall declined
... The installed plugin and active environment are unchanged" although
nothing was installed; migration notices now show that text to users.

fix(memory): one profile's refused migration no longer skips the others; hints name the right profile

Unattended consent is each home's own security.allow_lazy_installs, so a
refusal in one profile says nothing about the next: migrate_all_homes now
groups homes by (provider, consent) and only names the rest of a group
when that group fails. A default home with lazy installs off no longer
reports a lazy-on profile as failed while skipping its install.

The "answers apply to all of them" header is printed only when a terminal
can actually ask.

Install hints drop -p only for the default home with no sticky profile: an
agent started for a named profile (Desktop, gateway, hermes -p) printed a
bare `hermes plugins install <name>`, which installs into the sticky
profile instead. The lazy-installs-off startup line uses the same command.

fix(memory): show every memory-provider migration outcome, ask once per update

Agent-start recovery (recover_at_startup) reported installed / refused / failed /
not-in-catalog only to agent.log, and so did a selected provider that reports unavailable,
so a user with security.allow_lazy_installs: false, offline, or who declined the dependency
prompt silently ran without external memory (#119769).

- Startup outcomes go through _emit_startup_warning: printed in the CLI; other drivers get
  a sticky warn AgentNotice (Desktop toasts notices but drops warn-kind status.update), and
  the messaging gateway, which wires notice_callback per turn, receives it on turn 1.
- hermes update labels each line with the profile it is about and gives the exact
  `hermes -p <profile> plugins install <name>` command for non-active homes.
- Profiles sharing one environment get one set of dependency answers per provider
  (shared_dependency_answers): the first install asks the normal Python/Node questions,
  later homes reuse them; a decline or failure names the remaining profiles once instead of
  failing (or re-prompting) one by one; Ctrl-C ends the migration with a message (#125794).
- The success line no longer names memory.<name> (#124038); docs follow.

Co-authored-by: chelsealong <chelsealong@126.com>

fix(memory): migration note must not imply config.yaml provider keys still apply

Refs #124038.
fix(memory): identify profile homes in update migration notices
fix(memory): surface startup migration outcomes through warning sink

fix(memory): limit headless install consent to providers that left core

The unattended consent installs a plugin and its Python deps with no prompt.
It is justified for providers that shipped bundled (the user already accepted
those deps by choosing the built-in), not for any catalog plugin a synced or
cloned config happens to name in memory.provider.

docs(plugins): publish_plugin assume_consent covers the migration's lazy-install consent

The docstring still described assume_consent as only the caller's --yes-deps
answer; the memory-provider migration now passes its allow_lazy_installs
consent through the same parameter.

fix(memory): migrate deps-bearing providers without a terminal under allow_lazy_installs

Desktop, the gateway and a scripted `hermes update` have no TTY, so the
dependency consent gate refused every catalog provider that declares Python
deps: both migration hooks failed with 'Reinstall declined: dependency install
skipped (non-interactive)' and the provider stayed missing. The agent-start
hook exists precisely for those surfaces.

The configured memory.provider plus security.allow_lazy_installs (read for the
home being migrated) is the consent that let the bundled provider install its
deps on demand; carry it through dashboard_install_plugin ->
install_catalog_entry(assume_deps_consent=...). A terminal still prompts, and
allow_lazy_installs: false still refuses with the install one-liner.

test(plugins): surface the admission refusal cause in the --yes-deps e2e test

An external verification run on Linux saw this test fail with a bare
`assert 'yes-deps-plugin' in []`: the install publishes into plugins/ and
a second PM admission transaction then enables it, and that admission
folds every exception into a refusal (exit 0, plugin installed but
disabled), so the assertion carried no clue about the environment-specific
cause. Verified locally that the mechanism reproduces the exact reported
shape: injecting a failure into the second sync_venv call (the enable
admission) yields the same bare failure while the first (publish) call
succeeds.

Carry the captured CLI output in the failure message so any machine that
reproduces this shows the `Enable ... refused: <cause>` line directly in
the pytest output.

fix(plugins): let --yes-deps answer the consent gate for headless installs

A non-interactive `hermes plugins install <name> --enable` had no path
forward (#122134): the y/N gate for Python deps refuses without a TTY,
the publication of an active replacement is declined the same way
("Reinstall declined: dependency install skipped (non-interactive)"),
and the suggested `hermes plugins enable` recovery cannot publish a
plugin that was never installed.

Add an explicit `--yes-deps` flag (mutually exclusive with `--no-deps`)
that carries the user's own answer through both consent gates: the
enable-time `_consent_python_deps` prompt and the publication-time
active-replacement veto in `publish_plugin`. The fail-closed default is
unchanged — an unattended install without the flag is still refused
rather than consented to on the user's behalf.

chore(plugin-catalog): unlist retaindb, byterover and holographic (no Nous maintenance)

Nous Research will not maintain memory providers. These three entries
pointed at NousResearch/hermes-plugin-<name> repos labelled
Nous-maintained; with no maintainer they must not be offered as
official catalog plugins. The bundled copies under plugins/memory/
