* ci(sdk-java): anchor the flyway dedupe identity to runner-emitted lines

Sandboxed verification found the module-shape validator closing the
filename door but not the directory one: the guard prints file paths,
so a LF inside a directory component leaves the forged text after a
real `/` — slash-bearing and past the shape. The runner timestamps
every line it writes, and a decoded annotation continuation carries
none, so both flyway arms now accept their line only when it came from
the runner itself. The shape validation stays as the second layer for
every other channel, and its inline fixtures are timestamped so they
still reach it. The Surefire arm's matching exposure is pre-existing —
the vitest and pytest patterns share it — and is left to a follow-up.

Refs #12940

* ci(sdk-java): close the forgery family at the guard's emission sites

The third Critical in the family, and the round that ends it. The
guard interpolates contributor-controlled path bytes into ::error::
command data, and the runner percent-decodes that data where the
consumer parses — so percent-escaping control bytes was never enough:
a directory name carries the LF, the slash and every pattern byte the
decoded continuation needs. No charset rule over the consumer's module
shape can close that — the forged module is shape-indistinguishable —
and double-escaping regresses the genuine LF arm into the suppression
arm. What closes every measured arm is bounding the emitted alphabet
at the four emission sites: nothing outside a migration path's real
characters reaches the command data, so no decode pass can restore
pattern text from it.

The suppression arm needs no newline at all and no runner behaviour:
spaces on the timestamped line run the duplicate-version arm's lazy
module capture all the way to the payload, the shape rejects it, and
an unconditional continue used to discard the line's genuine config
identity with it — the duplicate storm this change exists to end, from
the opposite direction. The flyway arm now falls through to the config
arm when its capture is rejected.

chore: drop the unanchored workspace/ ignore rule that hides web-shell sources (#13155)

* chore: drop the unanchored workspace/ ignore rule that hides web-shell sources

The bare `workspace/` line under the brand-builder section matches every
directory named workspace at any depth, including the tracked source tree
packages/web-shell/client/daemon/workspace/. Its 34 files are tracked but
ignored, so a new file there never shows in git status and git add -A
skips it silently (a test in #13154 was nearly left out this way).

Nothing in the repo creates a workspace/ directory: the desktop brand
builder writes to brand-builds/, which stays ignored. The line arrived in
a squashed history import (99fd76553e), so its original intent cannot be
recovered from git.

* style(web-shell): format the two daemon/workspace tests prettier never saw

Prettier honours .gitignore, so the old bare `workspace/` rule also kept
packages/web-shell/client/daemon/workspace/ out of the formatting gate.
With the rule gone the gate checks the directory and flags these two
files; this is prettier --write output only.

fix(managed-hooks): bound Hook admission and cold restore cost (#13136)

* feat(managed-agent): implement durable Hosted Hooks (H2)

* style(runtime-broker): remove blank line rejected by Checkstyle

* test(managed-hooks): align CI guards with H2 enablement

* fix(managed-agent): select current Turn by admission sequence

* fix(hooks): keep managed command environment out of argv

* fix(serve): close Hosted Hook recovery and capacity gaps

* fix(managed-hooks): bound Hook admission and cold restore cost

Hook admission read every earlier Hook record of a Session, both in the
Session Store and in the Session authority, so the cost of each
operation grew with the Session's history and replaying a reopened log
was quadratic.

The Session Store now projects each Hook record's once key, occurrence
and ordinal, and catalog pin into indexed columns when the record first
commits. Unique indexes refuse a duplicate once key or ordinal, also a
concurrent one, and the occurrence binding and catalog digest are
compared with one committed record of the same key. V27 adds the
columns and indexes. V28 backfills them for V26 rows from their
verified bodies and blocks only the Session of a body it cannot verify.
The Session authority keeps the same keys in memory.

A cold Workspace load reads each Hook record, and each resource a
record names, once. The authority replays the log with a bounded
read-ahead; the Workspace verification reuses that result and reads the
rest in bounded batches. Hook Sessions also stop re-validating their
history on each check, read each saved Stop plan once, and group child
executions once per commit when draining.

Fixes #13132

* fix(serve): settle cancelled startup hooks and identify deletions

* docs(managed-hooks): state what the Hook admission backfill may check

Admission had already checked every row written before the index for
each condition the backfill checks, through the Session store's
resource read and the record store's apply. The backfill runs once on
those rows, so it must never check more, or it would block Sessions
whose records are valid.

* fix(hooks): settle cancelled callbacks and retry journal commits

* test(hosted): exhaust identical Store commit retries in fault gates

* fix(hooks): retain HTTP completion evidence after managed cancellation

* fix(hooks): settle cancellation before occurrence planning

* fix(managed-hooks): keep a load's verified resources only until it takes them

The Session authority kept every Stage H resource its replay verified
for as long as the Session stayed open, about 232 bytes each, although
only a cold Workspace load reads them, once. An MCP-profile load and
Sessions opened from config.ts never read them at all.

The authority now releases them when open() returns, unless the caller
asks to retain them, and takeVerifiedExtensionResources() hands them
over once. The load route takes them right after opening. The Workspace
verification queues the kinds it descends into from them, instead of
re-reading every Hook record's references, and the two unreachable
record branches are removed.

Tests now pin the reopen's read concurrency, a registration change
inside an occurrence, an equal-length digest tamper on replay, the
start and successor checks in the validation count, and a status check
that must see children committed after an earlier one.

* fix(managed-hooks): contain repeated keys in the admission backfill

V29 wrote each page's projections in one batch, so a pair of legacy
rows that repeat a once key or an occurrence ordinal of their Session
failed a unique index, and with it the whole migration. V29 now tracks
the keys it has given in the current Session. A row that repeats one
keeps no keys, and its Session is blocked with
hook_admission_record_duplicate, as a Session with an unverifiable body
is blocked.

The store logs a WARN, with the exception, when a unique index refuses
an insert, so the log shows which index refused it. The 409 message is
unchanged.

The admission tests now check that their SQL counters observed
something, and which executions they measured. The MySQL plan checks
explain the statements the store actually ran. The backfill damage
matrix covers a wrong recorded digest or length, and refuses an unnamed
kind. A new test shows two Sessions may consume the same once keys.

* fix(hooks): settle proven-unstarted pre-tool cancellations

* fix(hooks): recover initialization and bounded cancellation results

* fix(hooks): settle cancelled initialization and bounded tool results

* fix(ci): bound hosted browser dependency installation

* fix(ci): record the ci.yml growth in the workflow size baseline

The hosted-browser install step adds two lines to ci.yml, taking it to
147136 bytes: 4110 over the recorded 143026 and 14 past the 4096-byte
allowance, which is why "Check workflow file size" failed. Most of that
growth is main-side drift the allowance had been absorbing, but this PR
touches the file, so the ratchet's stale-baseline leniency does not apply
and the number has to move in the same PR. The growth is real — a bounded
apt/Playwright install — so bump the entry instead of shrinking the
workflow.

Verified locally: .github/scripts/check-workflow-size.sh exits 0 against
base a7deb01bcb, and scripts/tests/workflow-size.test.js passes 220/220.

Co-authored-by: Qwen-Coder <qwen-coder@alibabacloud.com>
Patrol-Run: qwen-pr-conflict/jmupvw3d00b

* fix(hosted): refuse cancellation with an unknown execution outcome

* fix(ci): reserve browser smoke time after slow dependency downloads

* fix(ci): keep time for smoke after slow hosted installs

* test(web-shell): wait for step expansion before selecting next group

* test(ci): align hosted browser timeout contract

* fix(hooks): preserve recovery owners and diagnostics

commits.message:
Use the app-server default output cap for TUI workspace commands (#50477)

## What changed

Remove the fixed 64 KiB output cap from `WorkspaceCommand` and send
`output_bytes_cap: None` in `command/exec` requests so bounded commands use
the app-server default. Preserve `disable_output_cap` for commands that need
uncapped output, including Git diffs.

GitOrigin-RevId: 6f2ed0d127d9ff2317670851894ae4988f7c7508

Enable Ultrafast service tiers for Amazon Bedrock Astra models (#50472)

## Why

Bedrock catalogs cleared all service-tier metadata, and requests omitted every selected tier. This prevented users from selecting `ultrafast` or using tiers defined in custom catalogs.

## What changed

- Advertise `ultrafast` for `openai.gpt-6-astra` on Mantle and the `global.openai.gpt-6-astra` and `us.openai.gpt-6-astra` Runtime variants, while retaining the implicit default tier unless users select otherwise.
- Preserve custom catalog speed tiers, service-tier definitions, and defaults while continuing to normalize Bedrock web search compatibility.
- Send selected service tiers only when the Bedrock model advertises them, including `flex`.

## Testing

Add coverage for `model/list` tier discovery, custom catalog preservation, configured and per-turn HTTP request tiers, and TUI slash-command selection, toggling, and model switching.

GitOrigin-RevId: 4793e7af7b9f604a6b7812611030da6adb8acd35

Account for JSON overhead when truncating MCP tool results (#50470)

## Why

Truncating the preview alone can leave the serialized MCP tool result above its byte budget because JSON escaping and the result wrapper add bytes.

## What changed

Measure the complete serialized replacement and progressively reduce the preview budget until the result fits or the preview is empty.

## Testing

Strengthen the regression test with quotes, backslashes, and newlines. Assert that the serialized result fits within the 1,024-byte budget and that truncating it again returns the existing result unchanged.

GitOrigin-RevId: ebd97b1a6ca71343941a96e472cb313028ac680c

Copy transcript selections as literal text while preserving rich HTML (#50467)

## Why

Copying rendered transcript selections added Markdown formatting and escapes to the plain-text clipboard payload. Selecting bold text such as `hello` could paste as `**hello**`.

## What changed

Separate the literal selection text from the Markdown source used to render clipboard HTML. Plain-text copies omit inline formatting delimiters, added code fences, and Markdown escapes while retaining list and table structure. Rich-text pastes continue to preserve formatting through HTML.

## Testing

Update clipboard and transcript selection tests to verify literal text alongside rich HTML, including lists, inline code, paths with Markdown punctuation, hard breaks, streamed code blocks, and tables across layout widths.

GitOrigin-RevId: 980ee2ed0b0e201b581a3a301fa04d796c65af2e

Retry registry authentication outages and jitter executor reconnects (#50465)

## Why

Remote executors need to recover from confirmed authentication-service outages and spread reconnect attempts after a shared outage. Registration retries must remain limited to confirmed failures before a write, since replaying an ambiguous request can replace a newer registration.

## What changed

- Retry registry responses with HTTP 502 and `authentication_service_unavailable`, alongside the existing HTTP 503 `registration_conflict` retries.
- Accept structured registry errors in `detail`, keeping the canonical `error` authoritative when both are present.
- Randomize reconnect delays between half and all of the current exponential backoff, retaining the 30-second cap.

## Testing

Add coverage for reconnect jitter bounds, authentication-outage retry cancellation, error-envelope precedence, and preservation of Noise identity and initialized sessions across retries. Make the HTTP-header helper cleanup test wait for the helper PID before cancellation and verify process termination when the provider is dropped.

GitOrigin-RevId: 35fdb57732d17b0bbfeca8a4dc557a0988e29a31

Add the `incremental_tools` feature flag (#50464)

Register `incremental_tools` as an under-development feature that is disabled by default, and expose it in the configuration schema for top-level and profile feature settings.

GitOrigin-RevId: 9579822c745e9fce598085bdc5ef8da6aabb06d7

Populate thread previews from delegated task inputs (#50462)

## Why

Delegated turns can begin without a user message, leaving threads without a task preview. Populate the preview from delegated input so these threads are discoverable before a user follow-up.

## What changed

- Extract previews from completed `create_thread` and `send_message_to_thread` outputs in the `codex_app` and `codex_tui` namespaces.
- Unwrap recognized `<codex_delegation>` inputs and decode their escaped task text for display, preserving model content. Keep plain or unrecognized wrappers as text and ignore blank inputs.
- Fill missing previews in state metadata extraction and live thread metadata updates without replacing existing previews or setting the title or `first_user_message`.

## Testing

Add tests for delegation decoding and tool filtering, preview-only metadata updates, preservation of later user-message metadata, and database listing before a user follow-up in both legacy and paginated history modes.

GitOrigin-RevId: f7b3c60ef75e08c76b4084d043e3967bf2bade22

Add capability overrides for custom model providers (#50459)

## What changed

Allow Responses-compatible providers to configure live web access and remote compaction under `model_providers.<id>.capabilities`:

```toml
[model_providers.custom.capabilities]
external_web_access = false
remote_compaction = "v2"
```

`external_web_access = false` keeps hosted web search from accessing the live web. `remote_compaction` accepts `v2` to send `compaction_trigger` items through the Responses endpoint, or `unsupported` to use local compaction. Omitted capabilities retain existing provider defaults.

## Testing

Add unit coverage for preserving unspecified defaults and a request-snapshot scenario verifying cached web search and V2 compaction for a custom provider.

GitOrigin-RevId: fbcc4870aa51c112af575d711679a3941d1e7878

Truncate oversized MCP results in paginated thread history (#50458)

## Why

Paginated thread history can persist large MCP results in completed tool-call items. Bound these stored results to avoid retaining multi-megabyte payloads.

## What changed

Apply a 64 KiB preview budget when persisting oversized MCP results in paginated history. Replace the result with a truncated text preview of its serialized JSON, preserving `is_error` and clearing `structuredContent` and `_meta`. Leave small results unchanged.

Share the truncation helper with the existing MCP tool-call event path.

## Testing

Add helper tests for unchanged small results and oversized results with structured content and metadata. Add a thread-history test verifying that persisted MCP results contain a bounded preview with the beginning, end, and truncation marker while preserving tool arguments.

GitOrigin-RevId: 09dce73c70bfd357c9b9630f456e9e5c1d8492cf

Measure rollout persistence size reductions (#50454)

## What changed

- Record original and persisted item sizes in `codex.rollout.persistence.item_bytes_v2`, distinguished by stage, and record positive size reductions in `codex.rollout.persistence.bytes_removed`. Count the full original size as removed for dropped items.
- Use explicit histogram boundaries from 1 KiB to 64 MiB for item sizes, bytes removed, and `codex.rollout.persistence.turn_bytes_v2`. Larger values remain represented in the overflow bucket and histogram sum.
- Align item and turn size stages and report a measurement error when a kept item's persisted size cannot be measured.

GitOrigin-RevId: 6487acf1c6f2c041ab9680ab398491d3c1541388

Remove the provider capability gate for tool namespaces (#50447)

## What changed

- Remove `namespace_tools` from `ProviderCapabilities` and `namespaceTools` from `ModelProviderCapabilitiesReadResponse`, updating generated schemas and SDK types.
- Preserve tool namespaces and configured collaboration tool namespaces without a provider capability check, and always use Responses Lite tool serialization for Responses Lite requests.
- Gate tool search on `supports_search_tool` and retain the existing image generation and web search checks without requiring a namespace capability.

GitOrigin-RevId: ae1843563736765a40e03a02c41ff5e470018a93

Bundle rollout attachments into a gzip tar archive (#50446)

## What changed

- Combine file-backed rollouts and buffered rollout prefixes into `rollouts.tar.gz`, keeping diagnostics as separate attachments.
- Bound the archive and its upload envelope by the existing size limit, skip invalid or duplicate archive filenames, and fall back to individual rollout attachments if archiving fails.
- Add `rollout_archive_filename` to the report thread index so rollout filenames identify archive entries or fallback attachments.

## Testing

Add an upload test that extracts the archive and verifies the filenames and contents of both a compressed file-backed rollout and a buffered rollout. Update the thread index test to check the archive filename.

GitOrigin-RevId: 973da6eec2249b04ef7992b5e1e4fd27f044b80f

Assert that only direct tool calls emit timing events (#50445)

## What changed

Strengthen `tool_call_timing_guard_ignores_code_mode_source` to capture tracing output and assert that direct and nested code-mode calls together emit exactly one `codex.tool_call` event. Disable ANSI formatting and keep callsite interest independent of untraced parallel test threads.

GitOrigin-RevId: cbf0c9bf6d4e5a72b6a1eb08e6aac43e257f2dcb

Stabilize paused-time code-mode service tests (#50443)

## Why

Tokio's paused clock can auto-advance while tests await the V8 thread. The service tests need explicit control over time when checking yield limits and grace periods.

## What changed

- Hold virtual time with a blocking-task guard that is released when dropped.
- Replace bounded polling loops with tool-start notifications and direct awaits of response tasks.
- Return an error from the test helper if the cell closes before a nested tool starts.

## Testing

Add tests covering tool-start acknowledgement when a cell throws or is terminated before invoking a nested tool, including assertions on the resulting cell responses.

GitOrigin-RevId: c221c0501ec0354052102c0211cc651008babff3

Preserve native USD amounts in thread usage responses (#50442)

## What changed

Add optional `native_usage_usd_micros` fields to thread usage totals and breakdown groups, and carry backend values through the client alongside existing credit and USD estimates. Missing or null native amounts remain `None`, while explicit zero amounts remain `Some(0)`.

## Testing

Add coverage for native totals and group amounts, mixed batches with legacy responses, and the distinction between missing, null, and zero native group amounts.

GitOrigin-RevId: 53891fc95807138e2eccb99d4cda1520b857dba4

Support ordered response items in world-state context updates (#50441)

## Why

World-state sections could return only a single optional text fragment, with message separation controlled by the fragment itself. They could not contribute explicit `ResponseItem` values alongside instructions.

## What changed

- Let sections return ordered `WorldStateUpdate` values containing fragments or response items, with `Prefix`, `Standalone`, or `Mergeable` placement.
- Preserve explicit item boundaries when grouping context updates, and place prefix updates first when assembling initial context.
- Move standalone-message decisions from fragments to world-state updates and retain snapshot handling.

## Testing

Add tests for mixed fragment/item ordering, role and standalone boundaries, initial-context prefix placement, and snapshot restoration without repeated updates.

GitOrigin-RevId: c2514c3c98538da83f5140c10a9d89f531de6549

Add a CLI command to uninstall the legacy Windows sandbox (#50437)

## What changed

Add `codex sandbox uninstall` to remove machine-wide legacy Windows sandbox accounts and network rules with administrator privileges. Run cleanup without loading configuration, preserving Codex home, sandbox directories, and filesystem permissions. Reject the command on other platforms.

Keep commands after `--` forwarded to the sandbox, including `codex sandbox -- uninstall --help`.

## Testing

Add parsing coverage for the uninstall subcommand and command separator. Add an integration test verifying that help and invalid arguments work with malformed configuration and leave configuration and credentials unchanged.

GitOrigin-RevId: d2b02ef7bc0a05742dd5eb3c47292ad517d46664

Persist additional tool definitions in rollout history (#50435)

## Why

`additional_tools` response items were excluded from rollout persistence, dropping their tool definitions from saved history.

## What changed

- Persist `additional_tools` items in both legacy and paginated history modes.
- Expose the variant in generated JSON schemas, TypeScript types, and Python models, with an optional `id`, a `role`, and arbitrary JSON tool definitions.

## Testing

Add a recorder round-trip test that verifies tool definitions survive recording and loading in both history modes without parse errors.

GitOrigin-RevId: 0e7c7b1c10401ec6513fb744de642a1cf9e461d7

Add keyboard copy selection to the owned transcript (#50434)

## What changed

- Make `/copy` select the latest completed response directly in the owned transcript. Navigate user messages, code blocks, and blockquotes with arrow keys or `j`/`k`, use `g`/`G` to jump to the ends, and press Enter to copy or Escape to close.
- Highlight selected blocks and keep surrounding context visible during navigation and resizing. Preserve source payloads for code and quotes, including rendered Mermaid diagrams and fenced Markdown tables.
- Pause queued submissions until copy mode closes, and report clipboard results in the transcript footer.

## Testing

Add tests for copy routing, keyboard navigation, highlighting and resize behavior, source whitespace and line endings, clipboard completion, and queued-input resumption.

GitOrigin-RevId: bd4f58ec17568f95d0e91014e5ddba33ca8bd57c

Allow API-key accounts to use Daybreak in the TUI (#50433)

## What changed

Allow accounts using an API key with the OpenAI provider to access `/daybreak` and Daybreak policy notices. Model availability and the connected server still determine program access.

Use the same eligibility checks for turn submission, continuation, and retries. For API-key accounts, send the selected `cyberAccessProgram` when Daybreak is enabled and omit it when Daybreak is off.

## Testing

Extend session lifecycle coverage to check API-key turn parameters with Daybreak enabled and disabled. Add an API-key `/daybreak` help snapshot and update the signed-out error snapshot.

GitOrigin-RevId: ab6d4313c430f316ef9835d4facb878aab0b9725

Preserve terminal hyperlinks in agents overview previews (#50431)

## What changed

Keep Markdown link destinations attached to prompt and last-message previews in the agents overview details pane as text wraps and is clipped. Render visible links as terminal hyperlinks, while keeping truncation ellipses unlinked.

## Testing

Add a regression test and snapshot covering links that span multiple rows, prompt links, and clipped previews with unlinked ellipses.

GitOrigin-RevId: d121e062b197790ce45a70d6d64aadcb181e4dde

Cap persisted command output in paginated history at 64 KiB (#50427)

## Why

Paginated history previously persisted completed commands' full `aggregated_output`, allowing large command outputs to inflate stored history.

## What changed

- Limit persisted command `aggregated_output` to 64 KiB, including a truncation marker. Preserve the beginning and end of the output without splitting UTF-8 characters.
- Apply the shared persistence policy to rollout recording, thread-store appends, and legacy-to-paginated history migration.
- Measure persisted payload bytes after truncation so persistence metrics reflect the stored representation.

## Testing

Add coverage for the byte limit, UTF-8 boundaries, unchanged inputs that fit, and markers that exceed the budget. Verify capped output in paginated thread history and migrated legacy history, and verify persistence metrics use the truncated payload size.

GitOrigin-RevId: 01d420d396ad34b42dc5dc208c0bf88d890639ee

Honor Retry-After headers in failed Responses events (#50418)

## Why

Streamed `response.failed` events can carry retry advice in `response.error.headers`. Ignoring it loses server-provided delays or uses a conflicting delay from a rate-limit message.

## What changed

- Parse nested `Retry-After` headers using the existing HTTP header validation and retry parser, and preserve them for rate-limit, overload, and generic retryable failures.
- Prefer valid headers over rate-limit message advice, falling back to the message when the header is absent or invalid. Keep terminal error classifications unchanged.
- Reject unrepresentable plaintext retry durations without panicking.

## Testing

Add regression coverage for header precedence, validation, and terminal errors, plus retry-loop coverage for SSE sampling, remote compaction, and WebSocket failures.

GitOrigin-RevId: 46433c2e9e6d5e804211ef96950fadd70e322b49

Clarify Git worktree choices for new and forked conversations (#50416)

## What changed

Label the `/new` and `/fork` picker options “Use current Git worktree” and “Create new Git worktree”. Explain that creating a worktree makes a separate checkout of the repository in another directory.

## Testing

Update picker assertions and snapshots for both commands to cover the revised labels and description.

GitOrigin-RevId: b7fb1aac3107e39c324707f9ae69c210a97346d7

Consolidate command execution output into `aggregated_output` (#50402)

## What changed

- Remove `stdout`, `stderr`, and `formatted_output` from `CommandExecutionItem` and `ExecCommandEndEvent`, retaining `aggregated_output` as the output field.
- Update command event producers, legacy conversion, rollout traces, and the precomputed schema. Use aggregated output for terminal trace results.
- Clear `interaction_input` in emitted and migrated command completion items.

## Testing

Update command execution and trace tests to use aggregated output, and assert that legacy rollout migration preserves `aggregatedOutput`.

GitOrigin-RevId: ed59827d4a5ec9a767084ee4feac72c2042440f2

Honor pager bindings for transcript page keys (#50396)

## Why

Transcript scrolling hardcoded `PageUp` and `PageDown` to full-page movement, ignoring customized pager bindings.

## What changed

Resolve unmodified `PageUp` and `PageDown` through the pager's scroll bindings so they can scroll by a full page, half a page, or one row, or remain unbound. Preserve the one-row overlap for full-page scrolling and leave pager typing shortcuts unhandled by the transcript.

## Testing

Add a regression test and snapshot covering default, half-page, single-row, and unbound configurations. Verify that `PageDown` reverses `PageUp` scrolling and that `j` and `Ctrl+u` remain unhandled.

GitOrigin-RevId: 945e99d7370f84f326ab71037be2924dddada32c

Honor configured keybindings before transcript navigation (#50389)

## Why

Transcript selection can consume a configured composer shortcut such as `ctrl-space`, preventing it from submitting a prompt or steering a running turn.

## What changed

Let explicitly configured shortcuts for active actions take precedence over transcript key handling when no transcript interaction is active. Include global binding fallbacks, while preserving empty `Enter` returning to the latest transcript content and default `PageUp` scrolling.

## Testing

Add regression coverage for `ctrl-space` submission with idle and running turns, default `PageUp` scrolling, and empty `Enter` returning to latest with composer or global submit bindings.

GitOrigin-RevId: 16613043a7634b47fd24e4ee9feacdce94a9fabd

Allow opting into 16 KiB ARM64 code pages for macOS signing (#50384)

Set `OAI_RCODESIGN_ARM64_16K_CODE_PAGES=true` to pass
`--arm64-16k-code-pages` when signing with `rcodesign`. The option is
disabled by default.

GitOrigin-RevId: ee7d4992f89a8fe2eb355fb2516a0188e7583812

Fix thread unloading after disconnect during MCP startup (#50380)

## Why

If required MCP startup outlasts the requesting connection's cleanup, the newly created thread can remain loaded without subscribers because its listener is never started.

## What changed

Start the thread listener even when the requesting connection has already closed, allowing normal idle unloading to clean up the thread while preserving the `ConnectionClosed` result.

## Testing

Add a regression test that disconnects during blocked required MCP startup, then releases startup and verifies a `thread/closed` notification, an empty `thread/loaded/list`, and MCP process exit on Unix.

GitOrigin-RevId: 4ad912a82177266316042d806f5faa1713a48fa4

Use printable ASCII terminal titles under GNU Screen (#50375)

## Why

GNU Screen truncates Unicode in OSC titles to a byte, which can turn visible characters into control bytes and spill title text into the terminal.

## What changed

Detect Screen through `STY` and convert the full terminal title to printable ASCII. Map activity spinners and the status dot to ASCII equivalents, and replace other non-ASCII content with `?`. Keep Unicode titles outside Screen and preserve Unicode in TUI status rendering.

## Testing

Add coverage for ASCII title output with activity indicators and Unicode names, preserved Unicode outside Screen, and removal of control and invisible formatting characters.

GitOrigin-RevId: e6b45b9be0d06ab3c3eece89885647f3e9db17da

Remove initial messages from session configuration events (#50360)

## What changed

Remove `initial_messages` from `SessionConfiguredEvent` and the corresponding schema. Stop attaching replay history to startup events for resumed or rejoined threads, and remove `InitialHistory::get_event_msgs`.

## Testing

Update the MCP resume test to verify persisted tool events through `load_history`, and retain coverage that resumed requests include prior conversation items.

GitOrigin-RevId: 54b72bc44423c9b1ef2051891ef392c0ede32fe5

Render ANSI styles in TUI hook system messages (#50359)

## Why

Hook system messages were rendered as plain text, leaving ANSI formatting uninterpreted.

## What changed

Parse hook system messages into styled spans so colors and text styles render across lines. Preserve hook prefixes, continuation indentation, and trailing blank lines.

## Testing

Add a snapshot test for multiline ANSI styling and style resets, and extend multiline coverage to include a combining character and a trailing newline.

GitOrigin-RevId: 0a5a88ec26fac114fc66efa656bacf6fa15a1adf

Skip unrelated subtrees during config alias normalization (#50354)

Return a clone immediately when the current path is not a prefix of any
registered legacy config key. This avoids recursively visiting unrelated
subtrees while preserving alias normalization along matching paths.

GitOrigin-RevId: 1c7e62898e12ab3f468b978f865805989914ac44

Back off automatic remote control reconnects with jitter (#50348)

## Why

Closed WebSocket connections previously triggered immediate reconnects, and successful handshakes reset backoff even when connections were short-lived.

## What changed

- Delay automatic reconnects before token refresh or enrollment, and report `Connecting` while waiting.
- Use exponential backoff with jitter between half and all of the delay, starting at 5 seconds and capped at 30 seconds.
- Retain backoff across short-lived connections and reset it after a connection lasts at least 60 seconds.
- Interrupt the reconnect delay on shutdown, auth owner invalidation, or enable/disable changes, including an immediate disable/enable pair.

## Testing

Add connection tests for delayed token refresh, backoff retention and reset, explicit re-enabling, and prompt shutdown. Update retry tests to check jitter bounds, saturation during sustained failures, and backoff retention after a successful handshake.

GitOrigin-RevId: 0b9055ff64ff7d96f2d974b73ced8d4ffd02ac9e

Keep the subagent picker consistent with thread archive state (#50345)

## Why

Cached subagents can remain in the TUI picker after being archived, including when archive notifications are missed.

## What changed

- Hide archived threads from the picker and keyboard navigation, and restore them when unarchived.
- Refresh both active and archived descendants to reconcile cached visibility, including after dropped server events. Queue a follow-up refresh when needed and preserve visibility changes received during an in-flight refresh.
- Preserve picker selection by thread ID as visible rows change, and mark archived thread attachments as replay-only.

## Testing

Extend regression coverage for missed archives, unarchive notifications, hidden subagent navigation, and the subagent enable prompt when only archived subagents are cached.

GitOrigin-RevId: 9e75906dfe6946b1400583a386922453e2b77ea1

Add end-to-end coverage for MCP sandbox state enforcement (#50339)

## What changed

Add an MCP integration test that forwards sandbox state from tool-call metadata unchanged to `codex sandbox --sandbox-state-json` and runs a real subprocess.

Verify that workspace writes succeed, overwriting an existing file outside the workspace fails and preserves its contents, and relative paths resolve against `sandboxCwd` rather than the MCP server's working directory.

GitOrigin-RevId: 768513c74679010e806a62dffdde6b7cccbfb41f

Record Guardian V2 Decisions agreement and latency metrics (#50273)

## What changed

Record `agree`, `disagree`, or `unavailable` comparisons between Decisions risk classifications and accepted Responses scores. Emit paired latency histograms only when both backends succeed, and include request preparation and queue time in Decisions duration. Report unavailable comparisons when the comparison feature is enabled but the Decisions sampler is not initialized.

## Testing

Extend lifecycle coverage for an uninitialized Decisions sampler, checking skipped outcome and unavailable comparison metrics while preserving the baseline score.

GitOrigin-RevId: f11789ab5d5fd6957b7913d849bbb2ae7006d3ed

Bound tmux option probes to one second (#50219)

## Why

A hung tmux command or a descendant holding stdout open can block terminal input setup indefinitely.

## What changed

Run tmux option probes on a worker thread with a shared one-second deadline, returning default input options when the wait times out. Prevent overlapping probes and kill and reap commands that exceed the deadline.

Capture stdout in a temporary file so completed commands do not wait for descendants to close it, and read at most 4 KiB of output.

## Testing

Add Unix regression tests for successful output, killing and reaping a timed-out command, and returning promptly when a descendant keeps stdout open.

GitOrigin-RevId: a5a4c9323a3e18d1baada5ab1cf3734ce6a9403a

Use the shared text editor for command-center task renaming (#50216)

## What changed

Replace the rename field with a single-line `TextArea` that honors configured editor bindings and the composer's Vim setting. Start renaming in insert mode and support Vim Escape recovery on legacy terminals.

Strip carriage returns and newlines from titles and pasted text, keep Vim linewise pastes inline, and scroll horizontally at grapheme boundaries to keep the cursor visible.

## Testing

Add single-line editor coverage for newline filtering, Vim commands, repeat edits, and inline yanks. Extend command-center tests to cover Vim renaming across status-filter changes and cursor placement in narrow layouts.

GitOrigin-RevId: 8d320d6b6de9f77e18292169418383929ca6ceda

Support Ctrl+Insert for copying TUI selections (#50215)

## Why

Windows Terminal forwards `Ctrl+Insert` when its Copy action has no native terminal selection. Recognize this shortcut so it can copy text selected within Codex.

## What changed

Add `Ctrl+Insert` to the shared copy-key detection used by transcript and composer selections. Use the same detection for transcript input ownership so the selection consumes the shortcut before other input handlers.

## Testing

Extend transcript tests to verify `Ctrl+Insert` input ownership and copying. Extend composer tests and snapshots to verify that failed or unconfirmed copies preserve the selection, while confirmed copies clear it without changing the draft or cursor.

GitOrigin-RevId: 5a33c72cff4c4395511779a7051fc92f8bd5e5d7

Make transcript mouse scroll speed configurable (#50209)

## What changed

Add `tui.mouse_scroll_speed` as a finite positive multiplier for transcript mouse wheel scrolling, including transcript overlays and session previews. Change the default from three rows to one row per wheel event; set the multiplier to `3.0` to retain the previous speed.

Fractional values accumulate movement across events and discard the remainder when direction reverses. For example, `0.5` scrolls one row every two events. Following the latest output pauses only when a whole row moves.

## Testing

Add tests for configuration validation, integer and fractional scroll speeds, direction changes, decimal accumulation, and following behavior. Extend local settings coverage to include a command-line override for the new setting.

GitOrigin-RevId: d355e246fd943415f0ce5a6affe849f77f3615e6

Release stable Markdown tables into scrollback during streaming (#50207)

## Why

Table holdback kept completed tables and subsequent content mutable until the response finished. Releasing completed tables earlier also requires a final scrollback reflow when late reference-link definitions change previously emitted content.

## What changed

- Release table holdback once the containing top-level Markdown block is stable, rescanning the remaining tail for later tables.
- Track completed-block boundaries across incremental and full renders.
- Request scrollback reflow at answer completion when reference-link definitions are present, including definitions pending without a trailing newline.

## Testing

Add regression assertions and snapshots for completed tables entering scrollback while later tables remain mutable, and for late reference-link definitions resolving correctly at completion. Cover reflow requests with and without a trailing newline and reference handling with inline visualizations enabled.

GitOrigin-RevId: a6b2aac74496281495b53840bbb1daf06bef60d2

Report the configured TUI mode in `codex doctor` (#50200)

## What changed

Add `configured TUI mode` to the configuration details in human-readable and JSON doctor reports. Report `fullscreen` when `tui.fullscreen_transcript` is enabled and `scrollback` when it is disabled.

## Testing

Add an integration test covering both configuration values in JSON output and update the human-readable report snapshot to include the mode.

GitOrigin-RevId: beb62ddfa62a3516a64b5a69d5a41b257434f5d5

Restore the account email in `/status` after account updates (#50199)

## Why

Account-update notifications include authentication mode and plan information but
omit the email, causing `/status` to lose the signed-in account's email after an
update.

## What changed

Fetch the ChatGPT account email asynchronously after account updates, with a
30-second timeout, without blocking terminal input. Apply the result only if its
request ID is still current, invalidating pending results on subsequent account
updates and disconnects.

## Testing

Extend the account-update test to verify that the email is restored and a stale
result is ignored. Update the status snapshot to include the account email and
plan alongside credits and limits.

GitOrigin-RevId: 202421f78f3d6a7b373194f9c65d1c22d70a04c1

Replace the Figma OAuth exception with Mercado Pago (#50189)

## What changed

Allow the issuer `https://mcp.mercadopago.com/mcp` to use authorization endpoints on `https://auth.mercadopago.com` and token endpoints on `https://mcp.mercadopago.com` without issuer-bound callbacks. Remove the previous Figma exception.

## Testing

Update the provider-exception test to accept the Mercado Pago combination and reject lookalike issuer hosts, unrelated token hosts, and HTTP issuer and token URLs.

GitOrigin-RevId: 3838c7e4c32d6a2022f0011d6020e383035fe67f

Add `dots` to issue labeler guidance (#50183)

Teach the issue labeler to suggest `dots` for issues about setting up
ChatGPT dots or managing their ongoing work. Exclude these issues from
the generic `agent` fallback.

GitOrigin-RevId: 6950c1bbde3aaf7f050e64484658f4ed1e4ae6e8

Enable writable file streaming in exec-server (#50177)

## What changed

Advertise `fileWriteStreaming` and support `fs/open` with `mode: "replace"` to create or truncate a file for writing. Implement `fs/writeBlock` with explicit offsets and nonempty chunks of up to 1 MiB, rejecting ranges beyond the signed 64-bit file offset limit.

Apply write sandbox permissions when opening writable handles, including when full-disk reads are allowed. Keep `read` as the default open mode.

## Testing

Add integration coverage for positional writes, chunk and offset bounds, replacement truncation, read/write handle permissions, and sandbox write restrictions. Verify that duplicate handle IDs and exhausted handle capacity reject replacement opens without creating or truncating files.

GitOrigin-RevId: 696ee6437dd5f5b69d5a7667dddea0ff44472094

Upgrade `age` to 0.12.1 and remove the obsolete advisory exception (#50166)

## Why

Local secrets storage pulled in the unmaintained `proc-macro-error2` through `age` and `i18n-embed-fl`, requiring an exception for `RUSTSEC-2026-0173`.

## What changed

Upgrade `age` to `0.12.1` and update the Cargo and Bazel lockfiles. The updated dependency chain uses `proc-macro-error3`, allowing removal of the advisory exception from both `cargo-audit` and `cargo-deny` configuration.

GitOrigin-RevId: 7e18dec4d71d9260512f54fbfe71dbe4e6ee8a5d

Bound in-flight file opens in exec-server (#50162)

## Why

The per-connection limit of 128 file read handles was checked only after opening the file, leaving pending opens outside the limit.

## What changed

Reserve a semaphore permit before polling the file-open future, counting pending opens and registered handles against the same limit. Release capacity when an open fails or is cancelled, or when a handle closes, even if a read still retains the file.

Use synchronous handle-table locks that never cross an await, and recheck duplicate IDs after opening to preserve the winning handle during concurrent opens.

## Testing

Add tests for stalled-open progress, pending-open admission limits, permit cleanup after failure or cancellation, capacity reuse while a file remains in use, and concurrent duplicate IDs.

GitOrigin-RevId: caabf38c74dda5951f2fc75234a7149daaa01263

Add managed worktree tools to the TUI (#50148)

## What changed

Expose `create_worktree`, `get_worktree_creation_status`, and `list_worktrees` through MCP when the worktrees feature is enabled for a trusted local project and attachment storage is available. Support both embedded and local daemon sessions.

Create worktrees asynchronously and attach them to the requesting task, with ownership and attachments retained across restarts. Default to the repository's remote default branch unless `ref` is supplied. Keep the task's working directory and execution environment unchanged, and leave uncommitted source changes in place.

Reject creation in ephemeral side conversations and explicitly untrusted source projects, reuse pending operations, and reject configured MCP servers that conflict with the TUI tools namespace.

## Testing

Add integration and model-request snapshot coverage for creation, polling, listing, attachment persistence across restart, task isolation, trust checks, namespace conflicts, and worker failure reporting.

feat(llms): opt-in Langfuse tracing for BYOK providers plus env tags, metadata and environment (#14787)

* feat(llms): opt-in Langfuse tracing for BYOK providers plus env tags, metadata and environment

Langfuse tracing was limited to the cline and cline-pass providers, so an
operator pointing LANGFUSE_* credentials at their own instance could not trace
OpenRouter or any other BYOK provider. CLINE_LANGFUSE_ALL_PROVIDERS=1 now opts
third-party providers in. They are exported only through the isolated direct
exporter and never through the host OTLP relay, so BYOK prompts cannot reach a
collector the operator did not configure themselves.

Benchmark and isolated-environment runs can label every trace from the
environment: LANGFUSE_TRACING_ENVIRONMENT sets the Langfuse environment on the
direct exporter, CLINE_LANGFUSE_TAGS adds comma-separated trace tags, and
CLINE_LANGFUSE_METADATA adds trace metadata as a JSON object or key=value
pairs. Env values merge under the runtime's own attributes, and env-only
attributes propagate even when a call supplies none of its own.

* docs(llms): state that Langfuse tracing covers streamed language requests only

Dedicated image generation uses the AI SDK's generateImage, which takes no
telemetry option and has no Langfuse integration hook, so it has never been
traced for any provider. Document that scope in the resolver and the runbook
rather than implying the BYOK opt-in covers it.

* desktop: format connectors view

AccountProvider exposes accountReady so the unavailable card can show a
spinner until the first identity lookup finishes instead of telling a
signed-in user without beta access to sign in.

fix(db): drop the legacy basejump account_user select policy (KRTX-1128) (#8793)

## Review in 60 seconds

- Dropped the legacy `users can view their own account_users` SELECT
policy on `basejump.account_user` — the exact object the Supabase
performance advisor flags with `auth_rls_initplan` (its `USING (user_id
= auth.uid())` re-evaluates `auth.uid()` for every row).
- The policy guards nothing: basejump was retired on 2026-07-06
(`20260706120000000_retire_basejump`), no code reads or writes
`basejump.*` (the API connects as postgres/service_role, which RLS does
not apply to; web/mobile/SDK never query the schema through PostgREST),
and a fresh install's bootstrap stub (`0000_bootstrap.sql`) creates this
table without any policy. Dropping the policy moves prod to the
fresh-install state instead of preserving dead state forever.
- Scope is exactly this one policy: the table keeps its ~394k historical
rows and its other two legacy policies (`users can view their
teammates`, `Account users can be deleted by owners except primary
account o` — not flagged by this lint). The full basejump drop remains
the separate planned migration documented in `packages/db/MIGRATIONS.md`
(existing).

No demo video: code-only change

**Risk:** low — no code path reads through the policy (grep over apps/
and packages/ shows zero `basejump` references outside comments and the
stub bootstrap; the readers left in the 2026-07-06 retirement deploy).
The only behavior change is what an `authenticated`-role query of
`basejump.account_user` would return, and nothing issues one. `DROP
POLICY` takes a brief `ACCESS EXCLUSIVE` lock on a table with no
writers; `lock_timeout` is the house 2 s.
**Verified:** `bun test
scripts/drop-legacy-account-user-select-policy.integration.test.ts` → `3
pass; 0 fail` (red `3 fail; 0 pass` before the migration file existed) ·
`pnpm --filter @kortix/db test` → `272 pass; 0 fail` · `pnpm --filter
@kortix/db lint` → `Found 0 issues in 178 files` · full migration corpus
on a fresh Postgres 15 → 304 migrations applied, exit 0 · `bun
scripts/schema-contract.ts` → `OK — kortix.ts describes the migrated
schema`. Unrun in this sandbox (named below): the full `pnpm test`, the
worktree local stack, and the `--db-only` lane — all require Docker,
which this sandbox cannot start.
suna-skills: migration, testing, learnings, worktree, contributing
ponytail: full · review: Lean already. Ship. · markers: 0

## Summary

The Supabase performance advisor reports `auth_rls_initplan` (WARN,
EXTERNAL) on `basejump.account_user`: the legacy policy `users can view
their own account_users` evaluates `auth.uid()` per row, which "produces
suboptimal query performance at scale". The advisor's generic
remediation is to rewrite the policy with `(select auth.<function>())`.
This PR goes one step smaller and removes the cause instead: the policy
is a leftover of the retired basejump framework that guards nothing, so
the migration drops it rather than preserving dead state. Fresh installs
never had it (the bootstrap stub creates the table with no policies), so
the change also aligns prod with the fresh-install state.

Closes KRTX-1128

## Demo video

No demo video: code-only change

## Type of change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Refactor / chore
- [ ] Docs / skills
- [ ] Infrastructure / CI
- [ ] Security fix
- [ ] Breaking change

## How was this tested?

All commands ran in this sandbox against a real PostgreSQL 15.19
(`initdb` cluster on 127.0.0.1:55432 — Docker is unavailable here, so
the local Supabase stack cannot start; `validate-engineering-runtime`
prints `SKIP Docker: the sandbox kernel has no netfilter/bridge
support`).

**The prod state, read from the prod database through the Management API
(read-only `SELECT`):**

```text
pg_policies → schemaname=basejump tablename=account_user
  policyname = "users can view their own account_users"
  roles = {authenticated}, cmd = SELECT, qual = (user_id = auth.uid())   ← flagged
  policyname = "users can view their teammates"          (has_role_on_account — not flagged)
  policyname = "Account users can be deleted by owners except primary account o"  (not flagged)
pg_stat_user_tables → basejump.account_user n_live_tup = 394576 (rows stay)
pg_class owner of every basejump table = postgres (the deploy migration role)
```

**1. Failing test first.** The new integration test recreates the prod
state on a real postgres (stub table + the three legacy policies,
`auth.uid()` stub, `authenticated` role from `test-prereqs.sql`), then
applies the migration the way node-pg-migrate does (one transaction) and
checks `pg_policies`. Before the migration file existed:

```text
$ TEST_DATABASE_URL=... bun test scripts/drop-legacy-account-user-select-policy.integration.test.ts
(fail) … > exactly one migration drops the legacy policy, and the fixture seeds the prod state
(fail) … > the migration drops exactly the flagged policy, idempotently
(fail) … > the migration is a no-op when the whole basejump schema is absent
 0 pass
 3 fail
Ran 3 tests across 1 file. [59.00ms]
```

**2. The same test after the migration lands** (green, and the
assertions are catalog state, not source text):


## Summary

Closes KRTX-1127.

KRTX-1127 files a slow `pg_stat_statements` fingerprint: `select
"kortix"."accounts"."account_id", …
"kortix"."credit_accounts"."balance_precise",
"kortix"."credit_accounts"."<literal>" ×3, … "ti…` at mean 3978 ms × 47
calls (186,947 ms total, buffer hit 98%, role `postgres`). That
normalized shape is the admin accounts-list query in
`apps/api/src/admin/index.ts` — the three `<literal>` columns are
`expiring_credits_precise` / `non_expiring_credits_precise` /
`daily_credits_balance_precise` (24+ character names the collector
redacts) and `"ti…` is `tier`. The `auth.users` in the issue title is
the correlated owner-email subquery inside the same statement, not the
`platform-roles.ts` anchors the issue lists (those are microsecond
primary-key point lookups and are not the slow statement).

Every recorded call of this fingerprint carries the `search` filter:

```sql
where accounts.name ilike $1
   or EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM auth.users au
              INNER JOIN kortix.account_members am ON am.user_id = au.id
              WHERE am.account_id = accounts.account_id AND au.email ILIKE $2)
order by accounts.created_at desc limit $3
```

Root cause: for that `OR` + `EXISTS` shape the planner materialized the
EXISTS as a **hashed SubPlan driven by `account_memberships`** —
`Parallel Index Only Scan on account_members_pkey` (46,092 rows) feeding
`Index Scan using users_pkey on users … loops=46,096`, ~0.97 ms per
probe because the 472 MB `auth.users` heap is evicted between the rare
admin searches. The per-row `owner_email`/`member_count` subplans were
cheap (they ran only for the 20 page rows); the materialization is the
whole cost.

Evidence (all read-only, prod):

| Measurement | Value |
| --- | --- |
| `pg_stat_statements`, filed fingerprint (old tiebreak shape) | 47
calls, mean 3977.6 ms, total 186,947.3 ms, hit 97.7% |
| `pg_stat_statements`, current-code shape (`ORDER BY (am.user_id = …)
DESC, …`) | 33 calls, mean 8408.8 ms, total 277,490.7 ms |
| `EXPLAIN (ANALYZE)` on prod, current shape, `search='%a%'` | 45,192
ms; hashed SubPlan 45,028 ms (99.7%); 30,423 shared reads |
| Same statement, fenced users-first form, `'%a%'` | 4,199 ms; `Seq Scan
on users` (ILIKE filter) + 399,769 index-only probes by `user_id` |
| Fenced form, selective pattern `'%kortix%'` | 756 ms |
| The count query (same predicate, no target-list subqueries) | mean
397.3 ms × 33 calls — the same hashed SubPlan, measured warm |

## What changed

- `apps/api/src/admin/accounts-search.ts` (new):
`adminAccountsSearchCondition(search)` — the shared search predicate.
The email branch is `accounts.account_id IN (SELECT m.account_id FROM
auth.users au JOIN LATERAL (SELECT am.account_id FROM
kortix.account_members am WHERE am.user_id = au.id OFFSET 0) m ON true
WHERE au.email ILIKE $p)`. The `OFFSET 0` fence stops the planner from
pulling the lateral up and reverting to the memberships-first hashed
SubPlan.
- `apps/api/src/admin/index.ts`: the search branch pushes the shared
predicate instead of the inline `EXISTS` (the count query shares the
same `conds`, so both statements are fixed).
- `apps/api/src/admin/accounts-search.integration.test.ts` (new, DB
suite): behavior equivalence against the pre-fence predicate plus the
plan-shape guard.

The fence composes with an index: a future trigram index on
`auth.users(email)` makes the users side index-driven without any
further change (the LATERAL pins only the join order, not the users
access path).

## Follow-up for a human (out-of-band index)

`pg_trgm` 1.6 is already installed on the prod project, but this repo's
migration pipeline **cannot** build an index on `auth.users`: the table
is owned by `supabase_auth_admin` and `CREATE INDEX` requires table
ownership (`pg_has_role('postgres','supabase_auth_admin','member')` is
false — verified read-only via the Management API read-only SQL
endpoint). A migration would fail the DB Migrations gate on
dev/staging/prod. When an operator with Supabase dashboard access can
run it:

```sql
create index concurrently if not exists idx_auth_users_email_trgm
  on auth.users using gin (email gin_trgm_ops);
```

That turns the users side into a bitmap scan (tens of ms per search) and
closes the pathological single-letter search too. This PR is
intentionally migration-free so it lands clean.

| `agent_versions_previous_version_id_fkey` | `previous_version_id`
(ordinal 15) | `agent_versions(version_id)` | NO ACTION / NO ACTION |

`public.agent_versions` is a legacy table from the retired Suna backend:
prod, dev and staging carry it (verified for prod; the others inferred
from the same lineage), and a fresh database never had it. A bare
`CREATE INDEX` on a missing relation would abort the whole migration
batch, so `up` probes `to_regclass('public.agent_versions')` and does
nothing where the table is absent — recorded as applied either way, so
the ledger stays consistent.

The migration is `perf`-scoped: no code change, no schema declaration
(the table is outside the `kortix` schema the Drizzle schema-contract
reads), no snapshot change.

## Rollout / rollback

**Rollout:** the release pipeline applies migrations before the new
version boots (`deploy-dev.yml` / `deploy-prod.yml` → `pnpm --filter
@kortix/db migrate`). The two `CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY` builds run
outside the batch transaction: each takes a brief `ShareUpdateExclusive`
lock on `public.agent_versions` (no query or write blocking), waits with
`lock_timeout = '180s'` for transactions that began before it, and
builds serially (the runner executes every queued statement one at a
time — one CIC per table at a time). On a ~385k-row / 3 GB table expect
minutes, not seconds. Fresh databases skip it via the `to_regclass`
guard and record the migration as applied.

**Rollback:** no code to revert; the migration is additive. Drop the
indexes concurrently, outside a transaction:

```sql
set lock_timeout = '180s';
drop index concurrently if exists public.idx_agent_versions_created_by;
drop index concurrently if exists public.idx_agent_versions_previous_version_id;
```

Re-running the migration afterward is safe (`IF NOT EXISTS`;
node-pg-migrate skips an already-recorded file). `pnpm migrate down` on
this file throws by design (`down = false`, like every `.concurrent.ts`
sibling) — the DROP INDEX above is the rollback.

**If the apply fails:** a `55P03` (`lock_timeout` exceeded) aborts the
deploy with the previous version still serving. A cancelled CIC can
leave an `INVALID` index shell that `IF NOT EXISTS` would then silently
keep — per `packages/db/MIGRATIONS.md` ("A migration failed in prod")
and the learnings rule (one CIC per table at a time): find it with
`select indexrelname from pg_stat_user_indexes s join pg_index i on
i.indexrelid = s.indexrelid where not i.indisvalid;`, `drop index
concurrently if exists <it>;`, re-run the migration's statements by hand
with `set lock_timeout='180s'; set statement_timeout='30min';`,
reconcile `kortix_migrations.pgmigrations`, and rerun the deploy. Never
edit the merged migration file.

**Confirm the fix:** re-run the advisor collector (`GET
/v1/projects/<ref>/advisors/performance`) after the prod promote —
`unindexed_foreign_keys` must no longer list `public.agent_versions`
(both its FK entries gone).

## Summary

The Supabase performance advisor reports `unindexed_foreign_keys` on
`public.user_roles` (foreign key `user_roles_granted_by_fkey`, column
`granted_by`). This adds the missing covering index in a new migration
under `packages/db`, following the repo's migration skill: a
`.concurrent.ts` escape-hatch migration with `CREATE INDEX
CONCURRENTLY`, 180s `lock_timeout`, one statement per call, `IF NOT
EXISTS`.

The table is not in the Drizzle model (`src/schema/kortix.ts` models the
`kortix` schema only) and not in the baseline, so there is no snapshot
change and no `kortix.ts` declaration; the schema contract scopes to the
`kortix` schema. Because the migrations never create
`public.user_roles`, the build is guarded by
`to_regclass('public.user_roles')` and skips fresh databases where the
table does not exist.

The commit also records one rule in the learnings ledger, paid for
during this change: a `CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY` issued directly from
an async `up()` (`await pgm.db.query(...)`) runs inside the runner's
still-open single transaction and fails with `25001`; the CONCURRENTLY
statement must be queued through `pgm.sql()`.
`tests/migration/user-roles-legacy-fk-index.test.ts` is its enforcement
(the has-table case fails with exit 1 when the statement is issued
directly).

Closes KRTX-1124

The Supabase performance advisor reports `unindexed_foreign_keys` on
`basejump.invitations` (KRTX-1087). Prod's live catalog (read via the
read-only SQL endpoint) confirms both foreign keys lack a covering
index:

is the table's 5th column (the advisor's `fkey_columns: [5]`)
- `invitations_account_id_fkey`: `FOREIGN KEY (account_id) REFERENCES
basejump.accounts(id) ON DELETE CASCADE`

The only existing indexes on the table are `invitations_pkey` and
`invitations_token_key`. The advisor's finding is per-entity, so both
FKs need indexes for the entity's finding to clear; they are two
statements in one migration for one logical change (cover this table's
unindexed FKs), built strictly sequentially per the repo's learning that
parallel `CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY` builds on one table starve each
other's lock-acquisition points.

Root cause: the basejump schema predates the repo's baseline; its
objects are not modeled in the Drizzle schema (existing:
`packages/db/src/schema/kortix.ts` models the `kortix` schema only), so
no migration ever covered this table and the schema-contract tooling

perf(db): prepared connections plan every execution for its own parameters (#8839) ## Summary Makes `DB_PREPARE_STATEMENTS` safe to turn on. It does not turn it on anywhere. - With prepared statements, PostgreSQL may switch a statement to a generic plan after about 5 executions. A generic plan cannot use a partial index whose predicate arrives as a parameter. perf(snapshots): exact-name Platinum template lookups; reap the predecessor off the session path (#8780) ## Problem The first session after every Kortix deploy spent **~8.7 s** in `image:resolved` (Dev, 2026-10-02, a8986fe7: 8,662 ms US, 8,851 ms EU). Warm sessions on the same process resolve in 137–443 ms, so this is a once-per-deploy cliff that users hit constantly on Dev. Cause, traced end to end: 1. The release gate (#8743) builds the next image **unpublished**, so the template row still points at the predecessor and the trust-the-row fast path misses. 2. That session's `ensureSandboxImage` records the new snapshot; `recordTemplateBuilt` **awaited** `reapPredecessorSnapshot` → `PlatinumAdapter.deleteSnapshot` → `fetchAllTemplates`: a walk of every template in the org. 3. Kortix Dev holds **1,671** templates = 34 pages at ~250 ms each (us-west-2 → EU control plane). The EU control plane logged ~95 `GET /v1/templates` in 17 s for two concurrent sessions. Also: `TEMPLATES_MAX_PAGES` was 40 (2,000 templates). Past that every full walk throws, `getSnapshotState` turns into `unknown`, and session starts fail. Kortix Dev grows ~70 templates/day. ## Change - Platinum control planes filter `GET /v1/templates?name=` (exact, since June). `findTemplateByName`, `deleteSnapshot` and `findFirstActiveSnapshot` now use it: one request per name. A control plane that ignores the filter returns an unfiltered page; that is detected and reused as page 0, so the old walk runs with the **same request count** as before. - `recordTemplateBuilt` no longer waits for the predecessor reap (already best-effort: it catches and logs, quota GC collects leftovers). - `TEMPLATES_MAX_PAGES` 40 → 200. ## Verification - Simulated 1,671-template org at 250 ms/request: first-session reap **35 requests / 8,839 ms on the critical path → 2 requests / 506 ms in the background**; `getSnapshotState` stays 1 request / 253 ms. - New tests: 10 exact-name cases (one request for found, absent, deep-in-org, delete with duplicates, ranked candidates; errors stay listing errors; 401 propagates; filter-ignoring server keeps its request count; walks past 2,000), plus `templates-record-reap-async` (the caller returns while the provider delete is pending). On the old source, 8 of the 10 and the reap test fail (timeout). - 73 test files (snapshots, providers, Platinum shared, session services, provider transition): **612 pass, 0 fail**. `tsc --noEmit` clean. No new biome findings in edited files; the new file is clean. --- Need help on this PR? Tag @codesmith-bot with what you need. Autofix is disabled.

perf(proxy): /v1/p reads the token row once and overlaps the sandbox row with auth (#8774) ## Problem On Dev, a tiny proxied call to `/v1/p///…` takes 0.9–1.3 s. Server-Timing shows most of that in the database: `db;desc="n=6"` at 760–964 ms. The Dev API runs in us-west-2 and its database in us-east-2, so every statement crosses the continent. File listing and every UI→box call pay this. Tracing the real statements on a real database (new suite below) showed what is sequential on a warm PAT request: 1. `account_tokens ⨝ accounts`: the PAT check. 2. `account_tokens` again: `buildActor` re-reads **the same row** for the token's IAM binding (`project_id`, `agent_grant`, `service_account_id`, `on_behalf_of_user_id`). 3. `session_sandboxes ⨝ project_sessions`: the sandbox row, which only started after auth finished. In prod the binding read is behind a 15 s memo, so calls more than 15 s apart (like the measured e2e) pay all three in sequence, plus the 10 s session-visibility check. That is Dev's n=6. ## Change - **The token row is read once.** The PAT check also selects `service_account_id`. `patPrincipal` stores the binding it just read, and `buildActor` uses it when the token id matches instead of reading the row again. Same row, same request, and fresher than the memo. This applies to every PAT request on every route, not only `/v1/p`. - **The sandbox row overlaps auth.** The `/v1/p` app starts the row read before `combinedAuth` (`sandbox-proxy/prefetch.ts`), and the route passes it to `forwardToSandbox` (`opts.record`, which existed for server-side delivery). - It runs only when the request presents a credential, so an anonymous probe costs nothing new. - The row is still read during the request and is never cached. Its status stays fresh, and it reaches nobody unless auth and the existing checks pass. - **The ownership check reuses that row.** `canAccessPreviewSandbox` takes the row the proxy already loaded instead of selecting it again, so a cold check is one round trip instead of two. ### Deliberately not cached - **Token validation** (`account_tokens`): revocation must apply on the very next request. A test revokes a token and asserts the next request gets 401. - **The sandbox row**: its status must be fresh. - **Session visibility (10 s)** and **ownership (5 min)**: TTLs unchanged. No verdict is shared across callers that it wasn't shared across before. - **The box hop** (308 ms EU, 122 ms US on Dev): geography, out of scope. ## Measured, same request on a real database (`integration-preview-hot-path-queries`) | `/v1/p` GET | before | after | |---|---|---| | warm | 3 statements, sequential | **2 statements, in flight together** | | cold (first per user+sandbox per process) | 17 statements | 15 (no token re-read, no sandbox re-read) | Expected on Dev: - calls more than 15 s apart: 4 sequential round trips → 2; - rapid calls: 2 → 1; - roughly −150 to −300 ms per call at Dev's ~130–160 ms per statement. Prod is colocated, so the absolute saving is smaller, but the depth halves. ## Verification - **New** `apps/api/src/__tests__/integration-preview-hot-path-queries.test.ts` (real Postgres, the real auth/IAM/ownership/visibility code, only the provider's address lookup faked). It asserts: - the statements on a cold and a warm request; - that the sandbox read and the token check are in flight together; - that an anonymous request reads no sandbox row; - that a revoked token is refused on its very next request. - **Mutation check:** with the product changes reverted, the cold and warm cases fail. - `integration-iam-build-actor`: 2 new cases. - A binding seeded the way `patPrincipal` stores it gives a credential deep-equal to the reloaded one for an agent-session token. - A binding for a different token is ignored. - **Real-database suites:** 10 related suites, 70 tests, all pass: preview access/authz, token revocation and scope, personal tokens, correlated-subquery isolation, heal-superseded-box-token, build-actor. - **Unit:** 46 related files (`sandbox-proxy`, `routes`, `middleware/auth*`, `iam`, `preview-ownership`, `account-tokens`), one process per file: 577 pass, 0 fail. - `apps/api` typecheck clean. Biome is clean on new files; the edited files keep their existing findings. --- Need help on this PR? Tag @codesmith-bot with what you need. Autofix is disabled.

fix(runtime): no relaunch on first open of a swapped template; direct regional creates (#8775) ## Problem Every session booted from an agent-swapped default template restarted its daemon about 10 s after it was ready. Measured on Dev on 2026-10-02 in both regions, with template `kortix-default-6bacca9b52cc` built in 3 s by the CAS agent-swap: | | US session `9f5886f4` | EU, fresh box | |---|---|---| | box started | 19:18:08.0 | 19:23:52 | | OpenCode ready, session pinned | 19:18:17.0 | 19:24:05 | | legacy-bootstrap fires: SIGTERM, relaunch | 19:18:26–29 | 19:24:22–26 | | ready again | 19:18:34 | 19:24:29 | That is about **17 s wasted per session**. The cause was captured from inside a fresh box (`curl localhost:8000/kortix/health` every 1.5 s from boot): - **On first boot,** `runtime.running` reported `agent_sha256 efd19aa3…` and `cli_sha256 9ba28976…`, with `build: null`. - **On disk,** `/usr/local/bin/kortix-agent` was already `d2019d30…`, the manifest's agent, with mtime 19:08:48 (the swap). - **The reported values were a bake record:** `running` is read verbatim from `/opt/kortix/runtime-assets-state.json`, which `bakeRuntimeAssetsState` wrote when the predecessor image was built. The swap patches only the binary and keeps that record. - **Session open misread it:** `guaranteeCurrentRuntimeOnOpen` compared the record to the manifest, classified the box `running_assets_stale`, and relaunched a daemon that already ran the right bytes. - **The daemon would have fixed itself:** its own boot pass, about 20 s after start, re-hashes the agent (reports `d2019d30`) and replaces the CLI in place (`cli: updated`) without any restart. A relaunch can't fix the CLI anyway. ## Change - **Daemon** (`runtime-assets-swap-report.ts`): `runtime.running` treats a stat-keyed digest (size + mtime) as a cache. When the file no longer matches, it hashes the file, memoised per file version. A missing file answers `null`, never the stale value. A state with no stat key is reported exactly as before. - **API** (`legacy-runtime-bootstrap.ts`): before the first convergence pass (`runtime.build` and `running.build` both null) and within `FIRST_CONVERGENCE_GRACE_S` (300 s) of boot, a digest mismatch alone is not `stale`. The box classifies `current` with `runtimeBuild: null`, which `bootstrapLegacyRuntime` already treats as "convergence pending" (it records no check, so the reaper keeps looking). - **Unchanged:** every other reason (`agentSwapPending`, missing capability, failed component, running unreported) still repairs during the grace. - **The window closes:** after the first pass, or after the grace, the same mismatch is stale again. A box whose first pass never completes therefore can't hide a genuinely stale agent. - **A genuinely stale agent** is staged by that boot pass, then reported as `agentSwapPending`, and repaired then. - **API** (`shared/platinum.ts`): a create naming a region this process has already seen a box in goes straight to that region's control plane, learned from that box's `api_url` / `x-pt-served-by`, with the same origin validation as #8740. Previously every US create was forwarded EU → US. A write is retried via the global origin only when the connection never opened. - **API** (`session-sandbox.ts`, `provision-timeline.ts`): `tl.note()` records the parallel image branch (`image:git-project`, `image:resolved`) and `network-boundary` without disturbing the main path's deltas, so the pre-create gap becomes attributable in `provisionTimeline`. - **Separate commit:** removes a duplicate `qualifiedColumn` import in `config-releases/quarantine.ts`. Two merges both added it, and current main fails the API typecheck with TS2300. ## The 8.4 s before the provider create, as far as it can be measured today US session `9f5886f4`: row at 19:17:57.9, provider create at 19:18:06.3. A fresh EU session's `provisionTimeline` broke down as follows: | step | time | |---|---| | `POST /sessions` | 4.4 s | | row + tokens | 1.0 s | | image resolution after that | 2.9 s (total ≈ 3.9 s, it starts in parallel) | | provider create | 3.7 s (Platinum itself took 1.8–2.5 s in the US/EU control-plane logs) | - **Not the template list:** Platinum's side is 15–35 ms per call (live control-plane log), and the listing query runs in about 2 ms. Only 1 template is newer than the default, so the name lookup is one page. - **The remaining image time is Kortix-side:** `resolveGitProject` plus `ensureSandboxImage` DB round trips. Dev's API (us-west-2) and database (us-east-2) are on different coasts. The new timeline notes will split it on the next run. - **Removed here:** the EU hop on US creates. ## Verification | Suite | Result | |---|---| | Daemon `runtime-assets`, `runtime-convergence`, `runtime-assets-boundary`, `runtime-assets-cli-replace` | 102 pass, 0 fail | | API, 23 files (`shared/platinum*`, `providers/platinum*`, `session-sandbox*`, `provision-timeline`, `legacy-runtime*`, `pinned-runtime-serves`, `config-releases/quarantine`) | 249 pass, 0 fail | | `tsc --noEmit` on `apps/api` and `apps/kortix-sandbox-agent-server` | clean | **New tests and mutation checks:** - **Daemon:** a binary replaced after the bake reports its real digest; a missing file reports `null`. On the old code: 2 fail. - **Classifier:** the captured first-boot payload is classified `current` / convergence pending. The same mismatch after a pass, after the grace, or with unknown uptime is stale. `agentSwapPending` and a missing capability still repair during the grace. With the rule disabled: 2 fail. - **Timeline:** a parallel `note()` never moves the sequential cursor. - **Origins:** - a regional create goes direct once the region has been learned, and no-region or unknown-region creates stay global; - a home-region box teaches nothing, and a foreign `api_url` is never used; - a connect-refused create retries once via global and forgets the region; - a reset mid-request is never re-sent. **Not verified:** a deployed before/after on Dev. This PR is not merged or deployed. The "after" is the captured Dev first-boot payload classified by the new code, plus the tests above. fix(files): upload sandbox files in 8 MiB requests, not 64 KiB round trips (1 MiB: 20 s → 2 s) (#8768) ## Problem A 1 MiB file upload through the SDK took **17–21 s** on Dev, in both regions. Any upload over 64 KiB was reserved, then appended in 64 KiB pieces. Each piece was one proxied round trip of about 0.9–1.3 s, so a 1 MiB file meant **17 sequential requests**. Prompt attachments written by the API (`runtime-prompt-file.ts`) used the same 64 KiB limit. That limit came from a 2026-09-04 measurement: back then the Platinum sandbox edge silently dropped request bodies over ~104 KB. Platinum has since fixed that: - platinum#923: drain the request body across backpressure, so large uploads aren't truncated. - platinum#1077: stream sandbox proxy and edge bodies, with bounded admission. The edge now accepts 128 MiB bodies. ## Evidence (2026-10-02, real Dev sessions, every byte SHA-256 verified) Single requests through the real route (Kortix API `/v1/p` → Platinum edge → daemon `/file/upload`): | body | eu-west | us-east | |---|---|---| | 1 MiB | 2.0 s ✅ | 1.5 s ✅ | | 4 MiB | 3.6 s ✅ | — | | 8 MiB | 3.6 s ✅ | 3.0 s ✅ | | 16 MiB | 6.6 s ✅ | 5.2 s ✅ | Same session, back to back, `main` SDK vs this branch's SDK (median of 3): | | eu-west | us-east | |---|---|---| | 1 MiB, main (64 KiB chunks) | **20.8 s** | **17.4 s** | | 1 MiB, this PR | **2.2 s** | **1.9 s** | | 4 MiB, this PR | 2.6 s | 2.7 s | | 20 MiB, this PR (reservation + 3 verified appends) | 10.3 s | 8.7 s | ## Change - `packages/sdk/src/core/files/client.ts`: the upload chunk goes from 64 KiB to **8 MiB**, a 2× margin under the largest body proven. The single-request path now checks the landed `size` and throws `UPLOAD_SIZE_MISMATCH` on a short body. The chunked path already checked every append. The constant stays internal; the public export surface is unchanged. - `apps/api/src/projects/session-lifecycle/runtime-prompt-file.ts`: the same 8 MiB chunk for prompt attachments. The whole-file path now checks the landed size, and on a mismatch it deletes the short temp file before failing, so a truncated attachment can never be renamed into place. ## Tests - SDK: the chunking test is reworked around the new size. New tests: - `a 1 MiB upload is a single request, not a chunk train` - `a single-request upload whose landed size disagrees fails instead of reporting success` - API: the append-path test now uses a file past the new chunk budget. New tests: - `a 1 MiB attachment is one upload, not a chain of appends` - `a whole-file upload that landed short fails and deletes its temp file` - Mutation check: putting back 64 KiB and removing the size checks makes the 2 new SDK tests and the 2 new API tests fail. - `packages/sdk`, run one file per process as the package script does: **4,871 pass, 0 fail**. SDK `tsc --noEmit` is clean. - `apps/api` `runtime-prompt-file.test.ts`: 17 pass, 0 fail. - `apps/api` `tsc`: the only 2 errors are in `src/channels/slack/session.ts`, from my local `node_modules` linked to an older checkout. They are unrelated to this change. ## Caveat The 8 MiB proof covers Platinum, the provider Dev and prod use. No Daytona or E2B body limit is documented in this repo. If a provider has a lower ceiling, the size checks above turn it into an explicit upload error instead of silent truncation. ## Separate finding, not in this PR Every `/v1/p` call costs ~0.9–1.3 s. Its `Server-Timing` shows **db ≈ 760–960 ms across 6 queries**, auth 180–350 ms, and only 120–310 ms for the hop to the box. On Dev the API runs in us-west-2 against a database in us-east-2, so each of those 6 sequential queries crosses the continent. That makes listFiles ~1 s per call, and it's what every chunk paid before this PR. --- Need help on this PR? Tag @codesmith-bot with what you need. Autofix is disabled.
