perf(api,sdk): R1 hot path: fewer statements, sleeps and git calls between a prompt and the harness (#8765)

## Summary

R1 (hot path) of the API + SDK refactor plan. It removes sequential
statements, a fixed sleep and git calls between a user action and the
harness. No route, response shape or product behavior changes, except 1
additive field (`capabilities` on the `/start` answer).

Measured with `apps/api/scripts/prompt-latency-bench.ts` on a local
stack with real Platinum sandboxes. 50 ms RTT to the database is the dev
condition. "Direct" is the prod condition (API and DB co-located).
Values are p50 in ms.

| Metric | Baseline, 50 ms | This PR, 50 ms | This PR + prepared, 50 ms
| Baseline, direct | This PR, direct |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `POST /sessions` wall | 1,833 | 818 | 593 | 911 | 66 |
| `POST /prompts` wall | 825 | 748 | 369 | 26 | 52 |
| prompt created → forwarded to the sandbox | 4,305 | 2,188 | 1,406 |
1,192 | 242 |
| POST → `busy` | 4,484 | 2,667 | 1,655 | 1,173 | 576 |
| POST → `idle` | 6,940 | 5,576 | 3,381 | 3,740 | 2,258 |

- Baseline = `main` at `39df4d0379`, measured the same day. 50 ms arms:
4 sessions, 12 turns each. Direct: 3 sessions, 9 turns (baseline direct:
1 session, 3 turns).
- "+ prepared" = `DB_PREPARE_STATEMENTS=true`. It is off by default (see
R1.2).
- `POST /prompts` direct reads 26 → 52 ms. Its `db` stage is 5 → 6 ms.
The difference is the local GoTrue call (19 → 34 ms), which this PR does
not touch.
- Full tables, stage rows and method:
`.agents/skills/testing/references/api-latency-baseline.md` → "After
R1".

One prompt, statement trace at 50 ms RTT:

- Request: 14 statements in 8 sequential waves → 15 in 6.
- Delivery: 49 statements in 27 waves and 2 git calls → 32 in 15 and no
git call. A prompt sent 70 s after the last one pays 1 `ls-remote`: 42
statements in 19 waves.

### What changed, per task

| Task | Change | Commit |
| --- | --- | --- |
| R1.1 | A mirror read with `forceRefresh: 'tip-proof'` is served when
its branch was proven at the remote tip within the 60 s refresh
interval. The per-prompt grant re-mint, the env sync, the connector-call
reconcile, session create and the fast-boot hint use it.
`invalidateProjectMirror` (already broadcast to every API process) drops
the proof. | `056290c1ff`, `8319d69ac4` |
| R1.2 | `DB_PREPARE_STATEMENTS=true` makes Drizzle statements prepared
statements: 1 round trip instead of 2 for a statement its connection has
seen. Off by default. | `e3799ebd85`, `85a17158c2` |
| R1.3 | `POST /prompts`: the session read, the inbox read and the
instance-scope read start together. The billing gate reads
`credit_accounts` once (it read it twice on every create, start, prompt
and LLM admission). | `fbc2109022`, `32986606b8` |
| R1.4 | The delivery claim is 1 statement (`FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED`).
The 250 ms burst wait runs only when a race is possible. | `32986606b8`
|
| R1.5 | The turn-ledger row is written in the authority statement, at
begin and at accept. | `2f8b6dfd94` |
| R1.6 | The delivery hands its sandbox row to the proxy. | `95c8626c6f`
|
| R1.7 | A delivered prompt is read back only when its body is 64 KB or
more. | `b1f4b374bf` |
| R1.8 | The env sync reads the session row, the project row, the agent
grant and the personal owner once for both of its legs. | `76f7d0a640` |
| R1.9 | Session create: 3 cap reads together. Provisioning: the env
build overlaps the image check and the token mint. `/start`: the
long-poll cap is 15 s (it was 8 s; the SDK asks for 15 s). First prompt:
the provision wakes the waiting delivery. | `8319d69ac4` |
| R1.10 | Single-flight on the sandbox ownership check, the
session-visibility check and the ingress resolve. Parallel reads on `GET
/projects`, `GET /projects/:id/sessions`, `GET /accounts`. |
`b509e88f44` |
| R1.11 | Tunnel RPC forwarder: NOTIFY wake + 1 s fallback (~1,140 → ~62
statements per minute per replica). 19 leader sweeps run 3 at a time. 1
partial index for the forwarded-prompt sweep. | `9cc8e02088` |
| R1.13 | SDK: an answered session-open snapshot serves the
saved-history read and seeds `model-defaults`. API: `/start` returns the
runtime `capabilities` with `stage: ready`, and `useSession` records
them. | `916fab4566` |
| R1.14 | SDK: consecutive text deltas of one part in one 16 ms flush
arrive as 1 event and 1 store update (200 → 1 in the test). |
`0f69acc91d` |

### Not done, and why

- **R1.12** (move the dev API to the region of its database):
infrastructure, no code. It needs a decision. Not applied.
- **R1.2 is not turned on anywhere.** The flag works (proven against
PostgreSQL). Turning it on needs a decision per environment: it requires
a direct or session-mode connection (dev is direct; staging and prod
were not read from this machine), and a generic plan cannot use a
partial index whose predicate arrives as a parameter.
- **R1.3 "4 waves or fewer"**: the request runs 6 waves, not 4. The 2
IAM waves and the agent-grant read are inside the IAM engine and
`resolveAndAuthorizeAgent`, which this PR does not restructure.
- **R1.5 "accept writes off the lane"**: the inbox confirmation after
accept stays awaited. Off the lane it races the row's close write, and a
lost race leaves the prompt listed as `delivering` until the turn ends.
- **R1.9**: the 2 SELECTs of each 200 ms `/start` tick stay separate (1
ms on a co-located database).
- **R1.11**: the orphan-box sweep gets no index. Its predicate matches
every row.
- **R1.13**: the first `/kortix/health` probe stays. It proves that the
browser reaches the box, which the API's own reach does not. A
saved-history read that starts in the same tick as the snapshot still
downloads the window (2 of the 3 history reads in the recorded session).
The "60 KB bundle" bullet is obsolete: `@opencode-ai/sdk` left the SDK
in W5.
- **R1.14**: `useSession` still subscribes to messages by default
(breaking change, next major).

### Behavior notes for review

- **R1.1 freshness.** A manifest change made through Kortix (API write,
git-proxy push, change-request merge) is read before the next turn, as
before. A push made directly on the upstream is read at most 60 s later.
That is the bound `DESIRED_TTL_MS` already gives the config release. The
same-blob tie-break read stays strict.
- **R1.4 ordering.** A send is claimed at once when no other prompt of
the session is queued or in delivery and its POST arrived within 1 s of
`client_sent_at_ms`. Every other send keeps the 250 ms wait: a sibling
exists, the POST waited on the client, or the caller sends no
`client_sent_at_ms`. Not covered: an older send whose POST lands within
250 ms after a newer, fresh one was claimed.
- **R1.11 rolling deploy.** A tunnel RPC forwarded between an old and a
new replica takes the fallback poll: at most +1 s on the pickup and +1 s
on the result.
- **`/start` contract.** `capabilities` is optional and additive. An old
SDK ignores it. A new SDK on an old API keeps the previous behavior.
- **Also in this PR:** `fix(config-releases)`: `main` is red on
`sql-correlated-subquery-guard.test.ts` since `b42ef6e976`. The fix
qualifies 1 column. The rendered SQL of both queries is unchanged.

feat(sessions): edit a queued prompt in place (#8753) ## Summary Editing a Queue List entry used to remove the row and send the edited text as a new prompt. A new prompt releases a Stop hold and is admitted immediately on an idle session, so saving an edit delivered the message. Opening the edit also waited for the `DELETE` round trip, a visible 1–2 s delay. This change edits the row in place. - **API** — `PATCH /v1/projects/:projectId/sessions/:sessionId/prompts/:promptId` with `{ text }` replaces the text of a `queued` / `failed` / `dead_lettered` row. The row keeps its position, file parts, wire message id and hold. No prompt is sent and no drain is triggered. Responses: `200` with the edited row; `409` when the prompt is already with the agent; `400` for empty text; `404` for a row outside the session. Audit label `session.prompt.edit`. - **SDK** — additive: `editSessionPrompt`, `session(...).prompts.edit`, and `useSessionPrompts().edit` with an optimistic text update. Public surface snapshots gain only `editSessionPrompt`. - **Web** - The pencil and the Up key open the edit synchronously; no request is made. - Submit saves into the same row. Only the visible words are replaced inside the stored text, so reply quotes and file references are preserved. - Cancel clears the composer; the row was never modified. - While an edit is open, a labeled **Submit** button replaces the Stop control. - The queue card renders the row being edited in its own slot. - Rows with attachments are now editable; their files stay on the row. - **Contract** — `tests/spec/end-to-end.md` (SESS-25) and the SESS-25 flow cover the new route; `routes.generated.json` regenerated. ## Test plan - [x] `pnpm --filter @kortix/sdk typecheck` — pass - [x] `pnpm --filter @kortix/sdk test` — 4870 pass, 0 fail (baseline 4867 + 3 new) - [x] `pnpm --filter @kortix/sdk run smoke:install` — pass - [x] `pnpm test -- --db-only integration-prompt-inbox` — 84 pass, including in-place edit, on-the-wire refusal and automation-row isolation against real Postgres - [x] `apps/api` route tests (`session-prompts.test.ts`) — 52 pass; audit-label and correlated-subquery guards pass - [x] `apps/web` session, composer and queue tests — 700 pass; `tsc` clean on touched files; `eslint` 0 errors; i18n catalog check passes - [x] HTTP against a local API with a held queued row: `PATCH` → `200`, row stays `waiting/held`; `GET` reads back the new text; stored row keeps status, file part, client id and wire id; empty text → `400`; unknown row → `404`; running row → `409` - [ ] Browser: queue two Queue List entries during a running turn, edit one, Submit — the row updates in place and nothing is sent; repeat after Stop - [ ] SESS-25 flow against a Daytona-backed stack --- Need help on this PR? perf(mobile): remove render and animation hot paths before store release (#8747) ## Summary This PR removes performance problems found in a code audit of `apps/mobile` before the App Store and Play Store submission. Each fix removes a cause of jank. The visible output does not change, unless this summary says so. **Thread** - The fresh-session hero (Skia shader and tilt sensor) used to stay mounted behind every thread at opacity 0. It now unmounts after its fade-out. - `interruptedIds`, the per-message sender, and the Stop and Edit handlers keep stable identities. Transcript rows no longer re-render on every 64 ms streaming tick or on every `useSession` render. - The queue poll keeps the previous array when the rows are unchanged. It polls every 3 s while prompts exist or the agent is busy, and every 15 s (`SESSION_PROMPTS_IDLE_POLL_MS`, the same value web uses) on an idle thread with an empty queue. - The composer height lives in a ref. The bottom spacer settles once per keyboard move, instead of re-rendering the page on every frame. **Streaming markdown** - New patch-package patch for `react-native-markdown-display@7.0.2`: node keys are now position-based (parent key, index, type) instead of a global counter. The growing last block updates in place instead of remounting about 15 times per second. - The reply keeps its key when streaming ends. `CommandOutputCard` gains a `chrome` prop, so slash-command replies also stay mounted. - Autolinking and block splitting process only the newly arrived text, with a bounded per-input prefix cache. Tests and fuzz runs show the output equals a full pass. - `MarkdownTextInput` is imported from its own module, so `expensify-common` is no longer in the bundle. **Composer and project home** - The composer sheets are memoized. - The project-home draft moved into a child component, so a keystroke no longer re-renders the Skia hero. - Each attachment tile subscribes to its own upload progress, and the composer subscribes only to status changes. **Navigation** - The `ProjectScreen` route context and the thread view are memoized, and `SessionPage` no longer receives `isDrawerOpen`. A drawer toggle no longer re-renders the open thread. - Drawer rows are memoized. The paged session hooks no longer re-render consumers on `isFetching` flips. - The Sessions page renders one list item per row. Sub-session trees cap at 5 rows behind "Show N more", and the open sub-session always stays visible. - `freezeOnBlur` is set on the root and project stacks. It freezes screens two or more levels below the top screen. **Sheets** - `SheetFill` lays out its height only at the mount target, on settle, or while the sheet grows past the laid-out height. - `PinnedBar` follows the visible edge with a `translateY` computed in the same frame. Both values are `useDerivedValue`s. - `SandboxPreviewSheet`, the HTML preview from a `show` row, turns off gorhom's content pan gesture. The page in its WebView now scrolls on Android. - The CSV preview puts its vertical scroll view outside the horizontal one, so vertical drags scroll on Android. - Image previews, and HTML previews on Android, now end above the pinned Download and Add bar. **Tool rows** - On Android, `TextShimmer` keeps the masked gradient sweep, the same as iOS. - Stale tools, and tools left running after their turn ended, draw as still text with no Lottie. - A sub-agent that is still working keeps its own live state. **App shell** - A same-user token refresh keeps the auth context value stable, and `session` is removed from the context. - Non-critical resume work (warm session, push re-registration, OTA check) starts 400–800 ms after the app returns to the foreground. - The disabled presence and agent providers are removed, along with the duplicate Web Crypto polyfill. **Dependencies and build** - Removed 11 unused dependencies and 10 dead files. - `react-native-drawer-layout` and `react-native-markdown-display` are pinned to their patch versions. - `postinstall` is now `patch-package`, without `|| true`. - Added `eas-build-post-install: patch-package`. The root `.npmrc` sets `ignore-scripts=true`, so EAS builds never ran `patch-package`, and store binaries shipped without the mobile patches. `lib/build-patches.test.ts` enforces this, and a learnings entry records it. **Visible changes** - Sub-session trees show at most 5 rows behind "Show N more". The label is translated into all 8 locales. - On an idle thread with an empty queue, a prompt queued from another device can take up to 15 s to appear, instead of 3 s. - While a sheet moves, centered loading and error states stay fixed to the sheet top, instead of drifting at half speed. ## Test plan - [x] `cd apps/mobile && bun test --isolate`: 2741 pass, 1 fail. Before: 2553 pass, 2 fail. The remaining failure, `only the shared module mocks AsyncStorage`, also fails on `main`. - [x] `cd apps/mobile && npx tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.json`: 5 errors, all pre-existing in non-test files, and 0 TS2304. Before: 21 errors. - [x] `npx expo export --platform ios` and `--platform android` both exit 0. The bundle has no `expensify-common` modules. - [x] `pnpm run eas-build-post-install` with `ignore-scripts=true` applies all 4 patches. - [x] New tests fail on the old code and pass on the new code: - render counts: composer sheets, project home, drawer, `SessionPage`; - markdown key stability and reply mount across the streaming-to-finished switch; - incremental autolink and split equivalence; - file-search equivalence on 5,008 paths; - sheet bar same-frame delivery in a model of the Reanimated mapper registry; - token-refresh render count; - resume-delay cancellation; - the build-patches gate. - [ ] Next EAS build log, iOS and Android: the post-install hook prints a ✔ line for each of the 4 patches. - [ ] Native iOS and Android builds compile and launch with the 11 packages removed. - [ ] Device, iOS and Android: - stream a long reply with an image: no flash, no height jump; - finish a reply and a slash-command reply: no flash; - open, close and drag the keyboard in a long thread and a short thread: the transcript end stays pinned; - open, drag, snap, close and raise the keyboard on the Files sheet, the project switcher, the activity sheet, the tabbed model picker, a searchable picker, Schedules, `FilePreviewSheet` and `SessionFilesSheet`: the bottom bar stays on the visible edge; - toggle the drawer over a long thread: no lag. Open a session's 7th sub-session, then open the drawer: that row is highlighted; - open an HTML file from a `show` row and scroll the page. Open a CSV and swipe down at a slight angle: both scroll; - type on project home and in a thread, and while 5 photos upload: no lag, and progress, Retry and Remove still work; - Android turn with 5 parallel tools: running rows sweep. After Stop, no row in history animates; - during a running reply, open account → Billing → Plans and return: the thread shows the full reply; - resume after more than 1 h in the background: no stall, and sending works. --- Need help on this PR? fix(config-releases): the meta coordinator runs its own governance-only release (#8745) ## Summary Prod incident, 2026-10-02, one internal project with `config_releases` and `meta_agent` on. **Symptom.** A meta coordinator session shows "Config failed to load": `tools failed to load: HTTP 500 UnknownError … (tool files: …)`. **Cause.** `releaseVariantFor` gave a meta session the `project` variant, because its session metadata reads `repository_access: true`. That release is the full project config dir. The meta box holds no checkout (`KORTIX_PROJECT_AUTO_CLONE=0`), and the meta image (`meta-dockerfile.ts`) has no `bun` and no baked `opencode-config-deps`. The daemon logs `ensureOpencodeConfigDeps failed … Executable not found in $PATH: "bun"`, the release dir gets no `node_modules`, every tool that imports a package throws at import, and the proven check declines the release. **Wider impact.** The quarantine ledger is keyed by release ID and shared by every session of the project. Two failing meta sessions quarantined each release in turn (`PROJECT_QUARANTINE_SESSIONS = 2`). fix(dev): build the next default image and make it resident in US before the roll (#8743)

## Summary

Deploy Dev now builds the Platinum platform default image of the new API
version and makes it resident in the US region **before** the ECS roll.
Sessions in both regions then boot the exact image of the version
serving them: no last-ready fallback, no in-place runtime repair, no
EU-to-US copy on a US create. The gate never blocks the roll. Supersedes
the release-gate portion of #8695.

### Problem

On Dev, a new API version starts before the Platinum platform default
image it computes exists. The gap shows in both regions:

- **EU and US:** for the first minutes of every Dev deploy, sessions
boot the PREVIOUS default image (the last-ready fallback in
`ensureSandboxImage`). The daemon then repairs its runtime in place. On
a measured US session (2026-10-02) the legacy runtime bootstrap
restarted the daemon about 18 s after it was ready, because the agent
download failed.
- **US only:** the first US session after each new image waits while
Platinum copies the image from the EU bucket. Its create answered `409
template_not_resident` 28 times over 150 s. Dev copies on 2026-10-01/02
took 150–255 s and moved 2.2–4.1 GB each. dev.kortix.com builds a new
default image several times a day.

### Change


A release gate in `deploy-dev.yml` (`deploy-api-ecs`) runs **before**
the ECS roll:

1. **Same environment as the roll.** `infra/scripts/ecs-deploy.sh
--dry-run` writes the container environment it would register (running
revision + `KORTIX_ECS_ENV_OVERRIDES` + version stamp) to
`ECS_DEPLOY_RENDERED_ENV_FILE`. The gate runs the new API image with
exactly that environment plus the secret document as `KORTIX_ENV_JSON`,
as ECS passes it. The image identity depends on the environment
(`snapshotEmbedsAgentForBootMode` reads `config`), and `ecs-deploy.sh`
keeps every key the running revision carries. So only the real renderer
reproduces it; blob + overrides alone does not.
2. **Build unpublished.**
`apps/api/scripts/prepare-platform-default-image.ts` calls
`buildPlatformDefaultImageForRelease('platinum')`. That is
`ensureSandboxImage(…, { publish: false })`: the provider holds the
exact identity, and nothing else changes. The template row is not
repointed, the predecessor is not pruned, and a build failure does not
mark the row `error`.
3. **US residency.** With `KORTIX_PLATINUM_US_REGION` set, it calls
`POST /v1/templates/:id/prepare` (Platinum #1381, live on Platinum prod)
via `preparePlatinumTemplateRegion`, until HTTP `200` `ready`/`ready`
for the exact template id and region. The deadline is 12 minutes.

After the roll, the new version's first session (or its leader's startup
pre-build) finds the image active and publishes it, as it does after its
own build today.

**Never blocks the roll.** The step uses `continue-on-error: true` and
`timeout-minutes: 25`. I chose `continue-on-error` over exit-0-in-script
because it covers every failure in one place: secret read, image pull,
build, copy, runner timeout. The script still exits 1 with a
`::warning::` naming the cause, so a failed gate is visible. A failure
leaves the deploy exactly as it behaves today.

### Why the gate must not publish

`recordTemplateBuilt` reaps the snapshot a row stopped pointing at as
soon as it repoints (`reapPredecessorSnapshot`,
`KORTIX_SNAPSHOT_REAP_PREDECESSOR` defaults to true). Skipping only the
`runInlineBuild` prune would still delete the image the serving version
boots.

The gate runs while the old tasks serve 100% of traffic, for the build
plus the copy (several minutes). Publishing then would make the old
tasks:
- miss their own image;
- boot the new one through the last-ready fallback;
- kick a background rebuild of their own identity, which on completion
repoints the row back and reaps the new image.

That is the mutual-destruction loop the predecessor guard in
`runInlineBuild` describes, and it would also discard the US residency
just prepared.

**Publication timing after the roll.** Startup pre-build runs only on
the elected leader (`startSingletonWorkers`), so new tasks do not
publish at boot while old tasks still serve. Publication happens at the
first new-task session, after ALB health. Today it happens after the new
tasks' own build. The repoint and reap therefore move earlier by the
build time.

**Residual risk, unchanged in kind.** The old leader's singleton workers
keep running through the 300 s deregistration delay. A session they
start after the repoint takes the existing fallback path. That window
exists today; it grows by at most the build duration.

## Deliberately not taken from #8695

This PR supersedes the release-gate portion of #8695.

- **The `builder.ts` publication refactor.** It put US preparation on
the publish path of the shared default for every session. A slow or
failed US copy would have held back new images for EU sessions too: an
EU dependency on the US, and a stale image means the in-place runtime
repair. The session path here is unchanged.
- **Deleted guard tests** (`unit-no-top-level-await`,
`unit-worker-scope-wiring`, `relay-transport`, `token-hash`). Not needed
by this change; the coverage stays.
- **SDK saved-transcript / `use-session` first-paint change, i18n and
mermaid edits.** Unrelated to the gate.
- **Its prepare client's state/status pairing.** It accepted only
`absent/queued`, `replicating/copying`, `failed/cooling_down`. The
control plane that runs a copy answers `replicating/queued` until the
copy finishes (`requestResidency` returns `queued` while its key is
pending), and a requeued failure answers `failed/queued`. That client
would have failed the gate on the normal in-progress reply. Here, any
`202` with state ∈ {absent, replicating, failed} and status ∈ {queued,
copying, cooling_down} polls. Only `200` `ready`/`ready` passes.
- **Explicit `KORTIX_SNAPSHOT_*_PATH` values.** The rendered task
environment is used as-is, so the gate cannot diverge from the rolled
tasks.

fix(platinum): send a sandbox's calls to its own regional control plane (#8740) ## Summary **Problem.** Every Platinum call about a US sandbox went the long way. `PLATINUM_API_URL` (api.platinum.dev) lands on Platinum's home (EU) control plane. A regional sandbox row lives only in its own region's database, so for each call the EU control plane first sends an authenticated discovery GET to the US control plane and then forwards the real request. That is two transatlantic hops per call, on every status poll, expose, exec, start and stop of a `us_region` session. Measured on prod, 2026-10-02: - **One US session box, 70 s of startup:** the EU control plane received 35 Kortix calls; the US control plane received 70 (each call = discovery GET + forwarded request). - **`GET /v1/sandboxes/` from a New York client:** 329 ms median via api.platinum.dev vs 26 ms direct to `https://us-east.api.platinum.dev`. - **Same GET from an Amsterdam client:** 243 ms vs 108 ms. **Change.** Platinum already names each box's owner: `x-pt-served-by` on every forwarded response, and `api_url` in a sandbox body (`https://us-east.api.platinum.dev` for a US box, `https://api.platinum.dev` for an EU one). `shared/platinum.ts` now learns that owner per sandbox id and sends later calls for that id straight there. - **No extra calls:** the owner is learned from responses Kortix already receives. The first call per box per process takes the old path; a create's answer teaches the new box's owner immediately. - **Every per-sandbox path is covered:** routing applies inside the transport to any `/v1/sandboxes/…` path, so call sites in `platform/providers/platinum.ts` need no changes. - **Global origin unchanged:** create, list and template calls still go to `PLATINUM_API_URL`. Templates are global, and a regional create is already forwarded. - **Key safety:** the Bearer key goes only to the configured origin, or to an https, default-port subdomain of its host with no credentials, path or query. `https://api.platinum.dev.evil.com`, `http://us-east…`, `…:8443`, userinfo and path forms are all refused. - **Failure handling:** a learned origin that cannot be reached is forgotten, and the call goes once via the global origin. A read retries after any network failure. A write retries only when the connection never opened (refused, DNS, TLS), so a reset after send cannot run an exec or stop twice. Timeouts and aborts are not retried, and their messages are unchanged. - **Cache bounds:** the map is bounded at 10k ids, oldest first. - **Single-region deployments** (e.g. Platinum dev, where `api_url` equals the base) behave exactly as before. - **Comments:** the `platinum-region.ts` and `api_url` comments described the old one-origin design and are updated. ## Demo video No UI surface: the change is the API's outbound route to Platinum. Proof below is the shipped `shared/platinum.ts` run read-only (GETs only) against prod Platinum from a New York host: ``` US box call 1: https://api.platinum.dev 649 ms region=us-east (cold TLS; learns owner) US box call 2: https://us-east.api.platinum.dev 67 ms region=us-east US box call 3: https://us-east.api.platinum.dev 44 ms region=us-east US box call 4: https://us-east.api.platinum.dev 30 ms region=us-east US box call 5: https://us-east.api.platinum.dev 34 ms region=us-east US box call 6: https://us-east.api.platinum.dev 24 ms region=us-east EU box call 1: https://api.platinum.dev 380 ms region=eu-west EU box call 2: https://api.platinum.dev 114 ms region=eu-west (EU box stays on the global origin) ``` ## Type of change - [x] Bug fix - [ ] New feature - [ ] Refactor / chore - [ ] Docs / skills - [ ] Infrastructure / CI - [ ] Security fix - [ ] Breaking change ## How was this tested? perf(mobile): stop the waking-session freeze, cut re-renders, render markdown images (#8468)

## Summary
- **Project home stops re-rendering on every ProjectScreen render.**
`homeContent` is memoized and `ProjectHome` gets a ref-stable submit, so
opening the drawer or a poll result no longer re-renders home and its
logo.
- **The "Thinking…" glyph animates on the UI thread.**
`SessionDotMatrix` reads a per-variant frame table (cached once per
variant) from a `useFrameCallback`; the JS thread does no per-frame
work. Verified animating under Hermes on the Android emulator.
- **The drawer is idle while closed and refetches once per open.** The
"mine" list polls only while the drawer is open; the open-time refetch
no longer re-arms on every render (it looped every ~0.5 s while open).
- **The other shared markdown regexes are Hermes-safe.** Markdown-link
and angle-link protected ranges are index scans (same ranges); the
setup-link label is bounded. Hermes on 50k-char adversarial inputs:
0.4–5.8 s → 3–20 ms.
- **The app no longer freezes on a waking session.** The URL
autolinker's bare-domain label
(`packages/shared/src/utils/url-autolink.ts`) let Hermes backtrack
through every split of a run: 19.8 s, then `RangeError: Maximum regex
stack depth reached`, on one ordinary 3.8k-character reply. The
saved-copy view renders every saved text part at once, so the menu
button and drawer links did nothing. The label now parses one way; a
label ending in `-` is rejected after the match. Hermes, same 21 fixture
parts: over 20 s plus a crash before, 39 ms after. Web (V8) never showed
it.
- **The session actions sheet re-renders on list data only.** It bumped
on every project-sessions cache event, including events fired during
other components' render ("Cannot update a component while rendering a
different component").
- **Waking and failed session views are cleaner.** A failure (stopped,
failed to start, runtime not ready, timeout) is one card with the
composer's surface: title and message, then Back to project (secondary)
and Restart session (default) side by side. With no messages it is
centred and no composer shows; over a saved copy it takes the composer's
slot. Restart shows the session's dot-matrix glyph while it runs. While
the computer wakes, the status is a card above a disabled composer
("Waking this session's computer. You can send messages when it's
ready."); the half-working waking composer and its unused queue path are
removed.
- **Sheets and the file viewer close the keyboard.** A sheet opened from
a focused field kept the keyboard up over its lower half.
`KortixBottomSheetModal`'s `present()` now calls `Keyboard.dismiss()`
first, and `FileViewer` does the same when it becomes visible. Six call
sites no longer dismiss by hand.
- **A send in a thread keeps the keyboard up.** `SessionChatInput` no
longer calls `Keyboard.dismiss()` on send.
- **A question from the agent no longer moves the keyboard.**
`SessionPage` swaps the composer for the question card and back. The new
field takes the focus only when the keyboard was up at the swap.
`QuestionPrompt` has no auto-focus of its own, and its return key sends
without a blur.
- **An alert dialog and a long-press menu close the keyboard.**
`AlertDialogOverlay` and `ContextMenu` do it when they open.
- **iOS drag-to-dismiss starts at the composer.** The thread list sits
in `KeyboardGestureArea` with the composer's height as `offset`. Android
keeps `keyboardDismissMode="on-drag"`.
- **The iOS keyboard's glass shows the thread.** The iOS 26 keyboard is
Liquid Glass and shows the content under it. The thread ended at the top
of the keyboard, so only the flat page lay under it and it read as a
solid panel. On iOS the list now draws past its bottom edge (`overflow:
'visible'`). Later rows draw under the composer block, which is now
opaque, and under the keyboard. Layout and scroll geometry do not
change.
- **Markdown images render.** Agent replies and project files show the
image, not a name card, in web's frame (`RADIUS.lg`, 1pt outline). Two
or more images in a row become one horizontal pager that snaps per
image, with a "2 / 5" counter (`groupImageBlocks`,
`components/markdown/markdown-image.tsx`). Sandbox paths load through
`useSandboxImage`; remote http(s) images load only where the agent wrote
the text (`remoteImages="load"`, web's `markdownPolicy('agent')`); tool
output and `data:` keep the placeholder card.
- **An image tap asks first.** A remote image opens a confirm ("Open
image in browser?", the host named) before `openLink`. A sandbox image
opens in the in-app file preview.
- **The confirm dialog's Cancel is the secondary pill.**
`AlertDialogCancel asChild` merged its outline classes over `secondary`;
Cancel is now a plain `Button`. Gaps: buttons 12pt, text to buttons
24pt; top and bottom padding read the same.
- **No require cycle from markdown to the preview sheet.** The file
preview store moves to `stores/tool-file-preview-store.ts`;

- `apps/mobile/design.md` has the rules in one "Keyboard" row.
`apps/mobile/AGENTS.md` has the sheet rule.

Not changed:

closes for that send.

- The thread list still moves to the end from JS when the keyboard

feat: OpenCode decoupling W7 — Kortix tools on pi, system skills and docs describe both harnesses (#8714) ## Summary Wave 7 of the OpenCode decoupling plan: the five tasks of "pi by default" (B10, G4, G1, G2, G3). This PR does **not** change the default harness. See "The default flip" below. **B10. Kortix tools on pi.** A pi session had `glob`, `grep` and `question` beside pi's own four tools. The five Kortix tools existed only as OpenCode files in the starter template, and 6 marketplace skill files name them 38 times. - pi now has `web_search` (Tavily), `image_search` (Serper), `scrape_webpage` (Firecrawl), `memory` and `show`, compiled into kortixd (`harness/pi/kortix-web-tools.ts`, `kortix-memory-tool.ts`, `kortix-show-tool.ts`). Names, arguments and output JSON equal the OpenCode template tools, so skills and the client tool views work unchanged. - Decision taken (the plan's recommendation): compiled into the daemon, not project files. No existing project has a `harnesses/pi/` directory. - The web tools call the API's billed router proxy (`/v1/router/{tavily,serper,firecrawl}`) with the sandbox token. A box with no control plane calls the upstream with the project's own key. - Permissions: `web_search` and `image_search` follow `websearch`, `scrape_webpage` follows `webfetch`. A `memory` command that changes a file follows `edit`, and `view` follows `read`, so an `edit: deny` agent cannot write through `memory`. pi asks for these tools like any other tool. A rule under the tool's own name wins. - The root agent and subagents get the tools. The read-only `explore` subagent does not. **G4. System skills describe pi.** - Step 1: OpenCode's built-in `customize-opencode` skill (compiled into the OpenCode binary; it teaches `.opencode/`, `~/.config/opencode/` and "quit and restart opencode") is denied in every Kortix session. `denyBuiltinSkills` adds the rule to the composed config's global permission block and to every compiled agent block, as the last `skill` rule. It compares the **raw HTML length, markup included** (`Mail::SpamAssassin::HTML::parse` adds `length($text)`), even though the rule description says "bytes of words". The shell renders every email at 2,253–2,795 bytes, and the brand requires the hosted logo ``. So every invite fell into a penalized window. The dev seed test scored 8.9/10: - −0.6 for this rule; - −0.5 for a dev-only "broken link": dev web returns `401` behind Basic auth. Prod invite links return `307` to sign-in. The invite also broke brand voice 5.5: - it had no closing note on what to do when the reader did not expect it; - its role chip was uppercase (`MEMBER`); - with no inviter email (a token-authenticated request), it said "You've been invited" and named no one. ### Change - `apps/api/src/accounts/email.ts` (invite): - The lead names the inviter. With no inviter email, it names the account. - The chip and the plain-text line are sentence case ("Member"). - One closing note names the invited address: "This invitation is for {email}. Sign in with that address, or sign up with it if you don't have a Kortix account yet — … If you were not expecting this invitation, you can ignore this email." Accepting requires that address (`email_matches_caller`). Before, the email never said which one, so a reader who signed in with a different address could not accept. - `apps/api/src/lib/email/template.ts` (the shell for every email). It gains standard email markup it lacked: - `lang="en"`; - light-only `color-scheme` metas (brand decision Q34: email ships light only); - `x-apple-disable-message-reformatting`; - `format-detection`, so iOS Mail does not turn the address in the note into a blue link; - an Outlook (`mso`) width wrapper; - a `width` on the logo (110 px for the 2001×399 PNG at 22 px high), which Outlook desktop needs. Depend on brotli so Hub downloads do not fail on brotlicffi

huggingface_hub downloads over httpx, which advertises Brotli to the Hub
whenever a Brotli package is importable. Its fallback backend, brotlicffi,
raises mid-stream on some CDN responses --

    brotli: decoder process called with data when 'can_accept_more_data()' is False

-- which httpx re-raises as DecodingError and snapshot_download reports as a
failed file. httpx prefers the C bindings over brotlicffi, so depending on them
keeps that path out of reach even when brotlicffi is already installed.

setup.py's version was still 0.9.1; pyproject's [project] table shadows it, but
a stale number there is a trap.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

Add KittenTTS 2 and rename the package to kittenml

KittenTTS 2 is a 1.7B speech language model: it reads text and writes S3 codec
tokens, which the s3gen vocoder turns into 24 kHz audio. Voice identity comes
from a speaker embedding projected into the first position's hidden state, plus
the reference clip's own codec tokens in the prompt, so cloning needs no
training. 47 built-in voices, nine of them reaching other languages, and
expression markup for emotions, vocal events and emphasis.

`import kittenml` now, and `KittenTTS(...)` reads the repository's config.json
and builds whichever backend it names. The ONNX models move to
kittenml.kittentts_legacy and keep working unchanged; neither backend is
imported until it is selected, so a KittenTTS 2 install never needs espeak and
an ONNX install never needs torch.

The language model's linear weights are ternary, so bf16 spends 16 bits to say
one of three things. ternary.py packs them five trits to a byte, losslessly,
taking the checkpoint from 3.47 GB to 954 MB; tl2_emb4.py reads a 469 MB variant
that also quantises the token embedding to 4 bits, the one lossy option here.
The flow decoder can likewise be swapped for a 39 MB distilled student.

s3gen and the student flow are vendored into one file each, generated from the
upstream checkouts by internal tooling and verified bit-identical.

Examples are now about KittenTTS 2, with example_onnx_0.8.py for the old models,
and docs/ carries the longer explanations.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

Studio: renew the chat-run lease while long prefill is still advancing (#12523)

* Studio: renew the chat-run lease while long prefill is still advancing

Dropped prompt_progress was replaced with : keep-alive, which the durable
lease deliberately ignores, so a healthy multi-minute prefill was reaped as
"Generation stopped making progress" (unslothai#12518). Stand in with
: prefill-progress and renew on it, same pattern as : tool-heartbeat.

* [pre-commit.ci] auto fixes from pre-commit.com hooks

for more information, see https://pre-commit.ci

* Studio: renew the lease from native GGUF prefill too

The Studio UI never sends client tools, so its GGUF chat and tool loop run
the native generators rather than the passthrough. Those consume
prompt_progress themselves and stay silent until the first token, so the
stall loop only ever sent ": keep-alive" and a long prefill was still
reaped after the lease ran out.

Wrap the GGUF perf callback in a small signal that counts moving
prompt_progress, and have both native stall loops send ": prefill-progress"
when it moved since the last tick. A generator that reports nothing still
gets ": keep-alive" and is still reaped. The wrapper opts out of per-token
timings unless a monitor is attached, and non-streaming requests keep the
plain monitor callback.

Count only the lock's own waits in the unlockable-filesystem row (#12529)

The row patches time.sleep process-wide to prove _optional_top_up_lock does
not retry a mount that cannot lock. The lock waits on the calling thread,
but a background thread left by an earlier test in the same worker that
sleeps 50 ms during the window lands in the same list, and the row fails
with "waited on a filesystem that cannot lock: [0.05]" for a wait the lock
never made. Record sleeps from the test's thread only, hand other threads
the real sleep so they keep their pacing, and print what was recorded.

Studio: move torchao int8 weights back to the GPU after an oversized request streams pinned groups (#12526)

* Studio: restore pinned torchao groups by their inner tensors

After an oversized request streams the pinned denoiser groups, restoring them
skipped every tensor whose wrapper already reported the onload device. A torchao
int8 weight can report cuda after a streamed offload while its int8 data and
scales sit on the host, so the restore left them there and the next request
failed with a device mismatch (Qwen-Image-2.1 int8 at 12 or 16 GB, a 2400x1792
render followed by a 1024 render).

_placed_on() judges a torchao subclass by its flattened inner tensors; plain
tensors keep the device check.

attention mask, so the padding changes the embeddings and adds 256 joint
attention tokens per step. ComfyUI pads to 256 and otherwise keeps the real
length. Pass max_sequence_length = clamp(T5 length incl. EOS, 256, 512) per

diffusers enables Qwen-Image true CFG only when a negative prompt is passed,
and Studio sends none when the box is blank, so the default guidance 4 never
applied CFG. ComfyUI encodes an empty negative and applies CFG. For
true_cfg_scale families with guidance above 1 and no negative, pass an empty
negative; an explicit negative and guidance <= 1 are unchanged.

the same checkpoint: FLUX.1 dev / Kontext / Krea dev 20 steps (Krea dev at the

Qwen-Image-2.1 25, Qwen-Image-Edit 2511 40 at 4, Qwen-Image-2512 50 at 4,

ComfyUI cfg - 1), SDXL 25. Backend and UI tables stay in sync; explicit
request values are untouched.

ComfyUI's Ideogram 4 template samples 20 steps at constant guidance 7 with
the logit-normal schedule at mu 0.5 / std 1.75. Default to 20 / 7 and pass
those schedule parameters whenever guidance is constant; an explicit 48
steps at 7 still runs the card's tapered schedule with the pipeline's own
mu / std.

ComfyUI's official templates sample Wan2.2-TI2V-5B at 20 steps / CFG 5,
Wan2.2-T2V-A14B at 20 steps / CFG 3.5 (Lightning LoRA off) and
HunyuanVideo-1.5 at 20 steps / CFG 6, against Studio's 50-step defaults.
Match them in the family defaults, the per-variant table (A14B now has its
own key ahead of the generic Wan one) and the UI table. Explicit values are
unchanged.

The shipped schedulers shift sigmas differently from ComfyUI's defaults for

shift (about 2.0 at 1024 px) with a 0.02 terminal stretch against a constant

3.0 against 8 / 5, HunyuanVideo-1.5 480p / 720p ship 5.0 / 9.0 against 7.

the old behaviour: two shapes per resolution. This deviates from ComfyUI's

Parity: keep the reap-margin check off the edge of its own window (#12514)

The row sleeps the first child for 3000 ms of a 2 x 4000 ms deadline and
asserts the CUDA-only child's bound lands in [2000, 3000] ms. The expected
value is 3000 minus the few ms spent around the sleep, which sits on the
window's upper edge, so a Start-Sleep that wakes one timer tick early on
Windows answers 3001 and fails a run that computed the bound correctly.
Sleep 3200 ms instead, so the expected bound is about 2800 ms with margin
on both sides, and print the bound in the row's name so the next failure
says what it saw.

* Stop a Windows host-RAM spill from looking like a healthy load

On Windows, cudaMalloc does not allocate device memory directly. It asks the
WDDM kernel memory manager, which treats VRAM and system RAM as one demand
paged pool, and since driver 536.40 an allocation past the end of VRAM
succeeds out of host RAM instead of returning out of memory. The load starts,
exits 0, answers /health, and nvidia-smi shows a healthy card, while decode
re-reads the spilled bytes over PCIe on every token.

Linux has no such path. The same allocation fails with "cudaMalloc failed:
out of memory" and llama-server exits, which is measurable: with 12 GiB free,
Qwen3-VL-8B at -c 65536 asks for 9216.00 MiB in one allocation and refuses to
start. That is why every rung of the spawn loop's recovery ladder is gated on
a non-zero exit code, and why the whole ladder is dead on the one platform
that needs it.

Three changes:

Raise the per-device reserve to 1024 MiB on Windows with a discrete CUDA
build, capped at an eighth of the card so it stays proportionate on small
GPUs. This is not a new magic number, it is the per-device margin llama.cpp's
own fitter keeps when nobody tells it otherwise, and where our estimate
carries all the risk we should be at least as conservative as the child would
have been. Linux and macOS budgets are unchanged, and the monotonicity
property in _vram_reserve_floor_mib still holds at every fraction.

After a full GPU pin comes up healthy, check that the load is actually
resident. Windows exposes the spilled bytes itself through the
'\GPU Adapter Memory(*)\Shared Usage' counter behind Task Manager's shared
memory figure, which nvidia-smi cannot see because on WDDM it reports
dedicated VRAM only. That counter is per adapter rather than per process, so
it is believed only when the device side independently shows the child short
of the weights plus KV cache that full offload must place on the card. Report
only, no recovery.

Warn when a hand-set context does not fit. The planner already prices this
correctly and already hands the load to --fit, but said nothing about why the
context was flexed. The notice also re-prices at q8_0 and mentions it when
that would make the configuration fit, rather than changing a user's cache
dtype for them.

Make RMSNorm, RoPE and the input-embedding hook traceable by torch.compile (#12171)

* Make fast_rms_layernorm and fast_rope_embedding traceable by torch.compile

Under torch.compile both now go through torch.library.triton_op ops (same Triton kernels, fresh
outputs, register_autograd) instead of a compiler.disable graph break. The eager autograd
Functions are unchanged; torch without triton_op and non-CUDA devices keep the old graph break.

* Tests: fast_rms_layernorm and fast_rope_embedding under torch.compile

Compiled (fullgraph=True) vs eager forward and backward as bytes for RMSNorm (Llama and Gemma,
fp16 / bf16 / fp32, strided input) and RoPE (positions and rope indices, GQA, Q / K laid out as
in the attention forward), 0 graph breaks, the eager path still being the autograd Functions, and
a LoRA Llama whose decoder layers compile with fullgraph=True inside Unsloth checkpointing.

* RoPE: SymInt-safe group count, contiguous eager backward gradient

The head-group count used divmod, which a SymInt rejects under torch.compile(dynamic=True). The
eager Fast_RoPE_Embedding backward rotated its gradient in place through a stride 0 view when it
arrived expanded (e.g. from Q.sum()), giving wrong dQ / dK; it is made contiguous first (a no-op
for the dense gradients attention produces). Tests for both, the compiled route rotates copies
only, formatting.

* Remove the input-embedding hook and return_dict graph breaks

enable_input_require_grads makes the frozen embedding output require grad with
output.requires_grad_(True), which torch.compile cannot trace. While compiling, the hook now
returns x + -0.0 through a small autograd Function whose anchor requires grad: the same values
(signed zeros included) and the same requires_grad, with no graph break. Eager keeps the in-place
flag. Both the transformers 5 hook loop and the older single-embedding variant are patched.

The forward passes read config.use_return_dict, deprecated in transformers 5 behind a
logger.warning_once that breaks fullgraph compiles; config_return_dict reads return_dict (and
keeps the torchscript tuple rule of transformers 4).

With both, the causal LM forward (embedding, decoder stack, loss) of a LoRA Llama without
gradient checkpointing compiles with fullgraph=True.

* RMSNorm, RoPE: key the torch.compile cache on the kernel source

Inductor's FX graph cache keys a torch.library.triton_op call without the
Triton source behind it, so with a warm cache an edited kernel is served as
the previous kernel's compiled code. Unsloth turns the FX graph cache on, so
an upgrade could keep running an older kernel under torch.compile. Add a hash
of each kernel file to torch.compiler.config.cache_key_tag.

* fast_lora: keep the LoRA Functions opaque to torch.compile before torch 2.11

With RMSNorm and RoPE traceable, a whole causal LM compile on torch 2.7 traces
more of the fast_lora autograd Functions, and Inductor before 2.11 miscompiles
their backward (18 of 28 LoRA gradients differed from eager on a tiny Llama, 4
of 28 already on main). Same guard as the NF4 kernels PR, so the two merge
cleanly in either order. The decoder and causal LM tests now compare every
LoRA gradient with eager on every torch version.

* enable_input_require_grads patch: keep transformers' source visible

Wrap both replacements with functools.wraps so inspect.getsource still returns
transformers' implementation. On transformers 4.57.6 the single-embedding
variant is now patched too, and unsloth-zoo's upstream drift check

* RMSNorm, RoPE: keep bf16 untraced on GPUs without native bf16

* Route 4bit dequant and gemv through traceable NF4 ops on the live stream

fast_dequantize and fast_gemv call a dequantize_nf4 / gemv_nf4 contract
registered as torch.library ops, so matmul_lora and the fast_lora autograd
functions compile with fullgraph=True and no graph breaks. The ctypes
fallback (UNSLOTH_BNB_TRITON=0) reads the live stream instead of the
import-time snapshot, the global buffer is kept per stream and skipped
while compiling or capturing a CUDA graph, and FP4 states use their own
codebook. nf4.py and nf4_gemv.py are bitsandbytes-backed stand-ins for the
fused kernels.

* Use fused Triton NF4 dequant and GEMV kernels behind the traceable ops

Replace the bitsandbytes-backed stand-ins with one-launch Triton kernels:
the dequant decodes the nested absmax (two roundings, as bitsandbytes does),
adds the offset and applies the NF4 table in a single pass, and the batch-1
GEMV fuses the same decode into the dot product. On HIP the dequant ops are
opaque custom ops so the eager launch keeps fp fusion disabled.

* Pass the quant state's NF4 codebook to the fused dequant

quant_state.code is bit-identical to the kernel's table and already lives on
the device, so a compiled graph no longer rebuilds the table on every call.

tl.gather is only used on Triton >= 3.6 (it fails to compile on 3.3).

Triton's JIT launch rebuilds the argument binding and specialization key on every call, about
12 us of CPU against about 5 us for launching the compiled kernel. triton.cdiv is itself a JIT
function on recent Triton and cost several microseconds per call. On fast GPUs a small QLoRA
model is CPU bound, so both showed up in the step time.

With the direct launch, the int32 words GEMV beat bitsandbytes' in kernel time on T4, L4, A100,

keeps bitsandbytes' GEMV before Triton 3.7 on CUDA. HIP keeps the old gate.

Inductor re-emits the GEMV Triton kernel and, for some Triton versions and launch configs, a
partial sum rounds differently than the eager launch (one ulp in 5 to 16 of 40 seeds on
Triton 3.6 and 3.7 with the byte kernel). The dequant has no reduction and stays exact.

* NF4 kernels: libdevice mul_rn instead of inline PTX

Both multiplies use libdevice mul_rn on CUDA. It is never contracted into an FMA with the
following + offset when torch.compile re-emits the kernel with fp fusion on, and it flushes
subnormal products to zero like the bitsandbytes kernels, so the dequant now also matches
bitsandbytes byte for byte when code * absmax underflows (the PTX mul.rn.f32 kept subnormals).
TRITON_INTERPRET=1 takes the plain multiply route, since the interpreter has no libdevice.

Tests: a fusion-on launch (the route torch.compile takes) and subnormal products, both of which
fail with a plain multiply.

* NF4 kernels: key the torch.compile cache on the kernel source

Inductor's FX graph cache keys a torch.library.triton_op call without the
Triton source behind it. With a warm cache, an edited kernel was served as
the previous kernel's compiled code (reproduced on torch 2.13 by swapping a
mul_rn for a plain multiply: the compiled output stayed identical to the old
kernel until the cache was cleared). Unsloth turns the FX graph cache on, so
an upgrade could keep running an older kernel under torch.compile.

Add a hash of each kernel file to torch.compiler.config.cache_key_tag.

On ROCm (gfx1151, AMD CI) the kernel has no libdevice.mul_rn, so a launch
forced to fp fusion on contracts code2 * absmax2 + offset into an FMA and
differs from bitsandbytes. That route never runs with fusion on: eager
launches pass fp_fusion=False and compiled graphs keep the op opaque. Every
other dequant, GEMV and compile test passed on gfx1151.

Triton 3.2 (torch 2.6) has no tl.gather, and its JIT resolves every attribute

never caches it and every call takes Triton's own path, which is correct; the
cache assertion only applies where the fast path exists.

* NF4 decode: repeat each weight's planned dequant launch

Batch > 1 decode dequantizes every weight into the scratch buffer once per token and is
CPU bound on typical hosts, so the per-call argument handling in fast_dequantize,
dequantize_nf4 and the launch cache key cost more than the kernel. The first call per
weight now plans the launch (triton_launch.relaunch) and later calls repeat it after
checking the weight pointer, the absmax tensor and the dtype. The plan is dropped on
copy and pickle.

Batch 4 decode vs the merge base, Llama-3.2-1B / Qwen3-0.6B 4bit: A100 +17.8% / +17.9%,

Batch-1 decode runs every weight once per token and is CPU bound, so fast_gemv now
repeats the first launch per weight (gemv_nf4_planned) after checking the weight
pointer, the absmax tensor, the activation dtype and its 16 byte alignment, as the
batch > 1 dequant path already does. fast_gemv CPU per call: 13.3 to 9.3 us
(2048x2048), against 24 us for main's bitsandbytes ctypes path.

Batch-1 decode vs main: A100 Llama 3.2 1B +17.3%, Llama 3.1 8B +19.4%, Qwen3 0.6B
+15.9%; L4 +18.1%, +17.2%, +14.0% (was +4% to +6%).

Drop the T4 BLOCK_K 512 rule for large weights. Interleaved CUDA graph timing (T4
throttles, so the sweep that chose it was not) has BLOCK_K 2048 faster at 14336x4096
(261 vs 285 us), 4096x14336 (261 vs 297 us) and the vocab shape (1218 vs 1349 us).

Under torch.compile the accumulating addmm_ calls in the LoRA forward and
backward became out-of-place addmm with a full copy of the accumulator, and
the in-place SwiGLU backward kernel made Inductor copy the saved gate and up
activations first. unsloth::addmm_ (a custom op mutating its output) keeps
the accumulation in place, and the traced SwiGLU backward is plain torch math
that Inductor fuses into one kernel reusing those buffers.

On Triton 3.7, T4 and L4 run the Llama 8B MLP GEMV shapes faster at BLOCK_K
1024 and 2 warps, and T4 dequantizes 5% to 7% faster with 512 byte programs,
8 warps and word loads. Other GPUs keep their configs.

* Studio: overlap the streaming tier's block onloads with compute

The streaming offload tier applied diffusers group offloading with
low_cpu_mem_usage=True and record_stream=False. An unpinned host copy is
pinned again on the CPU at every onload, and record_stream=False makes
every group's offload synchronize the compute stream, so the next block's
pin ran with the GPU idle. Pin the streamed DiTs (then the encoders)
within the host budget the group tier already uses, off the load path
when the caller requested background pins, and keep record_stream on.
UNSLOTH_DIFFUSION_STREAMING_PREFETCH=0 restores the previous kwargs.

* Studio: onload a streamed DiT's top-level weights from one pinned copy

diffusers block-level offload keeps the weights outside the block lists
(embedders, norm_out, proj_out) in a top-level group with no stream:
every forward re-uploads them from pageable host memory and every
offload copies them back into a fresh host buffer, which inference never
needs. Keep one pinned host copy: the onload becomes an async H2D on the
compute stream and the offload only re-points the tensors. VRAM is
unchanged. Skipped for torchao weights and when the copy does not fit
the pinnable host RAM. UNSLOTH_DIFFUSION_PIN_TOP_GROUP=0 turns it off.

* Studio: re-pin a streamed DiT's top-level weight replaced while offloaded

A .to() conversion or an adapter fused on the host swaps the tensor the
top-level group points at while it sits offloaded. The next onload now
pins and uploads what is there instead of the stale copy.

* Studio: size the top-level pin like the pinned allocator and honour the pin override

Round each tensor up to a power of two when checking the host budget, as
_module_host_mib does, and skip the pinned top-level copy when
UNSLOTH_DIFFUSION_GROUP_OFFLOAD_PIN=0 asks for no pinning.

moved onto the GPU whole, even when the memory plan streams or offloads it.
On an 8 GB card Qwen-Image-2.1's int8 DiT (~7 GiB) just fits that spike, and

resident (the end state every offload tier starts from, and what the
runtime-quantise path already does). Kill switch:
UNSLOTH_DIFFUSION_PREQUANT_SEED_ON_HOST=0.

The gallery PNG is encoded between the last denoise step and the HTTP response.
At Pillow's default level 6 that encode cost about 0.4 s on a 1024x1024 render;

balanced always planned group offload with every companion resident and never
checked the budget, so Qwen-Image-2.1 + int8 loaded at 16 / 12 / 8 GB and then
ran out of device memory at the first generate (the resident 9 GiB fp8 text
encoder plus activations); at 8 GB the group apply itself OOMed into

Inductor turns the extract step's key[:, :prefix].clone() into a view of the full
sequence buffer, so every cached layer holds the whole (text + image) K and V until the

* Studio: wait for the torch warm's dynamo import before a load's first unsloth_zoo import

import torch._dynamo reaches unsloth_zoo through its first download

had already lost the race. Gate the unsloth_zoo imports in

Studio: run MiniMax-H3's Diffusers INT8 path on 24 / 16 / 12 GB cards and near the host RAM floor (#12409)

* Studio: overlap the streaming tier's block onloads with compute

The streaming offload tier applied diffusers group offloading with
low_cpu_mem_usage=True and record_stream=False. An unpinned host copy is
pinned again on the CPU at every onload, and record_stream=False makes
every group's offload synchronize the compute stream, so the next block's
pin ran with the GPU idle. Pin the streamed DiTs (then the encoders)
within the host budget the group tier already uses, off the load path
when the caller requested background pins, and keep record_stream on.
UNSLOTH_DIFFUSION_STREAMING_PREFETCH=0 restores the previous kwargs.

* Studio: onload a streamed DiT's top-level weights from one pinned copy

diffusers block-level offload keeps the weights outside the block lists
(embedders, norm_out, proj_out) in a top-level group with no stream:
every forward re-uploads them from pageable host memory and every
offload copies them back into a fresh host buffer, which inference never
needs. Keep one pinned host copy: the onload becomes an async H2D on the
compute stream and the offload only re-points the tensors. VRAM is
unchanged. Skipped for torchao weights and when the copy does not fit
the pinnable host RAM. UNSLOTH_DIFFUSION_PIN_TOP_GROUP=0 turns it off.

* Studio: re-pin a streamed DiT's top-level weight replaced while offloaded

A .to() conversion or an adapter fused on the host swaps the tensor the
top-level group points at while it sits offloaded. The next onload now
pins and uploads what is there instead of the stale copy.

* Studio: size the top-level pin like the pinned allocator and honour the pin override

Round each tensor up to a power of two when checking the host budget, as
_module_host_mib does, and skip the pinned top-level copy when
UNSLOTH_DIFFUSION_GROUP_OFFLOAD_PIN=0 asks for no pinning.

The picker sends 24-48 GB cards to the GGUF (stable-diffusion.cpp) row because the
catalog's only streamed tier asks for 30 GiB VRAM and 80 GiB available RAM. /api/system
now reports diffusers_offload_tiers, which the picker unions with the catalog's tiers

* Studio: let MiniMax-H3 render again on a host near its RAM floor

The streamed int8 denoiser pinned every weight with pin_memory(), and torch's
host allocator rounds each pin up to a power of two: 19.45 GB of weights held
33.8 GB of pinned memory. The host guard then priced the denoiser twice, so on
a 94 GB host the second render was refused (85 GB needed, 82.5 GB available).

- Pack the up-front pinned copies into power-of-two slabs and point each weight
  at its copy during setup, so the pinned copy is the only host copy

- Price an arena-pinned streamed denoiser once in the host floor.
- Count what the process already holds (anonymous + shared resident pages) as
  reusable, and stop counting mmap'd page cache twice
  (UNSLOTH_H3_HOST_GUARD_HELD=0 restores MemAvailable + RSS).

Measured at 960x544x124 on a 40 GB tier: pinned 33.8 -> 20.4 GB, load peak RSS
69.7 -> 37.9 GB, first-render peak 80.1 -> 66.7 GB, repeat 72.9 -> 59.5 GB.
Under an 80 GB memory cap the base refuses the second render; this renders
three in a row with no OOM events. Repeat renders are bit-identical.

* Studio: run MiniMax-H3's Diffusers path on 24 / 16 / 12 GB cards

Stream the int8 conditioner leaf by leaf from pinned arenas instead of
rotating its 27.2 GB onto the card whole, keep the top-level group and a
prefix of the streamed denoiser's blocks resident, sized per request
from the measured encode / denoise / decode needs, and size the VRAM
floor from the largest phase. Kill switches: UNSLOTH_H3_TE_STREAM=0,
UNSLOTH_H3_DIT_RESIDENT=0.

61 GiB of available RAM (the single-count 64.5 GB host floor) while the streamed denoiser holds one host copy

* Refine the sidebar edges, desktop title bar outline, header alignment and hover intent

- Sidebar and side panel edges: drop the heavy sidebar border and draw the
  edges with two calm tokens. --sidebar-edge (left sidebar and the desktop
  title bar outline) fades as raised contrast turns those surfaces gray, via
  a new --contrast-seam-gain curve. --panel-edge (chat run settings panel)
  keeps a steady line, since nothing else separates it from the page.
- Unsloth Desktop on Windows and Linux: restore one continuous light-theme
  outline along the sidebar, its rounded corner and the top bar, and center
  the sidebar brand row on the chat header's model selector by deriving it
  from the same header variables. macOS and Unsloth Web are unchanged.
- Hover intent: sidebar tooltips wait for a short pause, then chain between
  neighbours instantly; only the first tooltip animates in. The More flyout
  opens after a brief pause, stays open while the pointer aims at it, and
  closes at once when the pointer heads elsewhere (useHoverFlyout with the
  pointer-grace geometry in lib/hover-intent).

* Stop the profile menu rows sliding sideways on hover

snapRowInsets is meant to round a menu surface's side padding once, as
it mounts. Radix's PopperContent composes its ref with an inline
callback, so React 19 re-runs the ref on every render, and every hover
re-render re-measured the rows and rewrote the padding. At a 1.5 device
pixel ratio the account menu's border snaps to 2/3px, so each pass
flipped the padding between 10.33/10px and 10/10.33px, and the menu's
100ms transition animated every flip into a sideways slide of all rows.

Snap each surface once per mounted element (WeakSet guard), which every
caller gets: dropdown, submenu, context menu, menubar and select. Verified
in Windows Chrome at 1x, 1.25x and 1.5x: padding and row positions hold
one value across repeated hover sweeps. Adds a regression test that fails
without the guard.

Merge pull request #4412 from Mentra-Community/aisraelov/16-kb-page-sizes-google-play

Build the LC3 native library with 16 KB page alignment

Build the LC3 native library with 16 KB page alignment

Google Play rejects apps targeting Android 15+ whose 64-bit native
libraries have ELF LOAD segments aligned below 16 KB. liblc3.so, the only
native library the public Bluetooth SDK ships, was 4 KB aligned on
arm64-v8a and x86_64 in every published com.mentraglass:lc3Lib version.
Any app that depends on the SDK therefore failed Play's 16 KB check.

lc3Lib builds with NDK r27, which aligns to 16 KB only when
ANDROID_SUPPORT_FLEXIBLE_PAGE_SIZES is on. React Native's Gradle plugin
sets that flag on the app module but never on library modules, so pass
it to lc3Lib's CMake build explicitly.

Fixes OS-2065

minor: add Anthropic API provider with native Messages routing (#1967) ## Why FCC needs direct Anthropic API access. Messages clients selecting Anthropic should retain native tools, content blocks, thinking controls, and response fields, including when they count conversation history before continuing it. ## How - Add an Anthropic provider with an API key, optional Workspace ID and proxy, paginated model discovery, per-model conversion capabilities, and a non-generating credential check in the standard provider modal. - Select the native Messages contract before compatibility parsing and local processing. Preserve native JSON and SSE payloads, replace gateway credentials with configured upstream credentials, and retain public model aliases. - Accept native histories and complete tool definitions in local token estimation. Counts remain approximate and require no upstream request. Compatibility requests retain their existing schema and counting rules. - Discard valid pings received before `message_start`, preserving bounded retries and native fallback before commitment. Commit and relay immediately at `message_start`, with no subsequent retry or fallback. Pre-start pings do not extend the existing terminal progress deadline. - Reuse admission, generation leases, cleanup, and candidate execution. Native fallbacks are limited to other Anthropic models. - Use client controls and Anthropic-hosted tools for native requests. Use FCC protocol conversion for Responses input and compatibility requests that fall back to Anthropic. - Document separate API billing, native settings behavior, and fallback limits in provider help and the README.

Confidence Score: 5/5

No outstanding findings block merging.
Summary The PR adds a directly billed Anthropic provider and native Messages routing. The current code suppresses leading upstream pings until a message starts and accepts opaque native content blocks for token counting. Both previously reported issues are fixed.

feat: maintain every index a table has, including ones created later (#4342)

**The maintained set is an intent, not a snapshot.** An unnamed set is
stored as
the intent to maintain every index, which lance re-resolves whenever it
builds a
MemTable, so an index created after the spec installs is maintained too.
A named
set is checked here, where the caller can be told which names exist; an
index of
a kind the MemWAL cannot mirror fails a named set and is skipped by an
unnamed
one.

**A newly created index reaches a writer that is already open.** lancedb
caches a
`ShardWriter` per shard and reuses it, so `create_index` installs the
current set
on the cached writer. A failure there is reported rather than
propagated: the
index is committed durably by then, and the writer this process holds
may be
fenced or poisoned, which is no reason to fail creating an index.

**A table carries one spec.** `set_lsm_write_spec` fails while one is
installed
and names `unset_lsm_write_spec` in the error, because the generations
already
written were homed under that spec. Accepting a repeat that changed only
the
maintained set would hand a caller who also passed a different sharding
a success
that changed nothing they asked for.

**The read path asks what is actually carried.** An unnamed set leaves
the stored
list empty, so the list alone cannot decide whether an index is
maintained. The
read asks the spec *and* every resident MemTable whether it carries the
index, so
a MemTable built before the index joined the set refuses the read rather
than
answering without its rows. Both spec routes report an unnamed set as
`null`
rather than `[]`: maintain whatever the table gains, and maintain
nothing, are
different settings.

## Known gap

The guard above covers resident MemTables. Once a writer flushes and
closes none
is resident, so a retained generation written before the index existed
still gets
an indexed read that omits its rows.

This window is **wider than on main**: a set resolved at install time
excluded an
index created later, so the read was refused; an intent includes it, and
the
refusal only holds while a MemTable is resident. Closing it needs the
generation's
own coverage, which this layer cannot see — its snapshot carries a
generation and
a path — so it belongs in lance's scanner or flush path.

## Testing

`cargo nextest run -p lancedb --lib --features remote` — **1479 passed,
3
skipped**. `cargo fmt --all --check`, and `cargo clippy --features
remote --lib
--tests --examples -- -D warnings`, both clean.

Covered: the round trip of an unnamed set, a set over an installed spec
refused,
a spec replaced through unset, a read refused while a resident MemTable
predates
the index, and an index created mid-write reaching the open writer.

Two Python binding tests move with the semantics: an unnamed set now
reads back
as `None` rather than the list it resolves to, and the refusal is
matched on
`already set`. Neither was run locally — no Python build here — so CI is
the
check on them.

commits.message: fix(stt): let only the serving owner fence recovery on a managed leg (#20393) ## What `socket_is_finishing()` (`backend/utils/stt/resilient_stream.py`) no longer descends into a managed leg's raw transport. For a managed `LiveLegSocket` (it has `leg_outcome`), "is the session tearing down" is decided only by `leg_outcome.owner_closing`. Unmanaged/legacy sockets keep their `_finishing` latch. One regression test file. ## Why (prod) Since #20343, `LiveLegSocket.send` calls `raw.finish()` as transport cleanup after a rejected send. When a failover replays the capture ring into Soniox and Soniox's 2,000-item send queue overflows (`capacity_full`), that cleanup sets the raw Soniox `_finishing` latch. `ListenReceiver._failover_stt_socket` and the Soniox reconnect path call `socket_is_finishing()`, read the raw latch as client teardown, and return without trying a successor — the session ends (`stt_live_session … outcome=exhausted`, client closed). Independent review finding 2 reproduced it (owner_closing=False, raw finishing=True, backup attempts=0). Listen logs at the evening peak show 6–11 sessions per 25 minutes lost this way, mostly `modulate→soniox` chains; on image `0ba6edb` (before #20343) the same chains recovered. This is the minimal hotfix for that regression. The queue overflow itself (replay is a burst) and the long-term recovery design are in #20391; this does not conflict with it in intent and #20391 will supersede this code. ## Serving behaviour changes | File:line | Old | New | | --- | --- | --- | | `backend/utils/stt/resilient_stream.py` `socket_is_finishing` | Any `_finishing` on the managed wrapper or its raw transport blocked recovery | Managed legs: only `leg_outcome.owner_closing` blocks recovery; unmanaged sockets unchanged | Effect: after a provider death caused by our own transport cleanup, recovery tries the next capable provider again, as on `0ba6edb`. Client-initiated teardown still sets `owner_closing` before flushing (#20343/#20350), so it still blocks recovery. ## Tests `tests/unit/test_recovery_fence_managed_leg.py` (4 cases) plus the neighbouring suites `test_live_stt_resilient_stream.py`, `test_stt_session_failover.py`, `test_live_evidence_settlement.py`, `test_parakeet_failover_exhausted.py`: 110 passed locally. ## Product invariants affected None. fix(people): record where live audio was captured and cut teaching clips there (#20390) ## Summary Labeling a speaker teaches a voiceprint only when the clip cut for that label is the audio that was actually spoken. On live conversations it usually is not: text is timed from the provider stream, stored audio from chunk arrival, and reconnects or provider failover pull the two clocks apart. On one hand-labeled account, `started_at + segment.start` lands within 1 s of the speech for 20% of 1,416 labeled runs and more than 10 s away for 68%. In production the first 13 hours after #20190/#20252 stored 11 of 105 person teaching attempts (text_mismatch 38, insufficient_speech 29). This PR makes new live conversations carry where each segment's audio was captured, and makes every teaching reader use it. ## Change - **Persist the receiver's capture window on live segments.** The receiver already computes a capture-clock window per segment for transient speaker identification and then drops it. Legacy (v2-off) persistence now stores it in two private fields, `audio_capture_start` / `audio_capture_end` (absolute Unix seconds). Text, speaker, `start`/`end` and ordering are unchanged; the fields are absent when unknown, cleared when a text merge spans a capture gap, kept out of the client schema and stripped from every client frame. `AUDIO_TIMELINE_V2` is untouched. New counter `omi_live_audio_capture_windows_total{outcome,reason}` shows what share of new segments are placeable. - **One placement module** (`utils/conversations/audio_placement.py`). `locate()` returns a trusted window only for audio-timeline v2 manifests and `sync:`-timed segments and refuses otherwise. `candidate_window()` gives verified readers the capture-clock position when every contributor recorded one with a consistent offset, else the legacy origin. Person teaching, the owner clip, tag-prompt clips and the text search all go through it. A capture window is a better candidate, not proof: every teaching path still runs the 0.9 transcript containment check before publishing. - **Bounded text-anchored recovery for teaching**, default off (`SPEAKER_TEACHING_TEXT_PLACEMENT`): after a text mismatch, search at most 32 s around the candidate using the verification transcript's word times, re-verify at most 12 s. Containment gate unchanged. - **Manual merge keeps source clocks.** The manual merge writer offset each donor by the prior transcript end plus a wall gap while copying audio at unchanged absolute timestamps, shifting later donors' text early. It now rebases from source wall-clock origins. - **Conversation-wide resolution never names from unplaced text.** Unplaced or abstained segments no longer inherit a cluster's name through a shared old speaker id. ## Evidence Offline replay on one hand-labeled account (aggregates only; one account, so no population claim): - Stored live conversations cannot be re-placed from metadata: strict `locate()` returns 0 of 1,416 runs (it refuses rather than guesses), and bounded text search recovers 13 of 748 mismatched windows, all 13 within 1 s. Old conversations stay as they are; this PR fixes forward. - Synthetic replay through the real receiver and persistence: capture windows stored for 0 of 18 segments before, 11 of 18 after (receiver had a window for 14 of 20 inputs; gaps and partial sentence repair clear it by design). All 18 stored payloads are byte-identical to before once the two new fields are removed. - A burst/clock-jump fixture shows the capture clock and the stored-chunk clock can still disagree (known metadata 2 of 2, exact stored-audio matches 0 of 2). That is why the capture window is used only behind transcript verification and `locate()` does not trust it. Not measured: production availability of capture windows (the new counter will show it) and the change in production store rates. ## Tests - New: `test_live_capture_windows.py`, `test_live_capture_persistence.py`, `test_live_capture_lifecycle.py`, `test_audio_placement.py`, `test_audio_placement_merge.py`, `test_teaching_placement.py`, `test_audio_capture_candidate.py`; additions to `test_conversation_speakers.py` and `test_merge_validation.py`. - `BACKEND_UNIT_TEST_FILE_LIST` over 19 related files via `backend/test.sh`: all pass. `scripts/typecheck.sh`: 0 errors. - TranscriptSegment and Conversation JSON schemas compared equal to pre-change snapshots; no generated client changed. - Not run: anything against a live backend or device, Docker image build. ## Rollout notes - Backend, listen and pusher should deploy together: the fields are written on the live path and read by teaching in the backend. - No migration or backfill. Existing conversations behave as before (legacy origin candidate). - Turn off: `LIVE_SPEAKER_CAPTURE_CLOCK=false` stops new windows being attached (it also changes the existing live matching path; use its established procedure). The text search is off unless `SPEAKER_TEACHING_TEXT_PLACEMENT` is set. - Watch: `omi_live_audio_capture_windows_total` persisted share; `omi_person_voice_learning_total` and the owner sample outcomes for text_mismatch falling on new conversations. ## Product invariants affected none ## Failure class Failure-Class: FC-transcript-and-audio-on-independent-clocks Teaching read transcript coordinates as if they addressed stored audio. This records the capture position at write time, routes every teaching reader through one placement gate that refuses unknown clocks for trusted use, and keeps transcript verification in front of every publication.
