commits.message:
Present the notebooks' design decisions without the repair history (#1141)

Thirty-two notebooks explained a choice by narrating what an earlier version of
the same notebook did wrong: "an earlier version of this notebook fixed a
reporting checkpoint in advance", "the previous version of this cell emitted the
union of the four", "it used to require the advance to equal `step` exactly",
"this case study reached 2026-09-14 with no such check". A reader working the
material gets the repository's repair log instead of the method, and a dated
incident in a teaching notebook is not something they can act on.

Every passage keeps the reasoning and the measurements that earned it and states
the alternative in the subjunctive: what a per-period walk would cost, what a
`tr.family = 'gbm'` clause in the query would refuse, what a policy reading
`case.answerable` would measure. Nothing is deleted except the claim that we
once did it the other way.

Markdown and comments only. Each pair is folded in with
`notebook_provenance.py sync-prose`, which refuses a moved code cell, so every
notebook keeps the outputs and the `executed_at` of the run that produced them;
the four notebooks that carry no stamp are synced with jupytext. No computed
value moves and nothing is re-run.

Feature windows and diagnostic lags stop at gaps in the session or bar clock (#1140)

* sp500_options: the IV lag sweep lags by sessions, not by a symbol's rows

`90_ic_diagnostic` built its "IC by feature lag" table with
`shift(lag).over("symbol")` on the concatenated validation windows. The
options panel is sparse per name and the windows are separated by training
spans, so the row `lag` rows back was usually not `lag` sessions back: on
the real panel 97,951 of 351,180 values at lag 5 came from the wrong
session, and most of them at lag 63.

`lagged_by_sessions` numbers the panel's session list and joins each row to
the value its symbol carried exactly `lag` sessions earlier, null where the
name did not quote. The notebook asserts that list has no NYSE session
missing before using it, and reads the lag from the full dataset so a
validation row may take a value from the preceding training span, which is
already known at the decision.

Lag table, old -> new (mean validation IC; IV autocorrelation):
  5:  +0.0173 -> +0.0144; 0.642 -> 0.779
  10: +0.0296 -> +0.0311; 0.435 -> 0.596
  15: +0.0168 -> +0.0208; 0.289 -> 0.427
  20: -0.0085 -> -0.0167; 0.181 -> 0.274
  42: -0.0067 -> -0.0250; 0.005 -> 0.065
  63: +0.0045 -> -0.0176; -0.017 -> 0.111
No other output changed. Executed against the canonical features and labels.

tests/test_sp500_options_lag_by_sessions.py fails on the row shift (two
synthetic cases and the real-panel check) and passes on the join.

* crypto_perps_funding: settlement windows stop at gaps in the 8-hour bars

The 8-hour perpetual bars have eight gaps of two and three days (MKR, NEAR,
SOL and XRP around 2022-03-01 and 2022-04-03). `03_financial_features`
took every shift and rolling window `.over("symbol")`, so the change across
a gap entered as one settlement's return and a window spanning it was
counted as its nominal length; `04_model_based_features` fed the same
cross-gap return to the GARCH walk.

`contiguous_run` (case_studies/utils/feature_engineering.py) numbers each
unbroken stretch of an entity's rows on a session or bar clock. Stage 03
adds `_run` to the panel and takes every per-symbol window over
`["symbol", "_run"]`, so a window that would span a gap returns nothing and
warms up again after it; the D.2 warmup audit now runs per stretch, so a
window that failed to restart would fail it. Stage 04 keeps only returns
whose previous bar is one bar length back before the GARCH fit.

Stage 03, old -> new: 99,877 -> 99,197 rows pass the gate (772 rows whose
windows spanned a gap are gone; every kept row's values are unchanged);
coverage 92.22% -> 91.60%; content digest cb5fc87851ad250f ->
8e2640cd5107505f; the Section E accounting now separates 720 keys that
follow a bar gap, and the unexplained residual goes 1,068 -> 1,028.
Stage 04: GARCH rows 98,798 -> 98,790; artifact rows 98,741 -> 98,733;
validation rows scored 34,140 -> 33,429; garch_cond_vol mean IC -0.0389 ->
-0.0390 (t -5.23 -> -5.11), garch_asymmetry +0.0183 -> +0.0200,
garch_vol_zscore -0.0042 -> -0.0028; the top price/funding feature by mean
IC is now premium_accel_medium rather than premium_accel_short.

Both notebooks were executed into an isolated output root, so the
canonical feature artifacts are untouched.

Co-authored-by: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

Strip the embedded Plotly JSON from committed notebooks (#1138)

* Strip the embedded Plotly JSON from committed notebooks, 131 MB of it

Plotly's notebook renderer serializes every data point of every trace into the
.ipynb under application/vnd.plotly.v1+json, beside a static image/png of the same
figure. 04_fundamental_alternative_data/01_academic_characteristics.ipynb was 25.3 MB
of which 0.03 MB was source and 26.1 MB that payload; opening it on github.com left
the content pane empty for over twenty seconds, measured 2026-10-01.

An Amazon reviewer called the notebooks impossible to read. The median notebook here
is 37 cells and 429 lines of code with roughly one line of prose per two lines of
code, so the complaint is not about length. It is about weight, and this is all of it.

Repository-wide: 654 Plotly outputs across 203 notebooks, every one of them already
carrying an image/png of the same figure, 0.11 GB of JSON. After the strip the largest
notebook is 1.22 MB and five exceed 1 MB, down from 41.

What a reader loses is hover, zoom and legend toggling while browsing a committed
notebook on GitHub without running it. What nobody loses is the figure, which the PNG
shows, or the interactivity when the cell is executed. An output with no static
fallback is never stripped - there the payload is the only copy of the chart - and
`--check` reports any such output rather than passing over it.

outputs_digest hashes the outputs, so the strip reads as stale. A re-run is the wrong
answer and not merely an expensive one: re-executing writes the payload straight back,
so the gate would be demanding the one action that undoes the fix. That is the argument
sanitize_notebook_paths.py already makes for a machine path in an output, so this takes
the same shape: a new `sync-plotly` re-derives the strip from the committed notebook and
refuses unless the working copy matches it exactly. sync_paths and sync_plotly now share
that guard logic in _fold_output_rewrite.

Fixes a bug in those guards while extracting them. A stamp written before outputs_digest
existed pins nothing, and the gate says so - it counts such a notebook rather than
failing it. The comparison read `<digest> != None` and refused it as "stale before this
rewrite", which is false: it is undated, not stale. Six notebooks in 18_transaction_costs
and 19_risk_management are in that state and sync_paths has been refusing them the same
way. They now fold in without a stamp being written, because writing a digest would
assert these outputs are the ones that run produced, which is the one claim an absent
digest means nobody can make. The rewrite-equality check moved ahead of every stamp
comparison so that branch cannot wave an edit through.

Verified against HEAD for all 203: 654 payloads removed, and no change to any cell's
source, cell count, output count, other mime type, output metadata, notebook metadata,
or any stamp field but outputs_digest and notes.

* Fix a crash on a relative path, and strip before stamping rather than after

Both found by the RoboRev gate on the first push of this branch.

A relative notebook argument - which is how anyone types one - reached
`relative_to(REPO_ROOT)` unresolved and raised ValueError. It fired only on the
branch that prints a path, so a run over an already-clean tree returned 0 and the
bug was invisible: `strip_plotly_json.py --check some/nb.ipynb` crashed whenever
that notebook actually had something to report. Arguments are resolved now, and a
notebook outside the repository is named absolutely rather than crashing the run.

The second is an ordering trap in the fresh-execution flow. Every re-run writes the
Plotly payload back, so a notebook has to be stripped again after each one. Stamping
digests the outputs, so run -> stamp -> strip leaves a digest describing outputs the
committed file no longer has, and the gate reports OUTPUTS CHANGED on a notebook
whose numbers never moved. Rather than document the order, `stamp_notebook` now
strips before it reads the outputs, so there is no order to get wrong and nb-run.sh
needs no change. It remains bounded by the same rule as the standalone tool: an
output whose payload is the figure's only copy is left alone, which is its own test.

commits.message:
fix: keep sources visible and hide the narrow nav scrollbar (#106)

* fix: keep sources visible and hide the narrow nav scrollbar

Sources were in a collapsed grey <details> toggle that readers missed. The template now renders them as a visible section, and the style guide says never to collapse them.

On narrow screens the sticky section nav showed a grey scrollbar under the links. The diagrams reference now says to hide it, fade the right edge, and keep buttons outside the scrolling list.

* fix: style the template sources label with the existing label classes
chore: release 0.12.0

refactor: draw every diagram by hand and make Mermaid opt-in (#105)

* refactor: draw every diagram by hand and make Mermaid opt-in

The skill still sent sequence, ER, class, git graph, and large graphs to
Mermaid. Its output ignores the page fonts and tokens, cannot use flow
dots, steppers, live figures, or linked highlighting, needs a CDN
script, and one bad character blanks a diagram.

Remove mermaid.md and route every diagram type to hand-drawn SVG, with
two layout lines for sequence and schema diagrams and the large-graph
overview rule moved to diagrams.md. When a user asks for Mermaid, one
Known-traps line covers theming, labels, sizing, and class collisions,
and the v0.11.0 zoom template stays linked.

* docs: keep the Mermaid opt-in in the generate command

feat: add a live figure pattern (#104)

* feat: add a live figure pattern

Explainers and plans could only show a setting's effect in prose. Add a
short live-figure contract: one to three controls drive one pure model
that redraws the figure, numbers, and headline, defaulting to the real
value. A policy toggle covers the why-demo from #96. Copying production
validators into the page stays out of scope.

Closes #96

* docs: hide live-figure controls without JS and keep them under reduced motion

feat: package the skill as an Agent Plugins 1.0.0 plugin (#103)

* feat: package the skill as an Agent Plugins 1.0.0 plugin

Agent Plugins clients discover skills only at skills/<name>/SKILL.md
under a plugin root with a plugin.json manifest, and the manifest cannot
point elsewhere. Make the repository root the plugin: add plugin.json
and skills/visual-explainer as a relative link to the canonical skill,
which stays inside the root as the spec requires. No files move, so
existing Claude Code, Pi, and copy-based installs are unchanged.

The version guard now covers plugin.json.

Closes #100

* fix: check the skill link and keep the npm package plugin-free

npm drops symlinks, so the package cannot carry skills/visual-explainer
and is not an Agent Plugins root. Stop shipping plugin.json, and stop
shipping scripts/, which only held the repo-only version guard. The
guard now also fails when skills/visual-explainer/SKILL.md does not
resolve to the canonical skill.

fix: keep page styles out of Mermaid diagrams (#102)

* fix: keep page styles out of Mermaid diagrams

The reference page defined a bare .label class for eyebrow and KPI
labels. Mermaid wraps every node label in .label, so a page that copied
the template and added a diagram shrank all node text to 12.75px.

Rename the template class to .ve-label, list every bare class Mermaid
emits in the guidance, and add a computed-style check, because the leak
looks deliberate in a screenshot.

Closes #98

* docs: limit the ve- prefix rule to Mermaid's class names

feat(pi): honor VISUAL_EXPLAINER_OUTPUT_DIR in the visual_explainer tool (#99)

* feat(pi): honor VISUAL_EXPLAINER_OUTPUT_DIR in the visual_explainer tool

The MCP server already lets VISUAL_EXPLAINER_OUTPUT_DIR move its output
jail, but the Pi extension always wrote to ~/.agent/diagrams. A Pi session
whose home directory is not writable, such as a sandboxed one, had no way
to put renders anywhere else.

The Pi tool now resolves the output directory the same way as the MCP
server. The default stays ~/.agent/diagrams. A configured directory must not
be a symlink and must resolve to itself; filenames stay basenames inside it.

* fix(pi): write renders through a temporary file, and point /fact-check at the output directory

Review on #99: with a configured directory another local user may be able
to write to, a target swapped for a symlink between the check and the
write was written through. Pi renders now go to a temporary file created
with O_EXCL and are renamed into place, as MCP renders already are; rename
replaces a symlink at the target instead of following it.

/fact-check without an argument looked only in ~/.agent/diagrams. It now
names the same output directory the render actions use.

* fix(pi): keep an existing render's permission bits, and match /fact-check to the blank rule

Review on #99: renaming a new file over an existing render dropped the
permission bits the original had. The temporary file now takes the
existing file's mode before the rename. ACLs and extended attributes are
still not carried over, the same as the MCP writer.

/fact-check said to use VISUAL_EXPLAINER_OUTPUT_DIR whenever it is set,
while the tool treats a blank value as unset. It now says non-blank.

---------

Co-authored-by: eaxeax <1449370+eaxeax@users.noreply.github.com>
Co-authored-by: Nico Bailon <nico.bailon@gmail.com>

The reviewer also found palette text below 4.5:1, missing figure captions, and an unnamed slide dialog. - style-guide.md: four registers (Instrument, Blueprint, Paper, Editorial), each with fixed fonts and contrast-checked light/dark palettes; one shared space/type/radius/motion scale, component specs, polish pass - linked highlighting: prose terms and figure parts light up together - page.html rebuilt as the Instrument register; slide deck trimmed and moved to Editorial - themes.md: lift --text-dim to 4.5:1 in failing palettes - restore source-brief companion trigger and dialog accessible name * fix(skill): keep dimmed and printed text readable; align guide and templates - dim diagram shapes, not text: unlit labels switch to --text-dim and future-step labels are hidden instead of faded below 4.5:1 - print uses light foregrounds, draws every step, and fits paper width - captions, table cells, and details use body size - linked highlighting keeps the focused selection after hover ends - deck outline: --text on the accent tint; tint 12%, rail radius r-2 - style guide: dimming rule, t-small scope, h1 line height, color fades, KPI size exception; diagrams.md examples match page.html * fix(skill): address Greptile review on #101 - quick mode: resolve render.mjs from the skill directory, not the cwd - slides: PPTX drops SVG, so figure slides also carry their claim in a

- themes: add --ok/--warn/--risk/--info columns (lifted to 4.5:1), lift --accent where needed, set --border-bright from --text-dim - registers: --border-bright raised to 3:1 so node outlines and control borders meet the line-contrast rule; --border stays decorative * fix(deck): decorative rules use --border, not --border-bright The title-slide divider, KPI grid lines, and dialog frame are decorative. --border-bright stays on key caps, buttons, and diagram outlines. * feat(skill): crafted, topic-aware figures with fewer words - topic motif: the subject supplies accent hue, stage texture, glyphs, type habit, or diagram convention, in 2-3 subtle touches - page.html: raised nodes on a dot-grid stage, cylinder datastore, node glyphs, halo on the key node, glow on the hot path, flow dots at the real 94:6 split, number-led headline - every number gets a picture (waffle, bars); failure cases become small multiples instead of a sentence table - entrance motion (rise-in, count-up, bar growth) via .js-motion, so no-JS, print, and reduced motion show the final state - three.js guidance for figures where depth carries data - diagrams.md keeps markup contracts and rules, not CSS/JS the template already holds; word limits become flexible guidance * feat(skill): editorial typography, layout, and chart rules Style guide gains compact Typography, Layout, and Figures tables drawn from Bringhurst, Butterick, Müller-Brockmann, Tufte, Datawrapper, and the FT Visual Vocabulary: measure, leading, tracking, numerals, real characters, font hygiene, text-box trim; 12-column grid, one axis, section openers, entry points, proximity, rhythm; chart choice by relationship, data-ink, layering, direct labels, annotation, honest scales, line weights, OKLCH color scales, optical alignment. page.html applies them: Swiss section openers, meta line, cap-trimmed headings, font hygiene, no-break unit spaces, an annotated waffle. * fix(skill): make page structure flexible - figures usually lead, but reasoning and definitions can be text-led - teaching pages may open on the question and its framing picture - add a page-shapes table (explainer, plan, review, comparison, essay, single diagram) as starting points, not templates - section openers: Swiss, kicker, or figure head, one per page - command section tables become typical sections to merge or drop - copy page.html's parts, not its outline * fix(page): stop flow dots while a stepper shows an intermediate step The dot loop kept spawning and moving hidden dots mid-step. It now stops and clears them unless the figure is visible and on the full picture, restarts on the stepper's ve:step event, and cannot run twice. * fix(mermaid): restore safe SVG insert, readable fit, pinch and 1:1 The rewritten shell had dropped earlier fixes: - insert via DOMParser again instead of innerHTML (#37, PR #54), so foreignObject labels survive and scanners stay quiet - readability floor: zoom never below 0.75, so 16px labels stay >= 12px and big graphs pan instead of shrinking; height follows the graph - two-pointer pinch zoom with a smooth hand-back to pan, and a 1:1 button SKILL.md links the removed long-form references and templates, pinned to v0.11.0, as optional on-demand recipes.

fix: use bounded read for workflow catalog HTTP responses (#3766)

* fix: use bounded read for workflow catalog HTTP responses

The workflow catalog fetch used unbounded resp.read() to read HTTP
responses into memory. A malicious or misconfigured catalog server
could return an arbitrarily large response causing OOM.

(1 MiB) at both call sites, consistent with how other JSON fetch
paths in the codebase enforce bounded reads.

rejection path at test_fetch_rejects_oversized_catalog_response.

Drop the two rejection tests that duplicated that coverage and patched
MAX_JSON_METADATA_BYTES, which no longer exists, so they failed with
AttributeError.

* fix(workflows): bound step package traversal by the entry ceiling

The 512-entry ceiling did not bound validation work: each directory
listing was fully materialized and sorted before any entry was counted,
and excluded subtrees (`.git`, `__pycache__`) were walked in full without
consuming the budget, so a `--dev` checkout with a large `.git` cost
unbounded time and memory.

- Stream `os.scandir` through a shared helper that drops excluded names
  unread and raises the entry-limit error once the remaining budget is
  exceeded, before sorting. Validation and staging copy both use it.
- Prune excluded directories instead of descending into them, matching
  `bundles/packager.py`. Their contents were already never staged, so a
  symlink or deep nesting inside `.git` no longer fails validation.
- Update the workflow reference to describe the exclusion behavior.
- Replace the symlink-inside-`.git` rejection test with pruning coverage
  and add read-count regressions for validation, a cross-directory

printed the ID, step directory, and exception text raw on every path, and

- Escape the step ID in the `step add` discovery-only catalog warning.

* fix(workflows): report step lock failures once

`step remove` shares the step lock with `step add`, but the shared helper

* fix(bundles): restore failed step refreshes under the step lock

When a bundle step refresh removes a step and the reinstall fails, the

commits.message:
chore(android): cross-compile and test the SDK on Android (#1415)

First step toward Android support. Cross-compiles the whole SDK and its unit
tests for Android and runs them on an emulator. 1273 tests pass on API 35 /
arm64-v8a; the macOS suite is unchanged at 1411.

Two portability fixes were needed:

- Android's Foundation does not vend `POSIXErrorCode`. The WebSocket close
  mapping now matches on the platform's own `ENOTCONN`/`EPROTO` constants,
  which are in scope everywhere and keep the Darwin-vs-Linux errno
  difference the original change was for.
- ConcurrencyExtras only implements `withMainSerialExecutor` where it can
  swap the runtime's global executor hook, which rules out Android. The
  existing Windows passthrough is generalised to cover both, and gains the
  async overload the call sites actually use.

Five Realtime tests drive a `TestClock` and rely on that serial executor to
know the task they are waking already reached its `sleep`. With a
passthrough they race: three hang, two observe a half-finished sequence.
They are skipped on Android and Windows through one condition trait rather
than five scattered `#if`s, and still run everywhere else.

Notably `URLOpener.live` compiles to an empty closure on Android, so
`signInWithOAuth` would hang, and there is no default `AuthLocalStorage`.
Full platform support — a CI job, a dynamic library product for JNI
consumption, and closing those gaps — is follow-up work.

feat(realtime)!: adopt Duration for the remaining TimeInterval intervals (#1401)

* feat(realtime)!: adopt Duration for the remaining TimeInterval intervals

RealtimeClientOptions takes heartbeatInterval, reconnectDelay, timeout
(renamed from timeoutInterval) and disconnectOnEmptyChannelsAfter as
Duration, matching HTTPClientConfiguration.timeout and
FunctionInvokeOptions.timeout. The per-call httpSend timeout is
Duration? too. withTimeout, ConnectionManager and ChannelStateManager
follow the public change, so no interval converts through Double
seconds any more.

The @_disfavoredOverload initializer without protocolVersion is
removed; the primary initializer accepts every call it did.

BREAKING CHANGE: RealtimeClientOptions intervals and the httpSend
timeout are Duration; timeoutInterval is now timeout and
defaultTimeoutInterval is now defaultTimeout. See V3_MIGRATION.md.

Fixes SDK-1854

* chore: register RealtimeClientOptions.defaultTimeout in capability matrix

The rename from defaultTimeoutInterval surfaces as a new public symbol
against main. It governs subscribe/unsubscribe/broadcast/broadcast_http
timeouts alike rather than belonging to one capability, so register it
in the top-level supporting_symbols list next to RealtimeError, which
is documented there for the same reason.

* fix(auth): scope signOut's /logout call to the session it signs out

execute(for:) expects SessionOwnership, not Session — the call didn't
type-check, breaking main's build. #1399 clearly meant .snapshot(session)
(authorizedExecute right below uses the identical pattern): scope cleanup
to the session read before the request went out, so a sign-in that lands
while /logout is in flight doesn't get wiped by a stale response.

fix(auth): pass the session being signed out as SessionOwnership (#1416)

signOut() called api.execute(_:for:) with the Session itself. The ownership
parameter takes SessionOwnership so the session-cleanup it gates is scoped
to the session that was actually signed out, not whatever happens to be
stored when the response comes back — this call passed the raw Session,
which doesn't satisfy that type and fails to compile.

.snapshot(session) is the case for that: clear storage only while it still
holds exactly this session, so a slow /logout response can't sign out
whoever signed in after it.

fix(auth): complete signOut when the server no longer has the session (#1399)

* fix(auth): complete signOut when the server no longer has the session

A /logout answered with session_not_found surfaced as a thrown sessionMissing error, emitted signedOut a second time, and cleared whichever session was stored by then. signOut now treats that answer as a completed sign out and scopes the cleanup to the session it signed out.

* fix(auth): finish the Dependencies subscript -> sut.dependencies migration in the new signOut tests

The three signOut tests added for session_not_found handling still used the
pre-#1395 `Dependencies[sut.clientID]` accessor, which no longer compiles
now that `Dependencies` is a plain struct held directly by `AuthClient`.

---------

Co-authored-by: Guilherme Souza <guilherme@supabase.io>

fix(auth)!: use UUID for MFA challenge identifiers (#1412)

AuthMFAChallengeResponse.id and MFAVerifyParams.challengeId are now UUID.
The Auth server stores mfa_challenges.id as uuid and decodes the verify
request's challenge_id as uuid.UUID, so a non-UUID string can only fail.

BREAKING CHANGE: AuthMFAChallengeResponse.id and MFAVerifyParams.challengeId
change from String to UUID. See V3_MIGRATION.md.

fix(postgrest): quote filter values and array elements with surrounding newlines (#1413)

* fix(postgrest): quote array elements in rpc GET/HEAD params

rpc(get: true) and rpc(head: true) send each param as a query value, and
an array param becomes a Postgres array literal. Its elements were
joined unquoted, so the function received something other than what the
caller passed, while the same call over POST was right:

- ["Paris, France", "Oslo"] became {Paris, France,Oslo}: 3 elements.
- "NULL" became a SQL NULL, and "{x}" a nested array.
- "" or a double quote made PostgREST reject the call with 400
  "malformed array literal".

Each element now goes through escapePostgRESTArrayLiteralElement, the
same per-element quoting the cs/cd array filters already use. Nested
arrays stay bare sub-literals and a JSON null stays a bare null, so the
existing snapshots do not change.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(postgrest): quote filter values and array elements with surrounding newlines

The quoting checks trimmed only `.whitespaces` (space and tab). Postgres
`array_in` and PostgREST's filter parser also strip leading and trailing
`\n`, `\r`, `\v` and `\f` from unquoted values, so an element such as
"line\n" silently arrived as "line". Use `.whitespacesAndNewlines` so
those values get quoted.

Follow-up to #1383.

---------

Co-authored-by: breken-ai <312387581+breken-ai@users.noreply.github.com>
Co-authored-by: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

fix(auth): scope session cleanup to the session a request redeems (#1402)

The session cleanup guard from #1374 took a `Session?` snapshot, where `nil`
meant both "no session declared, clean up unconditionally" (sign-in, sign-up,
`/logout`) and "storage was empty when I started" (the `setSession` hydration
path). `SessionStorage.changed(since:)` returned `false` for `nil`, so two
holes stayed open:

- A refresh that started with empty storage never saw a sign-in that landed
  while `/token` was in flight. On success it committed over the new session;
  on a cleanup error it deleted it and emitted `.signedOut`.
- `refreshSession(refreshToken:)` is public and takes any token. Called with
  token A while session B was stored, B became the cleanup scope, so a
  `refresh_token_not_found` for A deleted B and signed that user out.

Replace the optional snapshot with `SessionOwnership`: `.unscoped` keeps the
unconditional cleanup, `.snapshot(Session?)` clears storage only while it still
holds exactly that snapshot, `nil` included. `changed(since: nil)` now means
"storage is no longer empty", so hydration commits only while storage stays
empty. The refresh path scopes its cleanup to the stored session only when that
session's refresh token is the one being redeemed; the success-path commit guard
keeps the plain storage delta, so `setSession` over another user's stored
session still replaces it, as in supabase-js.

Fixes SDK-1894

Co-authored-by: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.message:
feat(lilygo): add T-Circle-S3 V1.1 board (#2286)

The T-Circle-S3 V1.1 revision differs from V1.0 only in the microphone: V1.0
uses an MSM261S4030H0R on standard I2S (BCLK 7, WS 9, DATA 8), V1.1 an
MP34DT05-A on PDM (CLK 9, DATA 8). Everything else - display, touch, speaker,
LEDs - is identical.

A PDM microphone cannot be read by an I2S standard-mode receiver, so V1.1
hardware captures nothing on the existing board and the wake word never
triggers. Board identity affects OTA compatibility, so this is a new board
rather than a change to the existing one.

Capture runs at 32 kHz rather than the 16 kHz the wake-word engine uses. The
ESP32-S3 derives the PDM clock as 64x the sample rate, so 16 kHz would give
only ~1.02 MHz, below the MP34DT05-A minimum, where the microphone stays in
power-down and its data line reads as a constant - indistinguishable from
absent hardware. 32 kHz gives ~2.05 MHz and the audio service resamples down
to 16 kHz for the detector.

The board uses the shared NoAudioCodecSimplexPdm codec, with a thin subclass
driving the MAX98357A SD_MODE pin (GPIO45) alongside the output channel.

Tested on physical V1.1 hardware: Wi-Fi provisioning, device activation, MQTT
session, wake word, microphone capture, speaker playback, display and touch.
A multi-turn conversation was run with the device speaking several long
responses - no false wake-word triggers, no self-transcription, no spurious
state transitions. Device-side AEC cannot engage without a playback reference
channel, which this hardware does not provide; server-side AEC is unaffected.

No existing board is modified.

Co-authored-by: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.message:
Confirm pose and display changes

Summary:
Add opt-in `--wait` support to physical rotation and hinge setters. Each command writes the requested pose exactly once, then performs bounded authoritative readback before returning.

Add `--wait-for-display` for callers that also require two identical active-display snapshots. JSON output reports the requested and observed pose, stable display, confirmation result, elapsed time, and sample count; timeouts emit the same result before exiting nonzero. Existing non-waiting setter and getter output remains unchanged.

Expose current display geometry separately from display identity so legacy single-display runtimes can report interface rotation without inventing a UUID.

Reviewed By: cute-jumper

Differential Revision: D122898945

fbshipit-source-id: fa7c4e1797d797cc13c8e758c51cc7209125602f

Pin simulator display capabilities and input

Summary:
Expose unsupported simulator capabilities explicitly, keep framebuffer attachments alive for their full consumer lifetime, and allow HID operations to target one named display. This is the FBSimulatorControl foundation used by Duo capture and touch routing.

The active-display resolver distinguishes transient no-active and ambiguous states from permanent unsupported capabilities, accepts identified sole-display configurations for pinned HID, and keeps the creating framebuffer alive until its attachment unregisters.

Reviewed By: lawrencelomax

Differential Revision: D122672039

fbshipit-source-id: 6708f215bda9c09310c048f187694e514eda9aa5

Spin the address bar that is on screen in the spin demo

Summary:
The `spin-safaris-address-bar` demo now spins the address bar Safari is showing, and fails if the view it spins does not surround the address bar that accessibility reports.

Safari on iOS 26 keeps an address bar capsule for every open tab, each with a `TabBarItemTitle` view, laid out beside the current one and outside the window. The injected Swift took the first `TabBarItemTitle` it found, which is the visible bar only when Safari has a single tab. On GitHub Actions, the web content demo runs earlier in the same shard and leaves its own tab open, so the spin went to an off-screen capsule (`Spinning a SFCapsuleView, 222×48 points`). Every step passed, but the published recording shows a still address bar.

- The Swift now spins only a `TabBarItemTitle` that is drawn inside its window, with no hidden or transparent ancestor. If it finds anything other than exactly one, it says how many and spins nothing.
- The result now includes the bar's frame on screen, and the demo checks that the frame surrounds the address bar's accessibility frame. Spinning an off-screen view is now a test failure instead of a silent no-op in the video.

This can't be pinned by a unit test: it needs a live Safari on a simulator with more than one tab open, and before this change every assertion passed. Verified by the next GitHub Actions run after export: the demos shard and the published recording.

Differential Revision: D123032904

fbshipit-source-id: afe9c627d5f7537f43799de1709ea73e1d0a53e9

Spin Safari's whole address bar in the spin demo, long enough to see

Summary:
The `spin-safaris-address-bar` demo now visibly spins the address bar. Before, it spun only the view behind the `TabBarItemTitle` identifier, which is the 66×20 point address text, so in the recording the demo looked as if nothing happened. It also spun for only a few seconds before the tap, and the stop step reported `Stopped 0 spinning view(s)`.

- The injected Swift climbs from the address text to the widest view around it that is still inset from the window's edges. In Safari on iOS 26 that is the 234×48 point `SFCapsuleView`, and the result names it and its size.
- Each turn takes four seconds, and the demo holds for ten seconds before tapping. Safari reuses the capsule for the edit field, so the spin carries on after the tap until the stop step.
- The spin snippet leaves the view in `Thread.main.threadDictionary`, and the stop snippet takes it from there. This works because the second injection runs in the same live Safari. The stop step now reports the view it stopped, instead of walking the hierarchy for an animation key.

This is a recording-only defect. A unit test could not pin it: every assertion passed before, and the problem showed only in the video.

Differential Revision: D123018042

fbshipit-source-id: 16b8c054476c1c2f351f538c9c38dee98b627d85

Open an app from a notification banner in the demos

Summary:
The notification demo now ends the way a user's would: the push it delivers to News while News isn't running shows as a banner over the home screen, and tapping the banner opens News. It replaces `send-and-clear-a-notification` with `open-an-app-from-a-notification-banner`, and still clears the app's notifications afterwards.

A SpringBoard banner is not in the accessibility tree idb reads, so the demo taps where banners appear rather than a banner it has found. Before the push, `ui describe-point` shows that nothing at that point opens News, so News running after the tap (read from `simctl`, not idb) can only mean the banner took the tap.

Differential Revision: D122615802

fbshipit-source-id: 2b1197a4ce196cd8b3ac748577fc4d30d381b539

Say what the demos are for, and document the site's landing and featured demos

Summary: No behavioural change. The `test_demos.py` docstring no longer claims that every behaviour a demo shows also has a targeted test. It now says that demos are written to be read, that the targeted tests hold behaviour, and that the two may overlap.

Differential Revision: D122614385

fbshipit-source-id: a16975e0ff9cfb0247d8f63568cb596fc3dda13a

Merge the tap and scroll demos into one list-navigation demo

Summary:
The `tap-by-accessibility-id` and `scroll-by-element` demos become one demo, `navigate-a-list-by-accessibility-id`. It scrolls the fixture's list down from its General row, scrolls back up from a row that scrolled into view, then taps General by its accessibility identifier and reads the navigation bar of the page that opened. Every step names its element by accessibility identifier. The steps and their checks are the ones the two demos already made, now run as a single sequence.

The targeted accessibility end-to-end tests still cover tapping and scrolling on their own.

Differential Revision: D122614304

fbshipit-source-id: b638fa8890cc6a16c5cc987a4e330878dc4117d2

Feature the highest-value demos on the fbidb.io home page

Summary:
The home page now ends with three demos, rendered with the same transcript component as the demos page: `drive-an-app-from-injected-swift`, `spin-safaris-address-bar` and `read-web-content-in-safari`. A link leads to the demos page for the rest.

A demo run publishes all of its demos or none. So if a build has demos but is missing a featured one, that demo was renamed, and the build fails instead of quietly featuring fewer. A build with no demos, such as a local docs build, features none.

Differential Revision: D122614224

fbshipit-source-id: 15777aae1f9c402483883bd4f2b686d1e6c907e5

Land fbidb.io on the docs, with the sidebar, in place of the video page

Summary:
fbidb.io now opens on the idb overview with the docs sidebar showing, instead of a landing page built around an out-of-date demo video. The docs are served from the site root (`/idb/...`, `/idb-repl/...`) rather than under `/docs/`. The landing page, its stylesheet and `idb_demo.mov` are removed.

Every old `/docs/...` URL redirects to its new path, so existing links keep working. `/docs`, `/docs/overview` and `/docs/idb/overview` go to `/`. The READMEs that link into the site point at the new paths.

Differential Revision: D122614090

fbshipit-source-id: 46bbe41d4caff55e39cf2a5e88d0bb53c45215e8

Demo crashing an app and reading its report

Summary:
Adds the `crash-and-read-the-report` demo. `idb-repl` injects Swift into `ReplHost` that schedules a `fatalError` and returns, so the REPL prints its result before the app dies. The demo then waits for the simulator's crash report, lists it with `idb crash list --bundle-id`, reads it with `idb crash show`, and deletes it with `idb crash delete`.

The report records the crashing thread's frames but not the `fatalError` message, so the demo checks for the closure the injected Swift scheduled (`closure #1 in userCode_0()`) and the `EXC_BREAKPOINT` trap, and marks both in the published output.

Differential Revision: D122614009

fbshipit-source-id: 780212a902d9f9c07eee79e885e213497192a886

Delete simulator crash reports whose path is redacted

Summary:
`idb crash delete` now removes a simulator app's `.ips` report when macOS has redacted the executable's path in it, as a current macOS does (`/Volumes/VOLUME/*/ReplHost.app/ReplHost`). Previously the report was listed but never deleted, and `crash delete` reported deleting nothing.

Simulator prune scopes reports to the simulator by its udid. That udid used to be looked for only in the executable's path. A report is now also the simulator's when its coalition is `com.apple.CoreSimulator.SimDevice.<udid>`, which the `.ips` parser now records on `CrashLogInfo` as `coalitionName`. Another simulator's report, redacted or not, is still left alone.

Differential Revision: D122613888

fbshipit-source-id: 7ebc9854d4929322f32d7b906bf64383a114da20

Pin simulator crash reports that delete misses when their path is redacted

Summary:
No behavioural change. Pins `crash delete` leaving a simulator app's `.ips` report behind when the report does not show where the executable lives.

A current macOS redacts `procPath` in a simulator app's report (`/Volumes/VOLUME/*/ReplHost.app/ReplHost`), so the only place the simulator's udid appears is the report's `coalitionName`, `com.apple.CoreSimulator.SimDevice.<udid>`. Simulator prune scopes reports to the simulator by looking for the udid in the executable path, so it deletes none of them. The report is still listed.

The pinned assertion is marked `BUG` and is flipped in the following commit. A second test pins that another simulator's report with a redacted path is left alone, which the fix must keep.

Differential Revision: D122613790

fbshipit-source-id: b04e519f677f3b06d0b91709527f9e2f4873056d

Report a crashed app's bundle id

Summary:
`idb crash list` now reports the bundle id of a crashed simulator app, and `--bundle-id` finds its `.ips` report.

- The JSON crash report parser identifies a report by `bundleInfo.CFBundleIdentifier`, falling back to the metadata's `bundleID`, and only then to the process name. Previously it always used the process name, so `idb crash list --bundle-id com.example.App` returned nothing for an app's report, and a filter on the process name worked instead.
- The companion's crash responses set `bundle_id` from that identifier. It was never set, so every report listed with an empty bundle id, including plain-text reports whose `Identifier:` was already parsed.

A report with no bundle id, such as one from a command-line process, is still identified by its process name.

Differential Revision: D122613659

fbshipit-source-id: fb516eeb8496695f92f19b6017d4694b46e0ecfd

Pin crash reports that lose their app's bundle id

Summary:
No behavioural change. Pins two places where a crash report's bundle id is lost between the report and the client.

- A simulator app's `.ips` report records its bundle id twice, as `bundleID` in the metadata and as `bundleInfo.CFBundleIdentifier` in the body. The JSON parser ignores both and uses the process name as the identifier, so `idb crash list --bundle-id com.example.App` does not find the report. The new fixture is shaped like the report a simulator on a current macOS writes, including the redacted `procPath`.
- `CrashLogInfoValueTransformer` never sets `bundle_id` on the response, so `idb crash list` prints an empty bundle id for every report, whichever format it came from.

Both assertions are marked `BUG` and are flipped in the following commit.

Differential Revision: D122613552

fbshipit-source-id: 9566e4733505f7ca574f4379937d536462797b70

List and delete crash reports written after a simulator's first crash request

Summary:
On a simulator, `idb crash list` read the host's crash reports only on the companion's first request, so a crash after that was never listed, and polling for a new report could never succeed. `idb crash delete` only forgot reports that had already been read, and left their files behind, so a deleted report came back the next time the companion started.

Both now match what a device already does:

- `crash list` reads the reports again on every request. `crash show` still uses the reports already read.
- `crash delete` reads the reports first, then removes the files of the simulator's reports that match. Reports from other simulators are left alone.

Differential Revision: D122613435

fbshipit-source-id: 0970d9bcfb3ba0932f569b4e0b5bd7d9631a17db

Pin simulator crash reports that list and delete miss

Summary:
No behaviour change. Pins two gaps in a simulator's crash-log commands, so the following commit reads as a flip of these assertions:

- `crash list` reads the simulator's crash reports only on the first request, so a crash after it is never listed.
- `crash delete` only forgets reports already read, and leaves the report's file behind.

A third test holds what must not change: deleting a simulator's reports leaves another simulator's alone. The commands take their crash log store as an argument, so the tests point it at a temporary directory rather than the host's.

Differential Revision: D122613182

fbshipit-source-id: 7fcf38382d9610f1501a021ce1eff0c31034a640

Demo one screen across display settings

Summary:
A new demo, `one-screen-across-display-settings`, checks one screen in dark mode, at an accessibility text size and with increased contrast, without relaunching the app:
- `idb-repl` injects Swift into `ReplHost` that shows a screen reporting the appearance, text size and contrast it is drawn with, and rereads them whenever one changes.
- `idb set appearance dark`, `idb set content-size accessibility-extra-large` and `idb set increase-contrast enable` change one setting at a time, and `idb ui describe` reads the screen after each.
- At the larger text size the label is taller than it was, so the font followed the setting.
- `idb get content-size` reads the setting back; the test uses the same command to restore the settings it found.

Reviewed By: bryanyantx

Differential Revision: D122613116

fbshipit-source-id: 3bc5168753900c7bec85b9589c9eaa19e77fc584

Describe a simulator's displays once a fold settles

Summary:
`describe` issued while a foldable simulator is changing display now reports the displays it settles on, rather than reporting none. A hinge change moves layout to the new display before its backlight follows; the displays read now waits that out, up to the same 5 second limit that display routing already uses, and only reports no displays if the change outlasts it.

The displays read and display resolution share one settling loop over the display report, so `resolveDisplay()` is unchanged.

___

Differential Revision: D122847289

fbshipit-source-id: 84db48e7431e8d2d7835c0e41c5f37a3970fb819

Inject DTUHID waits through a sleeper protocol instead of a closure

Summary: No behavioral change. `SimulatorDTUHIDConnection` takes a `DTUHIDSleeper` instead of a `DTUHIDClock` wrapping a `sleep` closure. Production passes `TaskSleeper`, which calls `Task.sleep(for:)` exactly as `DTUHIDClock.live` did. The type only ever slept and never read the time, so it is named for what it does. Tests pass a `RecordingSleeper` (recorder plus optional gate) or a `NoSleep` fake instead of building closures.

Differential Revision: D122986675

fbshipit-source-id: e543dcde009547f26a5f4605bc8ed42cb8f6ed55

Read expensive describe details through Target

Summary:
No behavioral change. `describe` now asks the target for the details that take asynchronous work to read, rather than casting to a concrete target type to read them itself.

`Target.details(_:)` takes a set of `TargetDetailKey`s (`diagnostics`, `displays`) and returns each requested detail as `unsupported`, `read` or `failed`. Only cancellation throws. Targets get every requested detail as `unsupported` by default:
- a `Simulator` reads its displays, as the platform-neutral `TargetDisplayDescription`;
- a `Device` reads its diagnostics.

`describe` maps each result to the wire exactly as before: a display read that fails is logged and leaves displays empty, a target without diagnostics reports empty ones, and diagnostics that fail to read fail the request. `SimulatorDisplay` construction and the display listing become internal to FBSimulatorControl again, and `IDBCommandExecutor.diagnostic_information()` goes away.

___

Differential Revision: D122847288

fbshipit-source-id: acda28c454121240037b88059e89d4395e69746d

Turn on keyboard auto-minimization when enabling the hardware keyboard

Summary: `idb set hardware-keyboard enable` now hides the software keyboard on a freshly created simulator. Before, the setting was written but apps kept showing the software keyboard, because they also need the keyboard daemon's `AutomaticMinimizationEnabled` preference, which a new simulator lacks. Enabling now writes that preference (`com.apple.keyboard.preferences`) before writing the attached state. Disabling is unchanged and leaves the preference alone, since the attached state alone brings the software keyboard back.

Differential Revision: D122806151

fbshipit-source-id: 0a9c96160a117e6a13d290eef4b04c40efcd287a

Pin that enabling the hardware keyboard writes only the attached state

Summary:
No behavioral change. Writing the hardware keyboard setting is now an explicit list of steps, so what accompanies the write can be tested without a simulator.

On a freshly created simulator, enabling the hardware keyboard has no visible effect: apps keep showing the software keyboard. Apps hide it only when the hardware keyboard is attached and the keyboard daemon's `AutomaticMinimizationEnabled` preference (`com.apple.keyboard.preferences`) is on. A new simulator has no value for that preference, and the daemon only turns it on when it sees the keyboard attach while an app's software keyboard is up.

The new tests pin today's behavior: enabling writes only the attached state. That assertion is marked as a bug and is flipped in the following commit. Disabling is covered too and stays unchanged.

[internal] Derive which cops the plugin template's RuboCop config drops (#30337)

prepare_rubocop_config listed fastlane's own cops by hand, so a new cop in internal/rubocop broke `fastlane new_plugin`'s rubocop until it was added there, and plugin_generator_spec only reported `expected 0, got 2`. The list is now derived from the cops the internal requires define, checked by a dedicated spec, and the plugin spec prints RuboCop's output on failure. The generated file is byte-identical.

[ci] Enable Security/Open (#30336)

* [ci] Enable Security/Open

Its 9 offenses were not exploitable: two Kernel#open on paths fastlane builds itself become File.open, and seven URI.open on https URLs or URI objects become URI.parse(url).open, which is what URI.open does for them.

* [match] Spec the GitLab secure file download

It had none, and the previous commit changes how it opens the URL.

* Remove offense count comment

[spaceship] Say why Apple refused to sign in, and send the refused sign-in once (#30320)

* [spaceship] Say why Apple refused to sign in, and send the refused sign-in once

A 403 from Apple's sign-in, e.g. for a locked Apple ID, became AccessForbiddenError: with_retry sent the same sign-in five times, then showed "Access forbidden" without Apple's serviceErrors message. It now raises UnexpectedResponse, as do_sirp does for signin/init, and preferred_error_info shows the serviceErrors. The 403 branch in send_shared_login_request was unreachable. See #14387.

* [spaceship] Only treat a 403 from Apple's sign-in as a refusal

The two-factor requests to idmsa.apple.com keep AccessForbiddenError and its retries: no 403 with serviceErrors has been seen from them.

[docs] Add AGENTS.md, testing instructions for specs, and a code-review skill (#30334)

* [docs] Add AGENTS.md, testing instructions for specs, and a code-review skill

AGENTS.md points every agent at the checks CI runs and at Design.md and Testing.md. Copilot code review also reads the instructions scoped to specs and the code-review skill. Tried on #30329 and #30330.

* [docs] Say what to do about a security problem without a private channel

fastlane has no SECURITY.md and private vulnerability reporting is off, so neither an agent nor a contributor can report privately: don't describe it publicly, and a review only flags that a maintainer's security review is needed.
[docs] Testing.md: a spec for a fix has to fail without the fix (#30333)

[docs] Add Design.md, the conventions action changes are reviewed against (#30332)

How options are declared and validated, and the limits of FastlaneCore::Configuration a change should not work around in one action. Linked from CONTRIBUTING.md.

[ci] Let RuboCop read its target Ruby from fastlane.gemspec (#30326)

RuboCop 1.91 reads required_ruby_version whatever the checkout directory is called, so .rubocop.yml no longer sets TargetRubyVersion. The spec now asks RuboCop for the version it targets.

[ci] Upgrade RuboCop to 1.91.0 (#30325)

* [ci] Upgrade RuboCop to 1.91.0 and rubocop-performance to 1.27.0

rubocop-performance is now loaded as a plugin, and Naming/PredicateName is renamed Naming/PredicatePrefix. The rubocop-ast deprecation warnings deferred in #30053 no longer appear.

* [match][precheck][produce] Fix the offenses RuboCop 1.91 finds in already-enabled cops

Two files used OpenStruct without requiring ostruct, and produce assigned App.create's result to a variable it overwrote on the next line.

* [ci] Record the offenses of the cops RuboCop 1.91 adds in .rubocop_todo.yml

40 cops, 537 offenses, generated with --auto-gen-config --exclude-limit 15 and appended so the existing entries stay as they are.

* [ci] Load rubocop-performance as a plugin in the plugin template's RuboCop config too

prepare_rubocop_config still listed it under require:, so every generated plugin printed RuboCop's plugin migration warning.

[match] Stop the change_password spec writing to the developer's login keychain (#30328)

It stored and deleted a match password in the default keychain through the real Encryption::OpenSSL. The same two lines are in #30304.

returns the first assignment it meets, consulting the deployment layer
(openmaic.yml, locked) before the workspace layer at every node. An
explicit null disables the subtree; nothing assigned up to the root is
unassigned, with no fallback to any vendor. The result carries the
provider, preset, registry entry, effective base URL, key, model, call
options, fallback, where it was resolved and whether it is locked, and

catalogue (met, unmet or unknown).

commits.message:
refactor(dtype): unify the dtype configuration of policies (#4786)

* feat(configs): make PreTrainedConfig.dtype a real torch.dtype

`dtype` was a bare string that every policy had to convert back into a
`torch.dtype` at its own call site. Nine such converters had drifted apart:
they disagreed on which dtypes they accepted and on what an invalid value
does — `ValueError`, `KeyError`, or a silent fall-through to a different
precision. Nothing in the base class owned the conversion, so each new
policy reinvented it.

Declare the field as `torch.dtype | None` and teach draccus the type once,
through the codecs registered on `PreTrainedConfig`. The on-disk form is
unchanged: `config.json` still stores the plain name `"bfloat16"`, and
`--policy.dtype=bfloat16` still works, so no checkpoint changes shape.
Names resolve against `torch` itself rather than a hardcoded allow-list,
so aliases such as `half` and any dtype a future torch release adds are
supported for free. Strings remain a serialization detail — the Python
API takes the `torch.dtype`.

Per-policy dtype restrictions are kept, with their literals translated;
they encode which precisions a policy was actually validated at, which the
base class cannot know. MolmoAct2's optimizer grouping, for one, still
assumes parameters are either bf16 or not.

Over 1458 in-place phrasings, 10610 of 上报, 上线, 下线, 升级 or 更新 followed by a docs word and 2752 checksum phrasings it joins the same ones as c6d922a8, over 19098 of 就 before a docs noun starting with 地 and a docs word the same ones as 7d891c9a (where ICU itself leaves 地 alone, as in 就地区域), and no index token changes over 19741 strings. perf(docs): bound the text icu reads after a chinese whole word

Finding the word that the characters after a whole word start segmented all the text after it, for each whole word ICU splits, so a long query took time growing with the square of its length: 就地址 repeated to 2000 characters took 45ms to tokenize (now 4ms), to 6000 375ms (now 8ms), and a search for 1800 of them, a 16KB URL, 48ms (now 6ms). ICU now reads the next 16 characters, from which it finds the same word: no index token changes over 19741 strings, no segment changes over 200000 texts with 就地 or 校验和 between pieces of docs text up to 60 characters long, and over 60000 runs of docs text up to 80 characters long ICU finds the same first word from the first 6 characters as from all of them. The longest word ICU finds in the docs, 地理位置, has 4 characters.

fix(docs): join chinese whole words only where the words after line up

c6d922a8 read 就地 (in place) where ICU joins its 地 to the characters after if those characters, taken from it, start a word, which also held where 就 (as for) comes before a word starting with 地: ICU finds 区分 at the start of 区分组, so 能否就地区分组 (能否, 就, 地区, 分组: can servers be grouped by region) lost 地区 and found only the in-place section instead of the two server grouping ones, 就地区内的服务器 put the server grouping section 43rd instead of first, and 那就地区内的节点 found 24 results instead of 44. Where both readings make words, as in 迁移后就地区间延迟变高 (地区, 间: the latency between regions got higher after the migration), 就地 and 区间 are still read. No index token changes over 19741 strings, all 630 checksum phrasings tried still join, as do the same 1580 of 1600 in-place ones (ICU keeps 就地取材 whole), and the new route check fails on c6d922a8.

fix(docs): let the current page's link stand in before a toggle

A control of the sidebar left with no copy to take focus, as a link of the page tree after a change of language while the search dialog is open (7f0b034a) or the header's drawer toggle once the window is widened past 48rem, gave focus to a sidebar toggle, where Space hides the sidebar, while the table of contents already lets its links to the headings in view stand in. fix(docs): give focus back to the title link across the header

The header shown above the page while the sidebar is a drawer holds the sidebar's title link, but the search dialog did not count it among the parts of the page showing the sidebar's controls, so focus on the header's title link fell to the page once the window was widened past 48rem while the dialog was open, and focus on the docked sidebar's went to the header's drawer toggle once the window was narrowed, beside the header's own title link. fix(docs): tell controls apart by their label before their text

6dc35929 finds a control of the sidebar again in its other part by its kind, link, label and text, but the drawer's language button shows the language beside the icon that the docked sidebar's shows alone, under the same label. Focus on it, or on an option of its menu, went to the sidebar's collapse button once the window was widened past 48rem while the search dialog was open, where Space collapsed the sidebar, and focus on the docked one went to the header's toggle once the window was narrowed with the drawer open. A control is now told by its label where it has one, and by its text otherwise.

fix(docs): join chinese whole words that icu splits across words

7d891c9a joined 校验和 and 就地 only where consecutive segments ICU finds spell them, but ICU also takes the 就 of 就地 into the word before, as in 也可就地升级 (也, 可就, 地, 升级), 然后就地升级 and 不就地升级, and its 地 into the word after, as in 就地上报 (就, 地上, 报): 也可就地升级 put the in-place section 41st instead of first, and 就地上报 and 就地上线 found nothing. A whole word is now read wherever the text holds it and ICU splits it, if ICU ends a segment with its last character or the characters it joins to that one, taken from it, still start a word, as 上报 does and the 址 of 就地址变了 (then the address changed) does not; 就地址变了, 就地区, 那就地图, 成就地位 and 就地震 still leave 就 and 地 apart, and no token of the index changes. Route checks require 也可就地升级 to find the in-place section first and 就地上报 to find what 就地 上报 finds. 7d891c9a also says 就地 found 66 sections before c40919ab: Orama found 69, of which fumadocs showed 66, at most 8 a page, 86 results with their 20 pages.

fix(docs): switch the sidebar to its drawer at the css breakpoint

fumadocs picks the drawer with a media query in px, (width < 768px), while the header holding the drawer toggle and the docked sidebar switch at Tailwind's md breakpoint, 48rem, which follows the browser's default font size. With a larger default font, as Chrome's Large (20px) or Very large (24px) font size, widths from 768px up to 960px or 1152px showed the header and its toggle but neither the drawer nor the docked sidebar, and since a3605cbe the toggle then said it had expanded a drawer that was not there, with an aria-controls naming no element, which axe flags. fix(docs): tell a sidebar link by where it was when the search opened

twinsOf asked a control with closest() whether it was in the sidebar once the dialog closed. A change of language while the dialog was open, as on Back after the language menu, keeps the sidebar mounted but takes each link of its page tree off the page on its own, since fumadocs keys the tree by its root, whose id carries the locale. The link then had no sidebar around it, nothing stood in for it, and focus fell to the page instead of going to a sidebar toggle as twinsOf's comment says. openerOf now records the parts of the page holding the element and each popup control while they are still on the page, so the docked sidebar's 故障排查 link on the Chinese page comes back as Collapse Sidebar after Back to the English one. The gap came with db29af99 and outlived the rewrites of twinsOf since.

fix(docs): let the table of contents stand in when focus comes back

A link of the table of contents focused before the search opened had no twin, so a resize that hid it while the dialog was open dropped focus to the page: the table of contents sits beside the page on a wide screen and in a popover above it otherwise. The table of contents now has places as the sidebar has. The docked list and the popover hold the same links, so a link of the popover comes back as the docked one once the window is widened, and the popover's button, or else the docked links to the headings in view, stand in where no copy is shown: the button for a docked link once the window is narrowed, the docked links for the button once it is widened, and the links of the page Back went to for a docked link of the page it left. The sidebar's parts and toggles become places of the same kind.

fix(docs): give focus back to its copy across the drawer and sidebar

A drawer link focused before the search opened, with the window widened past 768px while it was open, came back to the docked sidebar's Collapse Sidebar button, so the next Space collapsed the sidebar: the drawer is gone at that width, and copiesOf looked for a copy only in a sidebar with the same id that had mounted again. copiesOf now looks in every part of the sidebar, the docked sidebar, its floating panel and the drawer, for a control of the same kind, link and name, whether the control itself is still on the page or not. The drawer's Capabilities link now comes back as the docked one, scrolled into view in the sidebar, and its theme toggle as the docked theme toggle. Narrowing the window still gives focus to the header's Open Sidebar button, since the copy in the closed drawer cannot take focus.

fix(docs): bring focus given back into view where a scroller hides it

restoreFocus tells the browser not to scroll a control that is on screen, and isOnScreen only compared the control with the window. A sidebar link that Back, Forward or a remount of the sidebar moved under the sidebar's footer or header, inside the window but outside the sidebar's scroller, so counted as on screen, and focus came back to a link no one could see: Capabilities after Back to the quick start sat at y 876 under the footer, and Configuration Reference above the scroller after Forward. isOnScreen now asks whether the middle of the element is in view, in the window and in each element around it that clips what overflows it, up to one fixed in the window. A link that its scroller hides, or shows only a sliver of, is scrolled back into view in the sidebar alone, and the page still does not move when nothing changed under the dialog, since the same test decides whether the element was on screen when the dialog opened. This completes the claim of d8ea418f that focus on screen stays on screen, which held only for the window.

fix(docs): join chinese whole words only from the words icu finds

c40919ab cut 就地 (in place) out of the text before ICU split it, wherever 就 came before 地, so 就地址变了 (then the address changed), which ICU splits into 就, 地址, 变 and 了, was left with 就地 and the characters 地 and 址, and found nothing where 地址变了 finds the IP change section; 就地区 and 那就地图 found nothing either, and a page saying 就地址 would have lost 地址 from the index. A whole word is now joined only from consecutive segments ICU finds that spell it, which keeps 就地升级 and 校验和 whole and leaves 就 and 地址 apart, and a route check requires 就地址变了 to find what 地址变了 finds. c40919ab also says 就地 found 86 sections with the in-place one 54th: it found 66 sections, 86 results with their pages.

fix(docs): give focus back to its control in a sidebar that mounted again

The docked sidebar mounts again when the window is narrowed past the breakpoint and widened back, or after Back and Forward through the landing, and an element of the old one is no longer in the page. Since db29af99 such an element stood for a sidebar toggle, so focus on a sidebar link, the theme toggle or the language menu went to Collapse Sidebar, and the next Space or Enter collapsed the sidebar. The search now gives focus to the same control of the new sidebar, found by its kind, link and name, and only failing that to a sidebar toggle.

fix(docs): let the drawer toggles stand in when the search gives focus back

Focus went back to a search button wherever one was shown, but a sidebar toggle, or another control of the sidebar, stood only for the toggles of the docked sidebar, so focus fell to the page whenever a resize across the narrow breakpoint while the search was open swapped the docked sidebar for the drawer, or back, and when Back closed the drawer holding the focused link. The drawer's toggles, which now name it and say whether it is open, stand in too, and the header's is recorded as the control of the open drawer.

fix(docs): tell whether the sidebar drawer is open on its toggles

The buttons that open and close the sidebar drawer of a narrow screen, in the header and in the drawer, named neither the drawer nor whether it was open, so a screen reader heard a button that changed its name, and nothing could tell them from other buttons. The patch ports what later fumadocs releases give them: aria-expanded, aria-controls naming the drawer, and type=button.

fix(docs): scroll focus given back by the search as the browser does

887c79d3 scrolled the element given focus back to the middle of every scroller holding it, so for a link in the sticky sidebar or table of contents, which only their own scroller can move, the page behind them jumped too: 361 px when Back while the search was open scrolled the sidebar away from its link. Focus now scrolls the element into view itself, which centers it only in the scrollers it is out of view in, the same in Chrome, Firefox and Safari, and still only if it was on screen when the dialog opened and no longer is.

fix(docs): keep the kind of sidebar focus the window gives back

The browser fires focusin on the focused element when the window or tab gets focus back, and the patched sidebar sorted focus again there by the last input. A link clicked in the peeking sidebar, then a key such as Shift, then a switch to another tab and back, made the link count as keyboard focus: it moved to the panel's toggle as the sidebar slid away, and Space expanded the sidebar, the failure 704c9fcf fixed. The element focused when the window lost focus now keeps its kind when it gets focus back.

fix(docs): count a tab with a modifier as keyboard input in the sidebar

The patched sidebar left pointer input in force through keys held with Alt, so Option+Tab, Safari's default key for reaching buttons and links, gave focus that counted as the pointer's after any earlier click. Since 704c9fcf a collapse trigger reached that way and pressed with Space or Enter dropped focus to the page as it hid itself, instead of moving it to the trigger shown. A Tab now counts as keyboard input whatever modifiers it carries; Ctrl+Tab and Cmd+Tab never reach the page.

test(docs): cover the chinese adverbs for all and still in search

No route check failed with 都 (all) or 还 (still) taken out of the filler words, so nothing held b7decae6 to them. 都离线了 (all went offline) must now find what 离线 finds, and 服务器还在线吗 (is the server still online) what 服务器在线 finds; joined to the characters ICU splits 离线 and 在线 into, they found nothing.

fix(docs): keep the chinese word for in place whole in search

b7decae6 made 就 (then) a filler word, and ICU splits 就地 (in place) into 就 and 地, so the one section saying it, on upgrading a widget in place, lost the 就 from the index, and the query 就地 was left with 地, which starts 地址 and 地理: it found 86 sections with that one 54th, and 就地更新 lost it. 就地 is now kept whole like 校验和, and the route checks require the section first for 就地.

test(docs): correct what the uninstall search checks show

abac8ad0 said the sections holding the rarer 卸载 score more and come first, but most of them come after sections holding Agent, the heading 卸载与清除 14th. The section scoring most, the widgets page's 卸载 heading, holds 卸载, and the checks show that sections holding as many of the words are ordered by score.

fix(docs): leave adverbs out of chinese search queries

Adverbs of one character, 也, 都, 还, 又, 再, 就 and 才 (also, all, still, again, again, then, only), and 并 (and) match the start of any word, as a character alone does, so a section had to hold a word they start: 并不可用 found a section holding 一并 and 不可达 rather than the one holding 不可用. They also joined the characters ICU splits the next word into, so Agent 又离线了 (Agent went offline again) looked for 又离线 and found sections about Agent rather than about going offline, and the question word 为何 (why) did the same, so 为何离线 found nothing. They are filler words now.

fix(docs): stop chinese search reading unavailable as available

After 都 (all), 也 (also), 并 (and) or 为何 (why), ICU takes the 不 (not) of 不可用 (unavailable) into the word before and leaves 可用 (available), so 都不可用 found the sections about what is available. A word now starts at 不可用, which ICU then splits into 不可 and 用 as elsewhere.

fix(docs): center focus the search scrolls back into view

4a73692d scrolled the element given focus back to the nearest edge of the window, where Firefox left it a fraction of a pixel out of view. It now goes to the middle, where Chrome, Firefox and Safari bring an element they focus.

fix(docs): tell sidebar focus by how it arrived

68ba886a told pointer focus by the last input, so a key pressed after a click, such as Shift, an arrow key or Space while the collapsed sidebar peeked out, made the link the click had focused count as keyboard focus: it moved to the panel's toggle as the sidebar slid away, and the next Space expanded the sidebar. Focus is now told by the last input before it arrived, or by a press on it, and keeps that. Focus a pointer gave in a popup opened from the peeking sidebar goes back to the popup's control, which closes the popup, and falls to the page with the sidebar as it slides away, so that Tab goes on from the sidebar, as after a click on a link, rather than from the panel's toggle, which focus passed through to close the popup. The popup's control is also looked for from the focused element itself, as focus can be on a popup.

fix(docs): stand a twin in for any opener that cannot take focus

Closing the search tried the same control in the other half of the sidebar only for an element in the inert half, so focus fell to the page when what could not take focus was a popup's control there, as for the language menu opened from the peeking sidebar, which slides away under the dialog, or an element a resize hid, as the header's search button once the window is wide enough to dock the sidebar. Each element and control that cannot take focus now stands for its search button or sidebar toggle wherever one is shown.

fix(docs): give focus back through every popup that closed

The search gave focus back to the control of the popup holding the focused element, looked up from the element's parent, so focus on a popup itself, as on the page actions menu, whose items are links Radix does not focus, fell to the page, and a popup inside another, as the language menu in the 404 page's mobile menu, gave focus to its control, which had closed with the outer one. The element's own id is now looked up too, and the popups holding each control up to the outermost, and focus goes to the innermost control that takes it.

fix(docs): scroll focus given back into view only if it was on screen

c458cdd0 let focus scroll the element it went back to into view, so a reader who had scrolled away from the focused link before pressing Cmd/Ctrl+K was carried back to it when the search closed. Focus now goes back without scrolling, and the element is scrolled into view only if it was on screen when the dialog opened and no longer is, as after Back.

fix(docs): tell pointer focus in the sidebar by the last input

05a9b968 took focus matching :focus-visible for keyboard focus, but in Chrome a control focused by keyboard still matches it once clicked, so tabbing to the collapse trigger and then clicking it moved focus to the panel's toggle, and Space then expanded the sidebar again. The patched sidebar now records whether the last input was a pointer press or a key press, as the focus-visible heuristics do, and moves focus only after a key press: the collapse trigger, the peeking sidebar and a popup opened from it all follow the reader's last input rather than the state of the focused control.

refactor(docs): look only for the control of an open popup

The sidebar toggles name the sidebar in aria-controls, so the control the search dialog recorded for an element in the sidebar was a toggle, reached only after the element's twins had failed to take focus. The control must now also carry aria-expanded=true, as popover, menu and collapsible controls do while their popup is open and the sidebar toggles never do, which is also how the sidebar patch finds it.

fix(docs): close a popup opened from the sidebar as it slides away

The language menu opened from the collapsed sidebar as it peeked out stayed open when the sidebar slid away, mostly off screen and holding focus, so on a Chinese page Space chose English. When the half of the sidebar holding an open popup's control is hidden, focus now leaves the popup, which closes it: keyboard focus moves to the same control in the half shown, the sidebar toggle for the language menu, and focus a pointer gave falls to the page. The control is the element naming an ancestor of the focused element in aria-controls and carrying aria-expanded=true, which the sidebar toggles do not carry. This completes aff160af, which moved focus only from the controls inside the hidden half.

fix(docs): hand sidebar focus over only when the keyboard gave it

When the collapsed sidebar slid away, or a collapse trigger hid itself, focus on a control of the hidden half moved to the same control in the half shown, also when a click had given it: after clicking a link in the sidebar as it peeked out, or the collapse trigger, Space expanded the sidebar instead of scrolling the page. Focus now moves only from a control that matches :focus-visible, and focus a pointer gave falls to the page as the browser leaves it.

fix(docs): scroll the element given focus back by the search into view

Focus went back without scrolling, as Radix returns it to a trigger, but the page can move while the dialog is open, as when Back returns to a scroll position from before a fragment, so the focused link could end up far off screen. Focus now scrolls the element into view when it is not, and leaves the page where it is otherwise.

fix(docs): return focus to a popup's control when the search closes

Focus went back to the element focused before the search dialog opened, but a popup holding it closes once focus moves into the dialog or a click lands outside it, and takes the element with it: the sidebar's language menu, the mobile menu of the 404 page, and the table of contents on a narrow screen. Focus fell to the page body, so the next Tab started from the top. The dialog now also records, when it opens, the control that names a popup holding the element as the popup it controls, and focuses it if the element is gone. This completes 3d17b867.

test(docs): cover the chinese use verb after a question verb

用 (use) stays a word after a character alone only if that character is not a filler word itself, so the 用 of 能用 Nginx 吗 (can I use Nginx), where ICU splits 能用 into the filler word 能 and 用, is a filler word too. The comments said a character alone, and no check failed when the filler word 能 counted as the character before 用. 能用 Nginx 吗 must now find what Nginx finds.

test(docs): require a ranking check to compare sections

The check that sections holding more of a query's words come first passed whenever every section held as many of them, as when the fallback returned only the sections holding the most words, or when a page came to hold all of them and the first search found them. It now also requires sections holding different numbers of the words.

test(docs): check that the chinese fallback orders sections by score

The uninstall queries only had to find the deployment page, which they did with the sections in any order, so neither dropping nor reversing the score that orders the sections holding as many of the words failed a check. Their first section must now hold 卸载, the rarer word, and the comment no longer says that 服务端 and 卸载 sit in a heading and the paragraphs under it.

fix(docs): search a repeated chinese query word once in the fallback

The fallback searched each word of a query as often as it was typed, and counted each time as another word held, so in Docker docker 升级 回滚 the sections holding docker came before those holding 升级 and 回滚, where the first search reads docker once. A word is now searched once however often it was typed, compared by its tokens, so a word typed in another case is the same word.

fix(docs): keep the chinese word for unavailable in search terms

ICU splits 不可用 (unavailable) into 不可 and 用 too, and the 用 there follows a word, not a character alone, so the filler rule dropped it and 不可用 was searched as 不可 (cannot): 存储不可写, 不可达 and 不可编辑 came before the sections saying 不可用, and 预设目标不可用 found only one section. 用 now also stays after a word ending in the 可 of 可用 (available).
