fix(docs): index the pieces of the chinese word for checksum too

Keeping 校验和 (checksum) whole made it one token in the index, while a query for 校验 (validation) is still split into 校 and 验, and 验 starts no word of the section about checksums, so 校验, 升级 校验 and 核对 校验 lost that section, the one on checking a release's assets after a failed upgrade. A whole word's pieces, less its filler word, are now tokens too, so 校验 finds it again, while 校验和 still finds only that section. The route checks cover both.

test(docs): check that each checklist label holds its checkbox and text

The check passed whenever a task item started with a label opening on a checkbox, so a label around the checkbox alone, which leaves it unnamed, still passed. Each task item now has to hold one label, with its only checkbox inside and text beside it.

test(docs): require chinese text for the search dialog's own labels

The search dialog's close button name and result count lived in the dialog component, outside the translations check-contracts reads, and appear only once the dialog is open, where no route check sees them, so an English string left in their Chinese entries would have passed CI. They now live beside fumadocs-ui's translations in src/lib/ui-translations.ts, and check-contracts requires Chinese text in each.

fix(docs): keep focus when the collapsed sidebar peeks out

Pointing at the edge of the page slides a collapsed sidebar back in and hides the floating panel, and moving away does the opposite. Whichever half is hidden is inert, so focus on the panel's buttons, or on a control of the peeking sidebar, fell to the page body and the next Tab started over from the article. The patched sidebar now hands focus to the same control of the half shown: its search button, or else its sidebar toggle. The collapse trigger's handoff uses the same helper.

fix(docs): give focus back when the search dialog closes

fumadocs opens the search dialog without a Radix trigger, and Radix hands focus back to the trigger, so closing the dialog with Escape or its close button left focus on the page body. Focus now goes back to the element focused before the dialog opened, unless a result was chosen. When the dialog was opened from the docked sidebar while it was peeking out of its collapsed state, that half turns inert once the pointer leaves, so focus goes to the search button or sidebar toggle of the floating panel instead, skipping the header's search button, which is hidden beside the sidebar.

fix(docs): keep a language change from announcing the shown results

The status also followed the language, and a change of language starts a search, so going back or forward between /en and /zh with the search dialog open during a search announced the count of the results still shown, in the new language, before the new search ended. The language is now read when results arrive.

fix(docs): announce the result count again on returning to a query

fumadocs' fetch client answers a query it has searched before with the array it got then, which React takes for the results already shown, so typing a character and deleting it while its search ran, or after it failed, left the status cleared under results on screen, and the count was never announced again. Each search now gets a copy of the cached results.

docs(docs): say which pieces of the search misses the pages hold

The comment said that pages hold 企业, 微 and 信, the pieces ICU splits 企业微信 into. No page holds 企业 or 微, and 信 only starts other words, such as 信息.

fix(docs): rank chinese fallback results by the words they hold

The fallback said it put the sections holding more of a query's words first, but it ranked them by their summed scores, so a short section holding one word came before a long one holding two: for 告警 通知 邮件 (alert, notification, email) a section with all but one of the words came last on its page. Sections holding more of the words now come first, and those holding as many by score. The route checks cover the order on each page and the order of the pages.

fix(docs): keep the chinese word for checksum whole in search

ICU splits 校验和 (checksum) into 校, 验 and 和, and the conjunction filler dropped its 和 from the index and from queries, so 校验和 found every section that 校验 (validation) finds, 23 of them, with the one about checksums last. 校验和 is now kept as one word. This also corrects dd15319d's message, which said that no docs word loses a character to the conjunction fillers.

fix(docs): drop the chinese verb for use unless it ends a word

Keeping 用 (use) as a word for the sake of 已用, 调用 and 复用 also kept it in every question built with it, so a section had to hold a word starting with 用 to match 可以用 Nginx 吗, 怎么用终端 or 用 Docker 部署, and the Nginx headings, the terminal page's introduction and the limits of a Docker deployment dropped out. 用 is now a filler word unless it follows a character alone, which is where ICU leaves it from the words it splits, and the fallback searches each word as typed, so that 已用 keeps its 用. The route checks cover both.

fix(docs): end a chinese query word at a filler word

The fallback joins a character that ICU leaves alone to the word before it, but it dropped the filler words first, so a character after a filler joined the word before the filler: 服务端怎么卸载 was searched again as the one word 服务端卸载, and 流量和带宽 as 流量带宽, both the words the first search had not found together, and both found nothing. A filler word now ends the word before it. The route checks cover both queries.

test(docs): check every chinese label, also those shown after a click

The route checks read the aria-labels of three Chinese docs pages as the server renders them, so a missing or English translation of a label that appears only after a click, such as the sidebar triggers' Close Sidebar and Expand Sidebar, or an English label on any other page, passed. The Chinese interface text moves to src/lib/ui-translations.ts, check-contracts requires a Chinese translation for every fumadocs-ui key, and check-routes reads the labels of every Chinese docs page in the sitemap.

fix(docs): label task checkboxes up to the first block in their item

The label wrapped a task item only when all of it was inline, judged by tag name, but code blocks and tables reach the item as components, so a code block or table under a task's text ended up inside the label with its copy button, while a loose list item, the parent of a nested list or an item followed by a quote left its checkbox unnamed. The label now holds the checkbox and the inline content after it, up to the first block, and in a loose list it goes in the item's first paragraph. The route checks require a label on every checkbox of the deployment checklist.

fix(docs): outline the highlighted search result in forced colors

The result that Enter opens is marked only by its background, which forced colors replace, so in a Windows contrast theme nothing showed which result the arrow keys had reached. It now gets an outline in the system highlight color there.

fix(docs): keep hidden sidebar controls out of the tab order

On desktop docs pages the floating panel holding the expand button stayed in the tab order while invisible, and a collapsed sidebar kept its 35 controls focusable off screen, so focus disappeared for that many Tab presses. The patch ports the fix of later fumadocs releases: whichever of the two is hidden is inert, and a collapse trigger that hides itself hands focus to the other one.

docs(docs): say which url served the quick start for a decoded slug

The lookup found the quick start for %2571uick-start, but only the Markdown export served it: the page itself answered 500, as its content was then looked up under the slug as given. The comment named the page.

fix(docs): announce search results only once they arrive

fumadocs also stops loading when a search that a newer one replaced ends, with the older results still shown, so the status, which read the end of loading as the arrival of results, announced the previous query's count while a newer search was still running, up to three times on a slow link before the real count. The status now follows the results themselves and is cleared each time a search starts.

fix(docs): keep the search dialog's bottom border one pixel wide

The dialog draws a border under each of its parts but the last, which it takes to be the result list, and the screen reader status added after the list became the last part, so the list, or the header when the query was empty, kept its border on top of the dialog's own and the bottom edge was two pixels wide. The status now sits in the header.

fix(docs): leave conjunctions out of chinese search terms

A conjunction such as 和 stayed in a Chinese query as a word to find, and the fallback kept it with the word before it, so 防火墙和告警 found the 2 firewall sections that also hold a word starting with 和, where 防火墙告警 finds 14. 和, 与, 或, 及 and the longer conjunctions are now filler words. ICU leaves them apart in the docs only where they join words and keeps 参与, 以及, 及时 and 涉及 whole, so no docs word loses a character.

fix(docs): search a chinese query again for each word it holds

The fallback re-ran a Chinese query that found nothing for any of its tokens, and ICU splits words it does not know into characters that match the start of any word, so 区块链 and 企业微信, which no page mentions, returned 34 and 58 unrelated sections. It now searches each word the reader typed, and each word ICU finds in a run of Chinese with the lone characters it leaves kept with the word before them, and returns the sections holding any of those words, those holding more first. 卸载 Agent, 卸载agent and Agent卸载 still find the deployment page, 区块链 and 企业微信 find nothing, and the route checks cover both.

fix(docs): keep the chinese word for use in search terms

用 (use) was dropped from the index and queries as a question verb, but ICU splits 已用, 调用 and 复用 into a character and 用, so those terms became the single characters 已, 调 and 复, which start many other words, and the sections holding them no longer came first.

fix(docs): count each word of a chinese query once

Orama 3.1.18 counts a query word once for each word of a section it starts, and takes a section as a full match when that count equals the number of query words. With the threshold 0 of the Chinese index, a section holding server and serverbee matched server.toml, and a section holding every word, one of them in two forms, did not match. The patch counts the query words a section matches, in each of Orama's builds.

fix(docs): check every rule that sets the docs theme colors

The contrast check read fumadocs' dark colors and the first light override in app.css, so a dark override or a later light rule in app.css passed under the minimum. It now reads app.css and every stylesheet it imports in cascade order, merges each rule that sets the checked colors into the themes it applies to (light, dark, and the dark sidebar), and fails on a rule whose theme it cannot tell.

fix(docs): put the search listbox role on the element that scrolls

fumadocs puts the props of its result list on a wrapper, so the listbox role sat outside the element that scrolls. Accessibility checks then reported the scrolling results as unreachable by keyboard, which they skip for a listbox that a combobox controls. The patch moves the role and id onto the scrolling element; the arrow keys still move the highlight from the input.

fix(docs): name the search close button by what it does

fumadocs' search close button shows ESC and had no other name, so a screen reader announced it as "ESC". It is now named "Close search (Esc)" and "关闭搜索（Esc）", which keeps the key it shows for speech input.

fix(docs): keep a url's query as it came

TanStack Router parses search params as JSON, and on the server it redirects a request whose query does not serialize back the same, so ?v=1.10 went to ?v=1.1, ?q="x" to ?q=x, and a repeated param to a JSON array, also through the legacy redirects. The docs read no params, so the router now keeps them as strings.

fix(docs): stop redirecting paths with quotes or braces to themselves

On the server, TanStack Router redirects a request whose URL differs from the one it builds for it, and it built " < > ^ ` { } in a path unencoded. The browser encodes them again to follow the redirect, so /en/docs/x%22y and the like redirected until the browser gave up instead of answering 404. An identity rewrite makes the router build its URLs with the URL parser, which encodes them as the request's URL was; every other page renders the same HTML.

fix(docs): answer 404 for docs paths whose slug holds a percent sign

The router decodes a URL's slugs, and fumadocs decodes slugs that name no page once more, as Next.js passes them encoded. Decoding again threw on a lone %, so /en/docs/x%25y and its Markdown exports answered 500, and /en/docs/%2571uick-start served the quick start. The slugs are encoded before the lookup, which that second decoding undoes.

fix(docs): label the task list checkboxes

GFM renders a task list item's checkbox without a name, which accessibility checks report on the deployment pages' security checklists. A task list item whose content is inline now wraps it in a label, so each checkbox is named by its item's text.

fix(docs): let the keyboard scroll tables wider than the page

A table wider than the page scrolls inside its own container, which Safari does not make focusable, so it could not be scrolled from the keyboard there. The container takes focus while it scrolls, as fumadocs' code blocks do.

fix(docs): show keyboard focus on every docs control

fumadocs removes the focus outline of its controls. The mobile table of contents trigger showed no focus at all, and the buttons and code blocks mark focus with a box-shadow ring, which forced colors (Windows contrast themes) drop, so none of them showed focus there. They now draw an outline in its place.

fix(docs): raise light muted text and focus rings to aa contrast

fumadocs' light theme set muted text, which carries page descriptions, the sidebar, the table of contents and the 404 page, at 4.1-4.4:1 on its backgrounds, and the focus ring of its buttons and code blocks at 2.2-2.3:1. They now reach 4.5:1 and 3:1, and check-contracts.ts fails when either theme falls under them.

fix(docs): check heading links against the ids pages render

The anchor check derived ids with its own slugger, which read `#` comments in code blocks as headings, dropped underscores, collapsed repeated dashes and ignored case: of the 1078 heading ids the pages render, it missed 78 and accepted 166 that do not exist. It now uses fumadocs' own heading plugin, and fragments must match case.

fix(docs): keep chinese searches from coming back empty

A Chinese query needed every word in one heading or paragraph, so a question such as 升级失败怎么办 and words split between a heading and the paragraphs under it, such as 卸载 Agent, found nothing. Question words and the verbs questions are built with are no longer indexed or searched, and a query that finds nothing is searched again for any of its words, as English queries are.

fix(docs): load the landing search dialog on load in safari

Without requestIdleCallback the landing waited a fixed 2 s before loading the search dialog, so in Safari Cmd+K still lost the first keys typed in that time. It now loads once the page has.

fix(docs): announce the search result count

Nothing told a screen reader user that results had arrived or that there were none, so a query with no results was silence. A polite status now gives the count or the no-results message in the page's language.

fix(docs): keep search results out of the tab order

The results stayed tabbable buttons after they became listbox options. Tab moved focus onto an option while the highlight stayed elsewhere, so Enter opened a different result than the focused one, and Enter on the focused close button also opened a result. Options now take no focus, as the combobox pattern has it, and the close button keeps its Enter to itself.

ci(docs): run the docs checks when ENV.md changes

check-contracts.ts fails when ENV.md lists a variable the configuration pages omit, but docs.yml, the only workflow that runs it, did not run on an ENV.md change.

fix(docs): keep the page url verbatim in the ask-ai prompts

The translated prompts insert the page URL with String.replace, which reads $& and its siblings in the replacement as patterns, so a URL holding them changed the prompt. A replacer function inserts it as is.

fix(docs): translate the name of the 404 page's header

Radix names a navigation menu Main, and fumadocs renders the home layout's header as one, so the Chinese 404 page announced an English name. The route checks now fail on any Chinese docs or 404 page that names a control in English.

fix(docs): label the sidebar toggles by their state

The button inside the open mobile drawer closes it but was named Open Sidebar, and the floating button of the collapsed desktop sidebar expands it but was named Collapse Sidebar. They are now named by what they do: Close Sidebar and Expand Sidebar, in both languages.

fix(docs): give docs pages the share image alt text

Docs pages declare the landing share image but not its alt text, which the landing sends with it. The alt text moves to src/lib/site.ts, so both heads use one copy and the landing copy stays out of the docs bundle.

fix(docs): title 404 pages as missing pages

A 404 was titled with only the site name, so its tab, history entry and the title a screen reader announces did not say the page was missing. It is now titled like a docs page, Page not found | ServerBee Docs, in the language its content uses.
fix(docs): raise code token colors to 4.5:1 contrast
fix(docs): hide the github nav icon from assistive technology
fix(docs): give each docs page a main landmark
fix(docs): run the vercel function on node 24
ci(docs): pin node 24 for the route checks and watch the patches
feat(docs): publish a sitemap with hreflang alternates
fix(docs): redirect legacy and language-less urls, 404 unknown ones
fix(docs): localize the 404 page
refactor(docs): derive the page language from its path in one place
refactor(docs): share one docs language guard

fix(docs): keep the reader's scroll position across hydration and back

Hydration reset a page scrolled before it to the top, scroll-to-text matches included, and Back or Forward to an entry with a #fragment jumped to the fragment instead of where the reader was. The router now keeps a position scrolled before hydration, and fragment entries keep their key and skip the second jump. tests/manual/docs-scroll-restoration.md lists the flows to recheck after router upgrades.

fix(docs): route fumadocs fragment links and mark only the current page

fumadocs passes every internal href to the router as a path. A same-page heading link resolved to /<page>/#<id> and did nothing, and a cross-page one preloaded a page named <page>#<id>. Fragments now stay fragments or go to the router as the hash, and only the page itself carries aria-current instead of every link above it.

fix(docs): give each docs page its own head metadata

Every docs page shared the title ServerBee Docs and had no description, canonical, hreflang or social tags. Pages now carry their own title in their language, the description, a canonical URL with en, zh-Hans and x-default alternates, Open Graph and Twitter tags, and a link to the Markdown export.

fix(docs): split llms-full.txt by language in navigation order

/llms-full.txt held every page twice, once per language, sorted by file path and without page URLs. It now holds the English pages in sidebar order, each with its URL and description, and /zh/llms-full.txt holds the Chinese ones.

fix(docs): publish a valid llms.txt for each language

/llms.txt joined both languages under two H1s with no summary or sections and linked relative HTML pages, so llms.txt parsers found nothing in it. Each language now gets one file with a summary, an H2 section per sidebar group and absolute links to the Markdown exports; /llms.txt stays English and /zh/llms.txt is new.

fix(docs): keep section headings in markdown exports

fumadocs-mdx 14.2.9 serialized headings without their # markers, so exports and llms-full.txt had no structure. 14.2.14 fixes that but encodes some bold markers as *, which the export decodes again.

fix(docs): serve each page's markdown export in its own language

Copy Markdown and View as Markdown on Chinese pages delivered the English page. Exports now sit at the page URL plus .mdx, are sent as UTF-8, answer HEAD, and return a real 404 for unknown pages. The English-only /llms.mdx/docs URLs keep working and /docs/<page>.mdx redirects to the English export.

fix(docs): translate the docs ui labels into chinese

fumadocs-ui 16.6.16 hard-codes the sidebar, theme, search, code-copy and page-action labels in English. A bun patch routes them through its translations, and the Chinese pages now set every key.

fix(docs): show ctrl k as the search hotkey outside apple platforms

fumadocs switches the hint to Ctrl only for Windows user agents, so Linux and ChromeOS readers saw ⌘ K. Keep its
key matcher, and define the hotkey once so the keydown listener is not re-subscribed on every render.

fix(docs): load the landing search dialog when idle

The landing fetched the dialog chunk only when Cmd/Ctrl+K opened it, and the keys typed while it suspended went to
the page, so the first characters of a query were lost. Mount it closed once the landing is idle instead.

fix(docs): expose search results to screen readers

fumadocs' dialog renders results as buttons with aria-selected and keeps focus in the input, so the highlighted
result was never announced. Make the input a combobox that controls a listbox of options and points its active
descendant at the highlight, and keep the highlighted breadcrumb above 4.5:1.

fix(docs): keep card links out of the search index

remark-structure stringified each <Card> into a raw-JSX result that opened the page holding the card. The linked
page is already indexed under its own title.

fix(docs): tokenize chinese search with word segmentation

The zh index used Orama's English splitter, which treats every CJK character as a separator, so no Chinese query
matched anything. Segment with Intl.Segmenter, fold full-width forms and case, split dotted identifiers like the
English tokenizer, require every query word, and skip question words the pages rarely contain.

fix(watchdog): keep the node's output readable on non-English Windows

fix(watchdog): keep the node's output readable on non-English Windows

On Windows cardano-node writes its output in the console code page. A computer name with characters inside that code page produced invalid UTF-8 that the watchdog's line reader could not decode and stopped reading at, and a name with characters outside it made the node crash with a character encoding error. The watchdog now decodes the output lossily, reading bytes up to each newline, so invalid bytes are logged as U+FFFD and reading continues. Each read is bounded to 1 MiB, so a child that writes without newlines cannot grow the buffer, and a longer line is logged in consecutive chunks with no bytes dropped. End of stream ends the loop, and a genuine read error ends it with a warning.

The computer name reaches the node's output in two places: the host field on every trace line, and the application name in the startup configuration dump. The watchdog now sets TRACE_DISPATCHER_LOGGING_HOSTNAME to the fixed value daedalus in the environment of the node it spawns, overriding any inherited value and leaving the user's own environment untouched. The node configuration generated for every network and platform sets TraceOptionNodeName to the same value, and a flake check asserts it for each installer cluster. The startup and sync-progress parsers match on event text and do not read the host field.

commits.message:
Pico PIO USB Update (#1698)

* Pico PIO USB Update

* Fix hub hot-replug with upstream Pico-PIO-USB

Upstream 5a37a66 breaks re-enumeration of devices behind a USB hub after a
hot unplug/replug (PS4 auth dongles authenticate at boot, then never again
after being replugged through the hub). Root-port replug is unaffected.

Bisected on hardware (Haute42 COSMOX M-Lite, hub + PS4 auth dongle):
the regression is sekigon-gonnoc/Pico-PIO-USB 30283a9 ("Fix pre packet"),
specifically moving the RX state-machine enable from
pio_usb_bus_start_receive() (after the host's TX) into
pio_usb_bus_prepare_receive() (before it). 65708d3 passes, 30283a9 fails on
the first replug, and reverting only that enable placement passes; the other
two changes in that commit are innocent.

lib/pico_pio_usb now points at upstream 5a37a66 plus one commit that moves
the enable back after TX (device mode enables explicitly at init, so it is
unchanged). It lives on a personal fork (speedypotato/Pico-PIO-USB, branch
fix-rx-enable) pending the upstream PR against sekigon-gonnoc; maintainers
may prefer to mirror it to OpenStickCommunity/Pico-PIO-USB.

The single-PIO layout and the NeoPico move to PIO1 from the previous
revision are kept; they were verified not to be the cause (the failure
reproduces identically with the two-PIO layout).

Refs: sekigon-gonnoc/Pico-PIO-USB#149, hathach/tinyusb#2971

* Bump pico_pio_usb: second hub hot-replug fix (streaming devices)

The previous bump fixed hub hot-replug for idle devices (PS4 auth dongles).
Devices that transfer every frame (PS5/P5General controllers) still failed
to come back after being unplugged from a hub: the hub's port-change report
was never received, so no unmount/mount and no re-authentication.

Bisected on hardware to sekigon-gonnoc/Pico-PIO-USB 9be1f3e, which made
pio_usb_bus_start_receive() a header inline and added a read-back spin on
the RX IRQ flags. Restoring the pre-9be1f3e shape (out-of-line RAM function,
single flag write) fixes it. Both fixes together: PS4 dongle and P5General,
direct and through a hub, 10/10 replugs each on a Haute42 COSMOX M-Lite.

lib/pico_pio_usb -> speedypotato/Pico-PIO-USB fix-rx-enable @ ba9733c
(upstream 5a37a66 + 2 commits).

Refs: sekigon-gonnoc/Pico-PIO-USB#149

* fix(p5general): Filter host reports and time out lost completions

report_received() captured the next input report from any HID device
into hash_finish_buffer, which P5GeneralDriver then forwarded to the
console as the signed hash. With other dongles or controllers on a
hub, their reports were sent instead of the P5General's, so console
auth succeeded only intermittently. Only accept reports from the
bound dongle's dev_addr/instance.

The listener also advanced its state machine and cleared hash_pending
even when the tuh_* transfer was rejected (the host has a single
shared control slot), and P5GeneralDriver only accepts a new console
request while the listener is idle. A rejected or lost completion
(USBHostManager drops len == 0 failures) therefore left the listener
in a *_wait state, ignoring every later console request until replug.

- Advance state only when the transfer was actually queued.
- Return to idle after 500 ms in any *_wait state. A late completion
  is still ignored because each handler only acts in its matching
  wait state. Handling every enumerator also clears the -Wswitch
  warnings on this switch.

* fix(usbhost): Raise HID interface and device limits

CFG_TUH_HID caps HID interfaces across all devices, not devices. Auth
dongles often expose more than one HID interface, so a hub with four
dongles could exhaust the pool; find_new_itf() then returns NULL and
the surplus interface is silently never mounted, leaving the needed
dongle unavailable depending on enumeration order.

Raise CFG_TUH_HID from 4 to 8 and CFG_TUH_DEVICE_MAX from 4 to 6 so a
full 4-port hub fits with headroom for a dongle that re-enumerates
before its old address is released. Cost: ~1 KB of RAM (bss 140292 ->
141320 on Haute42COSMOXMLite).

* fix(ps4): Recover PS4/PS5 USB auth from lost transfers

The listener set awaiting_cb before issuing each GET/SET_REPORT and
ignored the result. When the transfer could not be queued (the host
has a single control slot, busy with the hub or other devices, or the
dongle had gone), or when it failed and USBHostManager dropped the
len == 0 completion, awaiting_cb stayed set and auth stalled until the
dongle was replugged.

- Only wait for a completion when the transfer was queued, and only
  advance nonce_page / nonce_chunk once their transfer is queued, so a
  rejected call is retried on the next pass.
- Time out a completion after 500 ms and restart the dongle exchange.
- Ignore completions that arrive when none is awaited. A defensive
  range check on nonce_chunk is added before indexing ps4_auth_buffer;
  it is not reachable with the single host control slot.
- On a signing error (state byte 1), abandon the nonce and wait for the
  console's next one instead of polling forever.
- Parse up to 32 report-descriptor entries when detecting a dongle; a
  full DS4-style descriptor lists 0xF3 well past the first four.

* chore(cmake): Fix ENV{CI} check for CMake 4.x

The optional Custom.cmake include tested `DEFINED ENV(CI)`, which is
not valid CMake syntax; environment variables use braces. Older CMake
tolerated it, but CMake 4.4 rejects the if() expression and configure
fails with "Unknown arguments specified".

* feat(ps4): Track dongle candidates; rebind on unplug, rotate on failure

The PS4/PS5 USB auth listener bound the first PS4-family (0xF3) dongle
and ignored every other one, so with several dongles on a hub the rest
were never used, even after the bound one was unplugged or stopped
responding.

- Remember every PS4-family dongle interface seen in mount(). When the
  bound dongle is unplugged, bind another one that is still connected.
- When the bound dongle fails repeatedly (3 consecutive completion
  timeouts, or 2 consecutive signing errors), bind the next connected
  dongle, skipping other interfaces of the same device. If the
  console's nonce is still intact the new dongle takes it immediately;
  otherwise wait for the console's next round. Each other dongle is
  tried at most once per console nonce, so two dead dongles cannot be
  rotated between forever.
- With nothing left to try, stop re-sending the current nonce and
  return to auth_idle_state until the console starts a new round,
  instead of retrying a wedged dongle every 500 ms.
- Wait 10 ms before re-polling PS4_GET_SIGNING_STATE after "not
  ready" instead of polling back-to-back.
- Request PS4_DEFINITION from process() for each newly bound dongle
  rather than from bind(): when bind() runs from unmount(), TinyUSB
  still holds the control slot for the removed device.
- Do not re-send the nonce after a timeout during signature readback;
  ps4_auth_buffer is already partly overwritten with signature data.
- static_assert that PS4_MAX_DONGLE_CANDIDATES covers CFG_TUH_HID.

The first dongle to enumerate is still the one bound at boot, and a
dongle that signs successfully but is rejected by the console (e.g. a
PS4-only dongle in PS5 mode) is not detected.

* build(tinyusb): Upgrade TinyUSB to 0.21.0

Move lib/tinyusb off the OpenStickCommunity fork of 0.17.0 to upstream
TinyUSB 0.21.0 plus one patch, on speedypotato/tinyusb
gp2040/0.21-ctrl-timeout:

- host: add control transfer timeout (upstream still has none, and
  Pico-PIO-USB retries NAKs forever, so one device NAKing a control
  request could stall the whole host).

Upstream now queues control transfers requested while the slot is
busy, releases a still-enumerating device when its port or hub is
removed, and drops stale control completions, which covers the rest of
the previous fork-only host fixes.

The OSC fork patches are no longer needed: interval override, host
SOF callback and the ep0 size fix only touch hcd_rp2040 (GP2040-CE
hosts on Pico-PIO-USB), and the device SOF callback and
tuh_get_hub_addr_port() are unused. "Don't force boot protocol" is
intentionally dropped: it reported every HID interface as

commits.message:
Merge pull request #2982 from square/shark-dive-harness-starts-the-agent

Have the harness start the investigation, and cut the skill to a pointer

Merge pull request #2983 from square/weak-hash-map-cleared-key

Read the value of a WeakHashMap entry whose key was cleared

Test the WeakHashMap cut set on the reader, not on a leak trace

"WeakHashMap with cleared key expanded" asserted the shape of a leak
trace whose leaking object the map was the only holder of, which made it
a race: anything else in the heap that reaches a stale entry offers a
competing path, and on CI something did, so the trace came back through
the entry's value field from a GC root rather than through the map. The
assertion it then failed is the one this change is about, which reads as
the fix not working when the fix is fine.

Assert on the reader instead. Flattening the map's references and
checking that the cut set holds the value, named and low priority, and
that the traversal of the internals never had to follow the entry's own
value field, is the contract the change is about, and no part of it
depends on what else in the heap reaches that value. It also states its
own premise — the key is cleared and the value isn't — so a GC that
didn't clear the key says so instead of failing somewhere downstream.

The leak trace test for an entry losing to the holder an application can
fix stays, since priority is a path finding behaviour and it passed on
CI. It now puts the trace in the assertion message.

findPathFromLeak returned the whole path when leakRoot wasn't on it,
because indexOfFirst returning -1 slices from 0, so a path through
something else was silently asserted about as though it went through the
structure under test. That's how the failure above read as a wrong
owning class rather than as a path through a different root. It now
fails with the trace in the message.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

Stop the harness staging a skill, restricting tools and pinning a model

Three things it was doing that it had no business doing, and one flag that was
doing nothing.

**It staged a copy of the skill and rewrote the paths in it.** With the skill cut
down to a pointer at `--help`, there is nothing left in it to carry: the prompt
names the launcher and the agent's own first move is finding out what it takes.
So the staging, the substitution and the check that the substitution still
matched the skill's prose are all gone — about seventy lines of machinery that
existed to keep a copy honest.

**It restricted the run to Bash and Skill**, copied from the eval without the
reason being copied with it. The eval restricts because it is scoring one number
and a run that reached a second heap dump tool would be scored on something
else. A harness is not scoring anything, and an investigation does not end at the
faulty reference — it ends at the code, so pulling sources, decompiling, reading
git history and compiling a check are part of the job. Full tool set now, with
permissions bypassed so it runs to the end unattended.

**It pinned opus.** A model name written down here is one that goes stale the next
time the default moves, so no --model is passed and the client stays on its own
default. --model is still there for pinning one deliberately, which is what the
eval does.

**And --strict-mcp-config was redundant, not load-bearing.** Measured: a session
on the default config directory here has 17 mcp__shark-dive__* tools — a whole
rival investigation surface, including open_heap_dump and conclude — and one on a
scratch CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR has none. The config directory was already doing that
job, so the flag is dropped here and the comment in run-eval.sh, which credited
it with work the config directory does, is corrected. It stays in the eval as a
second lock on the one contamination that would be scored as a pass.

Also documented, because running it twice is what found it: notes are kept per
heap dump under the shared ~/.shark-dive, so a second run on one dump is handed
the first one's conclusion by read_notes. Measured against
leak_asynctask_o.hprof, where the earlier note named the faulty reference
verbatim. SHARK_DIVE_DIR is how to get a blind run.

Verified both ways on that dump with no skill staged: 20 calls, none refused,
concluding MainActivity$2.this$0, and with a clean SHARK_DIVE_DIR the run read no
notes at all and reached the same answer.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

Cut the skill down to a pointer at the binary's own help

The skill was 154 lines and most of it was a second copy of what the build
already prints. `--help` names every command and opens with "Start with
open_heap_dump on the heap dump you were given", which was the skill's whole
first section; it covers --cli being required, --session, --run, --no-ui, hex
addresses, exit codes and the reason argument. `--investigation-help` and
`--leak-investigation-help` are the method.

A copy of that in a file describes the commands that existed when it was
written. The skill itself said so — "read that rather than trusting a list in a
file like this one, which goes stale" — while being the file in question.

So it is now where the launcher is, that --help is the rest, and why to prefer
those four texts over this page. The description stays as it was, since that is
the whole of what makes a client reach for it unprompted, and keeping the page
short is also what makes installing the app enough: nothing in it is knowledge
somebody has to remember to copy.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

Read the value of a WeakHashMap entry whose key was cleared

A WeakHashMap is read as one virtual reference per entry, from the map
straight to the value it maps, and the reader declares readsCutSet so
that FlatteningPartitionedInstanceReferenceReader folds the table and the
entries into the map instead of leaving them in leak traces. Entries
whose key the GC had cleared were skipped, which breaks that promise:
clearing a key doesn't clear the value, the map only drops the entry once
one of its own operations expunges the stale ones, so the table still
holds the value as strongly as any other.

Having been told there was nothing left to find, the flattening
traversal then followed the entry's value field itself and surfaced
everything reachable below it as if the map referenced it directly, each
object keeping the name and class of its real owner — a trace line
reading "java.util.WeakHashMap instance ↓ SomeClass.someField", for a
field WeakHashMap doesn't have, with the real holder gone from the trace.
Objects surfaced that way are also left unexplored, so a leak whose real
path ran through one of them was reported through the map instead.

The entry is now read like any other. Two decisions about how:

It's named "cleared key, removed on next map access" rather than after
the key, whose description is gone with it. A reader who lands on this
reference has nothing else to go on — no application code holds the
entry, and the next operation on the map removes it — so the name says
that rather than leaving them to work out why a WeakHashMap is holding
something.

It's low priority, so a leak trace reaches the value through any other
holder it has and only names the map when the map is the only thing left
holding it. An entry waiting to be expunged is rarely what someone wants
to be sent to fix.

The WeakHashMap tests all ran with flattening disabled, which is why none
of them caught this, and none used a cleared key. They can now turn
flattening on, and two do.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

Have the harness start the investigation, and the agent open the window

The harness staged a window and stopped, printing a command to paste. Which
meant the step an investigation is most likely to get wrong — opening the heap
dump — was the one step it never exercised, and the skill's whole first section
went untested. So it now stages and runs: the agent is given a file and opens
its own window, the way the eval already worked.

Five changes, and the one that makes the rest honest is the third:

- A directory per invocation, timestamp and pid, so two runs in a row or two at
  once don't land on each other. Nothing deletes the ones before it, unlike the
  eval: a window is launched from the bundle in one of these, and deleting it
  under a window kills that window.
- The staged bundle carries the timestamp too, since the dock reads a bundle's
  file name and two tiles called "Agent harness" are two windows nobody at the
  machine can tell apart.
- The staged skill is rewritten to name the copy this harness built. The shipped
  skill names /Applications and tells the agent to go looking, and this app is in
  neither place, so left alone an agent either finds nothing or — worse, and
  silently — investigates through a different build than the one just compiled.
  A grep afterwards is what makes that a failure rather than a bad measurement:
  if the substitution stops matching the skill's prose, the run stops.
- The prompt is one sentence naming the file. Not the method, not a tool, and no
  longer the launcher either, which the rewriting above is what buys: a prompt
  that names it works whether or not the skill ever loaded, and whether it loads
  from its description alone is a thing worth finding out.
- Claude is invoked by default and its output tailed back, with --print-command
  for driving a client yourself.

`--bare` was the obvious switch for "no memories, no local context" and it
cannot be used: it turns off skill auto-discovery along with everything else, so
the skill is reachable only by typing /shark-dive. A/B'd with a throwaway skill
whose description matched the prompt — discovered and followed without it, never
loaded with it. So isolation is a scratch CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR, which keys
auto-memory and leaves the person's own skills out, plus --strict-mcp-config for
MCP. What survives is ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md, and the comment in run-eval.sh
claiming CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR kept that out was wrong; it is corrected rather than
left to mislead the next reader of the eval.

Verified end to end on leak_asynctask_o.hprof: the skill triggered from its
description, the agent opened its own window, made fourteen calls with none
refused, and concluded MainActivity$2.this$0, which is that dump's answer.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

Merge pull request #2981 from square/shark-dive-desktop-java-17

Target Java 17 in the Shark Dive modules that only run on a desktop JVM

Target Java 17 in the Shark Dive modules that only run on a desktop JVM

`shark-dive-agent` calls `ProcessHandle`, which is Java 9, while taking the repo wide Java 8 target.
That built fine and always has: `targetCompatibility` without `options.release` compiles the
reference into Java 8 bytecode and resolves it at runtime, and no Java 8 runtime ever loads this
code. What it cost was the editor. IntelliJ checks API availability against the module's language
level, so every `ProcessHandle` call read as an error in a module whose declared target is a
contract with nobody — none of these modules is published.

So name the three desktop-only modules in the root build script instead of just the app, and let
`shark-dive-app` take its target from there rather than declaring the same thing itself.

`shark-dive-core` and `shark-dive-jdwp` stay on Java 8, which is the point of naming three modules
rather than the group: core has to stay loadable from the Android app, so a Java 9 API reference
there should still be an error in the editor.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Fetch the Gradle models in parallel again under Gradle 9.4

`org.gradle.parallel=true` stopped enabling parallel model fetching during IDE sync in Gradle 9.4;
it covers task execution only now, and Android Studio reads `org.gradle.tooling.parallel` for sync
from Quail 1 on. Without it, syncing this repo's modules is serialized, which is what Studio's
"enable parallel sync for this project" prompt is about.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Merge pull request #2980 from square/no-shark-dive-changelog

Delete the Shark Dive change log, which has never had a release to log

Merge pull request #2979 from square/hprof-file-associations

Open .hprof files with Shark Dive

Open .hprof files with Shark Dive

Double clicking a heap dump in Finder, Explorer or a Linux file manager now
opens it in Shark Dive, as does Open with → Shark Dive.

Two halves, and only the first is the same everywhere. The declaration is
`associateHeapDumpFiles()` on each `nativeDistributions` platform block, which
becomes `CFBundleDocumentTypes` in the macOS bundle, a registry entry in the
`.msi` and a MIME type with a `.desktop` entry in the `.deb`. The delivery is
argv on Windows and Linux, which `DiveArguments` already takes, and on macOS an
Apple Event that reaches `HeapDumpAssociation` through
`Desktop.setOpenFileHandler` — a running app is sent nothing else, so without it
a dump double clicked while Shark Dive is up does nothing at all, and one
double clicked while it is down opens a second copy of the app showing nothing.

A dump the OS hands over goes to the window already reading it, raised, rather
than to a second window on the same gigabyte: someone in Finder cannot see what
this app has open, so a double click names a heap dump. That is the rule
`goToHeapDump` and an agent's `open_heap_dumps` already followed, and
`windowShowing` is now the one declaration of it the three of them share.

What was measured, since none of it can be tried from `run`, is in

Merge pull request #2978 from square/cli-only

Redesign Shark Dive's command line around --cli, one run, and a named heap dump

Replace a file in one step, so a reader never finds it missing

The `checks` job of this pull request failed on one test and nothing else —
`LeakStatusSectionTest > keeping the new status flips every status that disagreed
with it`, with a `FileNotFoundException` for the statuses file out of
`shark/shark-dive/shark-dive-core/src/main/java/shark/dive/LeakStatusFile.kt:41`,
reached from the `waitUntil` at
`shark/shark-dive/shark-dive-app/src/test/java/shark/dive/app/LeakStatusSectionTest.kt:182`.
A read that had just passed `if (!file.isFile)` opened a path that had gone.

The gap is `Files.move`'s, not the test's. With `REPLACE_EXISTING` and nothing
else, a move onto an existing path is two syscalls: `unlink` of the target, then
`rename` of the save in flight onto it — `sun.nio.fs.UnixCopyFile.move`,
`java.base/sun/nio/fs/UnixCopyFile.java:444-473` of the JDK 17 `src.zip`, where
the delete at line 457 and the rename at line 473 are plainly apart. Between them
the file does not exist, and the window writes those files from the IO dispatcher
while the test thread, another window, a `--cli` command or somebody's editor
reads them.

So `ATOMIC_MOVE`, which is a single `rename(2)` and replaces the target in one
step. Measured both ways with a reader spinning beside a writer, 20000
replacements each: 7891 reads opened a file that had gone without the option, and
none with it. `HeapDumpFilesTest` is that measurement at 2000 replacements, which
fails without the option and takes a fraction of a second; it also pins the two
things this function already promised, that the whole text is what comes back and
that writing nothing deletes the file.

Nothing in the change log: this is `shark-dive-core`'s own writing, and every
entry of `docs/shark-dive-changelog.md` is still the initial release.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Answer with nothing but the answer, and name an open heap dump by a key

A review of the redesign, and the thread running through most of it is that an
answer was carrying things that were not the answer.

**Both halves of the method are printed rather than answered with.** `SURFACE`
was prepended to the first answered call of every session, so a
`list_heap_dumps` that wanted the name of a dump was handed the whole of how to
work here — and the session that only ever wanted that paid for the rest of it.
It is now `--investigation-help` beside `--leak-investigation-help`, both text
this build prints with no run, no heap dump and nothing open. Measured on
`leak_asynctask_o.hprof`: a first `open_heap_dump` answers 1,976 characters
where it answered 3,802, and another session's first `list_leaks` answers 6,495
where it answered 8,435. What carries the pointer instead is the answer that
opens a heap dump — the first call of nearly every investigation, and so the one
answer a session that has read nothing is certain to see.

**An open heap dump is named by a `heapDumpKey`.** It was `heapDump`, which read
as the dump itself rather than as the name of it, and the parameter every other
command takes is now spelled the same as the field an answer hands back. Two
files of one name — `crash.hprof` pulled off two devices — used to leave the
second unnameable, since the name resolved to whichever was opened first: a call
meant for one answered about the other with nothing saying so. The second is now
`crash.hprof#2`. A key says what is open right now, so closing the first of two
leaves the survivor under the plain name, and a session holding `#2` across that
close is refused rather than answered about the wrong dump; the path a dump was
opened as resolves too, and is the spelling that doesn't move.

**A `reason` is required of a named session and of nothing else.** It was
required of every call, which refused a person typing one command at a window
for the sake of a log nobody is going to review. `--session=` is what an agent
passes and the reason is what makes that session readable afterwards, so having
both or neither is the whole of it. The schemas still require it, since what a
model reads is the schema.

**A wait is only ever for a run this command line started.** There was a blind
ten seconds in front of every command — measured at 10.4 seconds for a
`list_heap_dumps` with nothing running — and what it bought was saying nothing
before saying what was already known. A run publishes itself as it starts and
that file goes away three ways as it ends, so a run that is up is a run that is
listed, and polling for one to appear is only a bet that one is in the middle of
starting. Worth making when this command line started it, and nothing otherwise.

**Three commands may start a run**, where only `open_heap_dump` could:
`dump_heap` and `list_devices` join it, which is the same rule read properly —
a command whose answer says nothing about what a run had open answers the same
in a run it just started. `list_heap_dumps` stays out, because what it answers
*is* what the run has open. So `--no-ui` goes with those three.

**`conclude` takes `reason` and no `rootCause`.** They were the same sentence
asked for twice: `reason` is why a call was made, and on `conclude` the call is
the conclusion. Two fields that want one answer get half an answer in each, so
there is one, and its description says what belongs in it — what assigned the
faulty reference, what should have cleared it, and why it didn't.

**And `show` is refused by a run with no window** rather than answering that it
showed you something it could not show anybody. The refusal carries the
`shark://` link, so whoever has a screen opens what was being looked at.

The help's opening line said the window was the thing and the heap dump was
whatever it had open; it now says what the app does, which is open heap dumps
and answer commands about them, in a window or with no window at all.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Publish a run by a rename, and delete only the file of a run that has ended

A `--no-ui` run logged itself as published, the command line that had just
started it never saw the file, the file was gone afterwards, and the run stayed
alive and unreachable for the rest of its life — a JVM holding a heap dump
nothing could ever ask about again, while the command that started it waited its
full sixty seconds and then reported that something had gone wrong opening it.

Nothing but the command line reads that directory, so what deleted the file was
the poll that read it in the moment between its creation and its contents, found
no `port` in it, and cleared it out as a file naming no run.

Both halves of that are worth changing. `AgentServer.write` now writes the file
under a name that does not end in `.agent` and moves it onto the name readers
watch, so a half published run is never in the list. And a file naming a process
that is still running is left where it is, whatever is in it: the two reasons one
might not parse are being written right now, and being written by a build older
than one of these properties — and the second is a run its own build's command
line can still talk to, so deleting it takes a live run's address away from the
one thing that could use it.

Measured after: five `--no-ui` opens in a row, all answered, 1.6 to 2.6 seconds
each, and a command against `~/.shark-dive` cleared out the four files of runs
that had ended while leaving the one a live run of an older build had published.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Redesign the command line around --cli, one run, and a named heap dump

`--agent` is gone, and with it every rule that made the surface two surfaces.
The old shape picked the most recently started run and said which it had
picked, took a window identifier for the case a heap dump name couldn't
answer, carried the leak method on `list_leaks`'s answer, and answered "what
can I do" with `--agent-help` beside a `--help` that listed everything else.

What replaces it:

- **`--cli` on every command**, required rather than inferred from a command
  name arriving, so a command line either says it is a command or is a run of
  the app opening windows and nothing has to guess which. `--cli` with nothing
  after it prints the same text as `--help`.
- **One run, or an error naming them.** Runs are filtered to the build sha of
  the launcher that made the call, and two left is a refusal listing them and
  asking for `--run=<pid>` — not `--agent-run`, since the surface is written
  for agents and typed by people.
- **Two ways in.** `open_heap_dump` and `list_heap_dumps`; every other command
  takes `heapDump=<file name>`. The window identifier is gone from the command
  line, because opening a dump that is already open joins that open, so a name
  is never ambiguous within a run.
- **`open_heap_dump` starts a run when there is none**, detached so it survives
  the command that started it, and blocks until the dump can be read. It is the
  only command that starts one, and with `dump_heap` the only one with a wait
  worth planning for.
- **`close_heap_dump`**, which closes the window too, and ends the run when it
  was the last dump open.
- **`--no-ui` only on `open_heap_dump`**, since it picks the kind of run to open
  a dump in rather than anything about one dump, and a mismatch is refused both
  ways round.
- **One help.** `--help` is every command with a line each and points at opening
  a heap dump; `--help <command>` is one in full; `--leak-investigation-help` is
  the method, which `list_leaks` now points at rather than carrying. Measured,
  that last move cuts `list_leaks` from 14,477 characters to 6,481.
- **`--session=`**, which an agent is expected to pass with its own session id
  in it, so that a reviewer reading the agent's logs can find the investigation.

Every rule above is verified against a packaged build rather than reasoned
about, and the measurements — including the three detaching routes and what
each leaves the run's ppid, pgid and session as — are in
shark/shark-dive/notes/agent-surface.md.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Answer --help, and serve agents from a run with no window

Two ways an agent arrives at this app that answered badly.

`--help` and `-h` were not options, so both fell through to
`DiveArguments.parse` and came back as `Unknown option --help` followed by
a usage line naming `--title` and the heap dumps and no agent option at
all — printed after `installLogging()` had put the JVM, the heap limit and
the log path over it, and exited 0. So the single most likely command a
program that has only been handed a launcher can type answered that this
surface does not exist, successfully. `DiveHelp.kt` is both spellings,
answered before any logging, naming the window's half of the command line
and the agent's, and pointing at `--agent-help` for the tools themselves.
Reading the command line moved out of `installLogging` with it: one that
genuinely doesn't read is now a line on stderr and a failing exit code.

`--no-ui` went with the MCP server, and comes back as a run rather than a
transport. The MCP version served the tools from the bridge process with
no window and no `<pid>.agent` file, so an MCP client was the only thing
that could reach it; this one opens no window and publishes the same
socket a window's run publishes, so `--agent` reaches it exactly as it
reaches a window and nothing on the calling side knows the difference.
`HeadlessAgentHeapDumps` is the whole of what differs — which dumps are
open, what opening one means, and `show` handing back a link and saying it
had nowhere to put a tab. The notes, the verdicts and the sessions are the
same files a window reads, so a dump investigated over ssh today opens in
a window tomorrow with all of it on. A call that also says `--no-ui` is
refused with the two commands to type, rather than having the word
stripped and quietly ignored.

And `agent_log` says what it is for. Its description opened with what has
already been done to this heap dump, which reads as the way to take up
earlier work; it is somebody else's transcript, for working out why an
investigation went the way it did. What an earlier reader found is
`read_notes`, and what the dump says shouldn't be in memory is
`list_leaks`.

* fix(latex): try Windows-1252 before Latin-1 when decoding sources

Latin-1 decodes any byte sequence, so the cp1252 fallback listed after it
never ran. A source saved as Windows-1252 (\usepackage[cp1252]{inputenc})
came out with C1 control characters in place of curly quotes, the euro
sign and dashes. The two encodings differ only in bytes 0x80-0x9F, and
the five of those that Windows-1252 leaves undefined still fall back to
Latin-1.

Collecting the files a TikZ picture needs read each \input dependency as
strict UTF-8. An 8-bit dependency failed to decode, so the files it
inputs in turn were never staged for Tectonic, and a picture that relies
on them fails to compile. Read dependencies with decode_latex_content,
the same decoding used for the main file.

commits.message:
Harden `:w !cmd`

Bound the wait for stdin with WaitDelay, so a child left behind by the
command, as with `:w !tool &`, can't freeze the UI. Pass the command line
to cmd.exe as is, with /S /C, since exec.Command's quoting breaks cmd.exe
quoting. Report a command killed by a signal as "signal: interrupt" rather
than "shell returned -1". Share the "written" message between :w to a file
and to a command. Tests pin SHELL to sh and skip on Windows.

Add `:w !cmd` to pipe JSON to a shell command, remove `v` key

`:w !cmd` feeds the JSON on screen, the query result if one is applied,
to the command's stdin, as in vim: `:w !less`, `:w !vim -`, `:w !code -`.
The command runs through `$SHELL -c`, so quotes and pipes work, and takes
over the terminal while it runs. `:wq !cmd` quits once the command
succeeds.

The `v` key, which opened the input file in `$EDITOR`, is removed;
`:w !vim -` covers it and also works for stdin and query results.
Add `--dungeon` to known flags

perf(qwen4): fused attention rows, unrolled verify tiles, deferred GDN states, MoE top-k fold (#4052)

* perf(qwen4): unrolled row-exact tiles for the DeltaNet verify projections

Verify blocks of 2..8 rows run the stacked in-projection and the
out-projection on a fully unrolled copy of the row-exact tile with
per-block-size tiles (R=4: 4 columns x 2 rows in, 2 x 4 out). Each
accumulator keeps its order, so every row still has the one-row qmv_fast
bits. Tiles stay inside a register envelope (16 accumulators, 80 input
values per lane): past it the M5 Ultra compiler produced wrong bits.
OMLX_QWEN4_GDN_VERIFY_TILES=0 keeps the rolled tiles.

* perf(row-exact): unrolled variant of the same-input group kernel

_group_kernel(..., unrolled=True) compiles the grouped launch on the
unrolled tile (same bits inside unrolled_tile_ok's envelope) for callers
that pick their own tiles.

* perf(qwen4): defer the DeltaNet verify's per-step rollback states

The fused verify wrote the recurrent state after every row but the last
(S-1 x 3 MB per layer, 9.4 MB at S=4) on every window, while a commit
reads at most one of them and only on a partial accept. Those writes
also held DRAM bandwidth from the following projections.

The verify now records a 'deferred' slot instead: the final state, the
entry state and a recomputation of the fused step on the first m rows,
which the ArraysCache commit patch runs only when it keeps 0 < m < S rows
(row t's arithmetic does not depend on the block length, so the state is
bit-identical to the one it replaces). The block's other outputs are
unchanged. OMLX_QWEN4_GDN_VERIFY_DEFERRED_STATES=0 writes the states.

* perf(qwen4): fused attention rows for decode and row-exact verify windows

Below the QSA block budget a decode row and every row of a row-exact
Lightning MTP verify window now run in five launches plus the cache
appends: q/k/v/index_qk in one row-exact qmv launch, the q/k RMS norms and
MRoPE in one, MLX's vector SDPA plan of each row (one pass below 1024 keys,
two passes with 128 partitions from 1024) with the gate multiply in two, and
o_proj. The one-pass key chains run spread over the GPU and meet in a
second launch for MLX's closing reduction; every row of a window keeps the
plan of its own serial step, in one launch pair. Masked decode rows and
masked verify windows past the budget use the fused projections, norms and
MRoPE around the unchanged selection and selected-keys SDPA.

Same float operations in the same order: bit-identical outputs and cache
state (tests at real shapes, FP32 kernel checks). OMLX_QWEN4_ATTN_FUSED=0
keeps the MLX ops.

* perf(qwen4): unrolled row-exact tiles for fused attention verify rows

The grouped q/k/v/index_qk launch and o_proj of verify windows take the
unrolled tile (2 rows x 4 columns per simdgroup for even row counts, 1 x 4
for odd) through quantized_linears_tiled's new unrolled flag, inside
unrolled_tile_ok; one decode row keeps the rolled 1 x 2 tile. Same one-row
qmv bits for every tile (checked R=1..8).

* fix(qwen4): fused attention rows only for quantized q/k/v/index projections

_fused_projections_ready passed the four projections to row_exact_qmv's
grouped plan, which reads each linear's bits, so a dense (unquantized)
attention layer raised AttributeError on its first decode step instead of
keeping the MLX ops. Check QuantizedLinear first.

* perf(qwen4): fold the MoE router top-k into the gate+up launch

One-token decode and verify windows of up to three rows select their
experts inside the gate+up launch: its first block stores the row's
indices and scores (the down launch reads them) and every expert
simdgroup recomputes the selection it serves from the router logits with
softmax_topk_row's arithmetic. The block runs three dependent launches
instead of four. From four rows on the recomputed selections cost more
ALU than the routing launch saves, so wider windows keep it.

The bf16 selection packs each probability with its expert index into one
integer key (ties to the highest index, NaN never selected) and keeps
each lane's three largest keys, so a selection is one simd_max. The
standalone softmax + top-k launches use the same selection; FP32 test
instantiations keep the per-lane scan.

The router gemv runs one simdgroup per (expert, row), so a window has as
many simdgroups per row as one-token decode and keeps its arithmetic.

Bit-identical to the served kernels at R=1..8. OMLX_QWEN35_MOE_TOPK_FOLD=0
keeps the separate routing launch.

* fix(row-exact): check each unrolled tile against stock quantized_matmul on the running GPU

The unrolled row-exact tiles stay inside a register envelope measured on
M5 Ultra, but an M3 Ultra computes 4-bit gs64 tiles inside that envelope
with whole rows wrong. The first launch of each unrolled shape now runs
once on a fixed input against stock one-row quantized_matmul of the same
weights; a shape with any differing bit runs the rolled tile (same
geometry, same arithmetic) from then on, with a warning.

perf(engine_pool): stop the unload settle barrier when the gauge plateaus (#4162)

The settle barrier in `_unload_engine` polls 10 times at 0.5s and then
runs a 3-round emergency reclaim, but it only breaks early when the
gauge settles or another engine is serving. A model whose footprint
plateaus just short of the required freed amount measures the *same*
value every round, so all 10 rounds elapse and the 3s reclaim follows —
a ~10s shutdown hang that repeats on every quit (#2757, reported as
freed=27.39GB against need>=27.63GB on every one of ten rounds).

Two consecutive rounds measuring the same non-zero freed amount with a
settled footprint ledger means gc/synchronize/clear_cache are no longer
releasing anything, so the remaining rounds cannot succeed. Bail there
and skip the emergency reclaim, which is three more cycles of exactly the
work that just proved it is a no-op. Recovery is unchanged: the
accumulator is still decremented unconditionally, the enforcer re-poll
is still woken below, and pre-load admission still re-reads the live
gauge (#1623) — the same two nets the concurrent-activity bail relies on.

Scoped to the reported shape on purpose:

- `actual_freed > 0`. Memory was returned and merely fell short. A gauge
  pinned at exactly 0 is a different situation and keeps the full barrier
  and its reclaim, so those diagnostics are untouched.
- `not footprint_pending`. Metal can return arrays before macOS updates
  the phys footprint ledger, and admission reads both. Bailing while the
  ledger lags is what makes an immediate settings reload fail 507, so
  that case keeps waiting.

Fixes #2757

fix(bonsai): add the mlx wheel rpath to the bonsai kernel extension (#4155)

Every other custom kernel extension links `-Wl,-rpath,
@loader_path/../../../mlx/lib` so the installed extension resolves the mlx
wheel's `libmlx.dylib` from the packaged site-packages layout. bonsai shipped
with only `@loader_path`, leaving the sole libmlx rpath pointing at the
link-time absolute path into the build environment. That path is dead after
install, so a venv or wheel install failed to import bonsai with `dlopen:
Library not loaded: @rpath/libmlx.dylib` and the kernel silently reported
`available: false` through `GET /api/status` while the other four kernels
loaded from the same install (#2233 fixed the others, #2822 is bonsai).

The regression test parses each kernel's CMakeLists for the relative rpath, so
a kernel added or edited later is covered without needing CMake or a
`--with-custom-kernel` build.

Fixes #2822

fix(scheduler): clear SpecPrefill state after failures and cache rejects (#4035)

* fix(scheduler): release SpecPrefill state when decode fails or cache corrupts

The engine stopped admitting requests after a SpecPrefill request failed
mid-decode or hit cache corruption. Neither fail_all_requests nor
_recover_from_cache_error released the active SpecPrefill id or the offset
RoPE patch, so _schedule_waiting kept deferring every request, including the
corruption retry of the SpecPrefill request itself.

Both paths now call _cleanup_specprefill, as abort and generation-overflow
recovery already do.

A retried SpecPrefill request (cache corruption and generation overflow) now
prefills densely. Its indices and position offset were scored against the
pre-reset cache state: after a prefix-cache hit they index the uncached
suffix. The reset sets cached_tokens to 0 and does not re-run scoring, so the
retry fed those suffix-relative indices into a sparse prefill of the full
prompt and forwarded the wrong tokens at the wrong positions, with no prefix
KV. _reset_request_for_reprefill now drops the indices, the same fallback
used when sparse prefill fails.

* fix(scheduler): drop SpecPrefill indices when a restored prefix cache fails validation

SpecPrefill scores a request while its prefix cache is being prepared, so
the selected indices are relative to the uncached suffix and the RoPE offset
is the restored cached_tokens. When _validate_cache then rejected the
restored cache, the fallback reset the request to prefill the full prompt
from position 0 but kept specprefill_indices. The sparse path applied the
suffix-relative indices to the full prompt, so the wrong tokens were
prefilled at the wrong positions, with no prefix KV and no error. Scoring
does not run again for that request, so nothing corrected it.

The fallback now clears specprefill_indices, and the request is prefilled
densely. specprefill_position_offset is only read when indices are set, so
it is left alone.

The regression test stores a prefix on a tiny hybrid model through the
paged SSD cache, rewrites the stored block so its recurrent layers carry a
different slot count than the live model, and checks in a second engine
session that the rejected restore is followed by a dense prefill of the
full prompt.

* fix(grammar): skip thinking budgets without a reasoning phase

fix(tool-calling): limit parameter tag repair to tool-call payloads

Also moves the #4008 and #4129 tests onto the real qwen3_coder parsers with a shared tokenizer helper, and drops the parser-detail README line.

fix(tool-calling): keep Qwen parameters whose open tag lost its '>' (#4008)

The Qwen templates delimit a parameter as `<parameter=name>value</parameter>`.
Models occasionally emit a parameter with an empty value as

    <tool_call>
    <function=bash>
    <parameter=proxy=
    </parameter>
    ...

with no `>`. mlx-lm's qwen3_coder parser runs `match_text.index(">")` over that
payload and raises `ValueError: substring not found`. The per-match XML fallback
then recovers the call but silently drops the malformed parameter, so the client
receives a tool call with an argument missing and nothing in the response says
so -- and when the malformed tag is the only parameter, the fallback returns
`{}`, losing the argument list entirely.

`repair_parameter_open_tags` rewrites the two malformed spellings
(`<parameter=name=` and `<parameter=name` with nothing between the name and the
next close tag) back to the template's `<parameter=name>` before any parser sees
the payload: the native qwen3_coder path, the per-match XML fallback, the
standalone XML fallback and the qwen recovery scanner. Only the open tag is
touched, and only in that shape -- no argument bytes are inferred, so
`<parameter=name>value</parameter>` stays byte-identical, which makes the pass
idempotent and cheap enough to run at each entry point.

Tests cover the missing-`>` payload through both the native and XML paths, plus
idempotence on well-formed tags.

repos.name: lovyan03/LovyanGFX
repos.description: SPI LCD graphics library for ESP32 (ESP-IDF/ArduinoESP32) / ESP8266 (ArduinoESP8266) / SAMD51(Seeed ArduinoSAMD51)

commits.message:
Merge pull request #952 from ainyan03/release_1.2.32

Release 1.2.32
Bump version to 1.2.32

Bus_Parallel8/16 (ESP32-S3): never queue a zero-length DMA chunk

The copy path splits a transfer into chunks whose first four bytes go
out as LCD command cycles and the rest by DMA. For some lengths (for
example 257 to 260 bytes) a chunk was only four bytes long, so the DMA
descriptor had no payload; Bus_Parallel16 then waited forever for its
TX FIFO to fill. These lengths reach the copy path more often now that
DMA-inaccessible sources are copied.

Bus_Parallel16 now fills each chunk up to the buffer size (one byte less
when a byte is pending from an odd length) and sends a five-byte
remainder as four command bytes plus the pending byte. Bus_Parallel8
enlarges a four-byte chunk so that it carries a payload.

Bus: send DMA-inaccessible sources through the CPU path

pushImageDMA() hands the caller's pointer straight to the bus. On the
ESP32 the SPI DMA cannot read PSRAM or flash, so an image held in PSRAM
was sent as garbage. The SPI bus now sends such sources by CPU, after
the queued DMA has finished. External RAM stays on the DMA path where
the SPI DMA can read it (GDMA targets without flash encryption), with
the existing alignment handling.

The ESP32-S2 / S3 parallel buses copy DMA-inaccessible sources (PSRAM,
flash) into their internal DMA buffer instead of passing them to the
DMA without writing the data cache back.

Backport of #949.

Bus_SPI: wait for queued DMA before the CPU fallback of addDMAQueue()

When flash encryption keeps external RAM out of DMA, addDMAQueue() sends
what is queued and then writes the external RAM source by CPU. The
queued DMA could still be reading a flip buffer that writeBytes() then
reused, so a queue that held two getDMABuffer() buffers could have one
of them overwritten while it was being sent. Wait for the queued
transfer first.

Backport of the corresponding part of #947.

Bus_SPI: build the ESP32-C6 clock takeover with arduino-esp32 3.0 (ESP-IDF 5.1)

The SPI clock takeover (Arduino builds on C5 / C6 / C61 / P4) wraps its
read-modify-write of the clock-source register in PERIPH_RCC_ATOMIC(),
which ESP-IDF added in 5.2. arduino-esp32 3.0.x is built on ESP-IDF 5.1, so
an ESP32-C6 sketch failed to compile ("'PERIPH_RCC_ATOMIC' was not declared
in this scope"). C5 / C61 / P4 need arduino-esp32 3.1 or later and were not
affected.

ESP-IDF 5.1 has no shared lock for that register (its own SPI driver writes
the clock source without one), so where PERIPH_RCC_ATOMIC() is missing the
same block runs inside a critical section of its own.

(cherry picked from commit a1d71b3ae97fca997f4e95524a160d797e149a7a)

Split the v1 implementation into functional translation units

1.2.30 built the whole v1 implementation as one translation unit
(lgfx_v1.cpp included every *.inl file). With the esp-2021r2 toolchain
(GCC 8.4 / binutils 2.35, used by arduino-esp32 2.0.x and the PlatformIO
espressif32 6.x / 7.x platforms) an ESP32-C3 firmware grew from 329 KB
to 904 KB, because unused panel and touch code and its data tables were
no longer removed by --gc-sections.

The older RISC-V assembler appends the CFI relocations of .rela.eh_frame
after the FDE header relocations, so they are not in offset order. When
the linker marks the FDE of a live function, it walks relocations from
that FDE up to its end offset without a lower bound, so the last FDE of
an object also picks up the out-of-order relocations of earlier
functions and keeps them. Within one object this pulled in nearly the
whole library.

Keep the shared header parsing of the single translation unit, but split
the implementation by function: lgfx_v1.cpp (sprite, button, misc),
lgfx_v1_panel.cpp, lgfx_v1_touch.cpp and lgfx_v1_platforms.cpp include
the *.inl files of their group, and LGFXBase.cpp, lgfx_fonts.cpp,
panel/Panel_M5HDMI.cpp (FPGA bitstream) and touch/Touch_GSLx680.cpp
(touch firmware) build on their own. With the same toolchain the
ESP32-C3 firmware is 346 KB again.

The ESP-IDF CMake and make lists, the Pico SDK list and the PC CMake
globs take the new files. The source check accepts several hubs and
standalone sources, and rejects an *.inl reached from two hubs.

chat could neither name nor remember; a script still passing one is told so.

feat(hints): open a hinted link in a split view with `sf`

The new mapping asks the background to create the tab with
`splitWithTabId`, so the link lands beside the page it was hinted in.
Nothing in the page waits on that create, so every outcome -- an
unsupported browser, a `javascript:` URL, a refusal from the browser, a
`createProperties` key it rejects outright -- comes back as a banner in
that page. Whether the mapping exists at all is answered by the
background through the settings, since a content script cannot see
chrome.tabs.

repos.name: iandchasse/silkscreen-pcb

commits.message:
Rev 1.01: R84 USB hot-plug damper, JLC placement corrections, docs

- R84, 1 ohm 0603 (Yageo RC0603FR-071RL; JLC C22936, Basic) in series with
  C2's ground leg. It damps the ringing an already-live USB-A source causes
  at plug-in: the modelled worst case on U2 VIN1 falls from 7.95 V to 5.60 V.
  No DC current flows in it. One GND stitching via below the cut line moved
  to make room (a board trimmed at y 62 still shows 0 unconnected); the CHRG
  track is nudged 0.2 mm.
- FT Rotation Offset (U2, U5, D2, D8) and FT Position Offset (J7, J4, U4)
  fields on the symbols and footprints, so every Toolkit run writes
  positions.csv rows that match JLC's library footprints.
- Bottom silkscreen notes enlarged; R83, R67 and C3 reference texts moved;
  D3's description reads 26.0 Vr.
- production/ regenerated (zip SHA-256 5b819f11..., 166 placed parts, 67
  LCSC codes) and checked: DRC 0 unconnected / 0 parity, Gerbers and drills
  match a fresh kicad-cli export as shape sets, netlist.ipc matches a fresh
  IPC-D-356. jlc_bom.csv, part_fields.csv and other_fabs updated; schematic
  and layout PDFs re-plotted.
- Docs: README, HARDWARE.md (hot-plug in section 3.1), DESIGN_REVIEW.md,
  fabrication README/BOM/NextPCB notes, the 2026-09-30 audit banner and
  BRING_UP section 3.2. New docs/LED_ALT.md: the TPS923610 alternate-driver
  study.
